document.title: 21st Century Visual Arts Content Standards and Objectives for West Virginia Schools

3D311B50DFE80131DE9868A86D17958E.description: discover ways other disciplines are interrelated with the visual arts, e.g., explore architecture through historical and/or mathematical concepts.

3D30D990DFE80131DE9768A86D17958E.description: compare two or more arts disciplines in a cultural context.

3D309710DFE80131DE9668A86D17958E.description:
Students will:
  • identify characteristics of the visual arts and other disciplines; and
  • analyze by comparing and contrasting connections between disciplines.

3D300D80DFE80131DE9468A86D17958E.description: select, describe, and display his/her artwork(s) through oral, written, or technological presentations as part of the critique process.

3D2FA470DFE80131DE9368A86D17958E.description: use a critical process to evaluate two-dimensional and three-dimensional artworks from various eras and cultures; e.g., the model of Description, Analysis, Interpretation, and Aesthetic Judgment

3D2F4D20DFE80131DE9268A86D17958E.description: examine and compare the meaning and purpose between two-dimensional and three-dimensional artworks.

3D2F06A0DFE80131DE9168A86D17958E.description: justify reasons for creating works of art and cite examples, e.g., aesthetic, tradition, preservation, and self-expression.

3D2EC0F0DFE80131DE9068A86D17958E.description:
Students will:
  • identify multiple purposes for creating works of art;
  • analyze contemporary and historic meanings in specific artworks through cultural and aesthetic inquiry; and
  • describe and compare a variety of individual responses to their artworks and to artworks from various eras and cultures

3D2E4300DFE80131DE8E68A86D17958E.description: create two-dimensional or three-dimensional art based on a specific historical period.

3D2E00D0DFE80131DE8D68A86D17958E.description: discuss how time and place influence meaning and value in a work of art.

3D2DBC80DFE80131DE8C68A86D17958E.description: compare and contrast artwork from different cultures in a selected time frame, e.g., oral, written, or technological presentations.

3D2D74E0DFE80131DE8B68A86D17958E.description: analyze the characteristics of artworks and artists from different periods of time, styles, and cultures.

3D2D2E10DFE80131DE8A68A86D17958E.description:
Students will:
  • identify how the visual arts have a history and specific relationship to culture;
  • analyze works of art that reflect different styles and time periods; and
  • demonstrate an understanding of how history, culture, and the arts influence each other.

3D2C91D0DFE80131DE8868A86D17958E.description: analyze how symbols and ideas communicate desired aesthetic results in an artwork.

3D2C4370DFE80131DE8768A86D17958E.description: select symbols and ideas as a subject for artwork.

3D2C00C0DFE80131DE8668A86D17958E.description: integrate symbols and ideas to evoke a specific feeling in an artwork.

3D2BB340DFE80131DE8568A86D17958E.description:
Students will:
  • identify symbols and ideas to communicate meaning in art;
  • determine potential content for artworks; and
  • apply problem-solving skills when creating art relative to subject matter, symbols, and ideas.

3D2B3560DFE80131DE8368A86D17958E.description: use the elements of art and principles of design to effectively communicate ideas.

3D2AF2B0DFE80131DE8268A86D17958E.description: analyze and evaluate application of elements of art and principles of design in two-dimensional and three-dimensional works of art

3D2AAD50DFE80131DE8168A86D17958E.description: create a two or three-dimensional human figure using standard proportions.

3D2A3CA0DFE80131DE8068A86D17958E.description: create two-dimensional design incorporating overlapping and visual direction to show unity.

3D29E060DFE80131DE7F68A86D17958E.description: create artwork using visual rhythm and repetition of patterns, e.g., Escher's use of mathematics.

3D295890DFE80131DE7D68A86D17958E.description: create three-dimensional forms using symmetrical or asymmetrical balance.

3D291AD0DFE80131DE7C68A86D17958E.description: compare and contrast the characteristics of principles of design.

3D28DC00DFE80131DE7B68A86D17958E.description: create an artwork using actual or simulated texture

3D289AA0DFE80131DE7A68A86D17958E.description: produce value scales using various media.

3D284EF0DFE80131DE7968A86D17958E.description: create art using positive and negative space, e.g., architectural forms; printmaking; sculpture; or ceramics.

3D281180DFE80131DE7868A86D17958E.description: create a color intensity chart and a monochromatic color scheme.

3D27D100DFE80131DE7768A86D17958E.description: create a non-objective artwork using geometric and/or biomorphic (organic) shapes or forms.

3D278A80DFE80131DE7668A86D17958E.description: create a drawing using line as the expressive element.

3D273F10DFE80131DE7568A86D17958E.description: compare and contrast the characteristics of elements of art.

3D26FBF0DFE80131DE7468A86D17958E.description:
Students will:
  • identify selected elements and principles of design as they relate to art and the environment;
  • understand qualities of elements of art and principles of design as they apply to two-dimensional and three-dimensional objects and artworks;
  • apply elements of art and principles of design as they relate to problem-solving skills in the creation of art; and
  • communicate expressive ideas that demonstrate an understanding of structures and functions in art.

3D26BA70DFE80131DE7368A86D17958E.description: Elements of Art and Principles of Design

3D266A40DFE80131DE7268A86D17958E.description: demonstrate the safe and effective use of materials, tools, and technology.

3D262730DFE80131DE7168A86D17958E.description: evaluate the effectiveness of their choice of media, techniques, technologies, or processes used in the communication of a personal experience or idea

3D25DFD0DFE80131DE7068A86D17958E.description: experiment and refine use of selected media, techniques, technologies, and processes in the communication of a personal experience or an idea.

3D259DC0DFE80131DE6F68A86D17958E.description: select a media, technique, technology, or process to communicate a personal experience or an idea, e.g., chalk, acrylic, printmaking, painting, digital alteration, animation and sculpture

3D255A20DFE80131DE6E68A86D17958E.description:
Students will:
  • identify media and materials used in creating art;
  • understand processes and techniques in creating art;
  • apply problem-solving skills in creating two-dimensional and three-dimensional works of art; and
  • use materials and tools in a safe and responsible manner.

document.title: Next Generation Content Standards and Objectives for Mathematics in West Virginia Schools

BD7BD6489D4D421980B0F9147022E924.description:
find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation.
  1. understand that, just as with simple events, the probability of a compound event is the fraction of outcomes in the sample space for which the compound event occurs.
  2. represent sample spaces for compound events using methods such as organized lists, tables and tree diagrams. For an event described in everyday language (e.g., "rolling double sixes"), identify the outcomes in the sample space which compose the event.
  3. design and use a simulation to generate frequencies for compound events. For example, use random digits as a simulation tool to approximate the answer to the question: If 40% of donors have type A blood, what is the probability that it will take at least 4 donors to find one with type A blood?

FF42FBD220F14E42A82A6ACB8156B0B6.description:
develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of events. Compare probabilities from a model to observed frequencies; if the agreement is not good, explain possible sources of the discrepancy.
  1. develop a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events. For example, if a student is selected at random from a class, find the probability that Jane will be selected and the probability that a girl will be selected.
  2. develop a probability model (which may not be uniform) by observing frequencies in data generated from a chance process. For example, find the approximate probability that a spinning penny will land heads up or that a tossed paper cup will land open-end down. Do the outcomes for the spinning penny appear to be equally likely based on the observed frequencies?

84E351A795174C8C9DCE25EAD255D2B2.description: approximate the probability of a chance event by collecting data on the chance process that produces it and observing its long-run relative frequency, and predict the approximate relative frequency given the probability.
comments: For example, when rolling a number cube 600 times, predict that a 3 or 6 would be rolled roughly 200 times, but probably not exactly 200 times.

D560CB5E9F764C24B0E037A55C22803D.description: understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1 that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring. Larger numbers indicate greater likelihood. A probability near 0 indicates an unlikely event, a probability around 1/2 indicates an event that is neither unlikely nor likely and a probability near 1 indicates a likely event.

A79BF0BB20664F06A96A87305413E4FF.description: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models.

2E95B0DF44B543509A3C9EDAD131C768.description: use measures of center and measures of variability for numerical data from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.
comments: For example, decide whether the words in a chapter of a seventh-grade science book are generally longer than the words in a chapter of a fourth-grade science book.

A7F74D9D755847EB9A1BA761EF35276A.description: informally assess the degree of visual overlap of two numerical data distributions with similar variabilities, measuring the difference between the centers by expressing it as a multiple of a measure of variability.
comments: For example, the mean height of players on the basketball team is 10 cm greater than the mean height of players on the soccer team, about twice the variability (mean absolute deviation) on either team; on a dot plot, the separation between the two distributions of heights is noticeable.

D6EF0562C6AE49019D3CDCE87AD52FEC.description: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

1427A773100346FEB0B1E36230528402.description: use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest. Generate multiple samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation in estimates or predictions.
comments: For example, estimate the mean word length in a book by randomly sampling words from the book; predict the winner of a school election based on randomly sampled survey data. Gauge how far off the estimate or prediction might be.

68B33ED7422E4D299E63E224A4105F59.description: understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by examining a sample of the population; generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative of that population. Understand that random sampling tends to produce representative samples and support valid inferences.

0A26F9A6EC8F4756B08A81E47919EB65.description: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population.

EF78659B554A4F54BF27AD636D3BCDB5.description:
use variables to represent quantities in a real-world or mathematical problem and construct simple equations and inequalities to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.
  1. solve word problems leading to equations of the form px + q = r and p(x + q) = r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Solve equations of these forms fluently. Compare an algebraic solution to an arithmetic solution, identifying the sequence of the operations used in each approach. For example, the perimeter of a rectangle is 54 cm. Its length is 6 cm. What is its width?
  2. solve word problems leading to inequalities of the form px + q > r or px + q < r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Graph the solution set of the inequality and interpret it in the context of the problem. For example: As a salesperson, you are paid $50 per week plus $3 per sale. This week you want your pay to be at least $100. Write an inequality for the number of sales you need to make, and describe the solutions.

5E1940909F074C2F9A49D31174112B45.description: solve multi-step real-life and mathematical problems posed with positive and negative rational numbers in any form (whole numbers, fractions, and decimals), using tools strategically. Apply properties of operations to calculate with numbers in any form; convert between forms as appropriate; and assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies.
comments: For example: If a woman making $25 an hour gets a 10% raise, she will make an additional 1/10 of her salary an hour, or $2.50, for a new salary of $27.50. If you want to place a towel bar 9 3/4 inches long in the center of a door that is 27 1/2 inches wide, you will need to place the bar about 9 inches from each edge; this estimate can be used as a check on the exact computation.

7C2F503D287A4A35AB7DCF53C2D795B2.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions and equations.

415C2D3DBFE745CB9F25D9D939F53A50.description: understand that rewriting an expression in different forms in a problem context can shed light on the problem and how the quantities in it are related.
comments: For example, a + 0.05a = 1.05a means that "increase by 5%" is the same as "multiply by 1.05."

BA01979AB3D64819B34FFA5F9544CCE4.description: apply properties of operations as strategies to add, subtract, factor and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.

D7BFE1D4E5DE4791A3EEA103FD36A123.description: Use properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

2D7CB4AC07C845F7BBEA06793CD52883.description: solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations with rational numbers. (Computations with rational numbers extend the rules for manipulating fractions to complex fractions.)

F551431071F2406DAE5ABD05F301BC28.description:
apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division and of fractions to multiply and divide rational numbers.
  1. understand that multiplication is extended from fractions to rational numbers by requiring that operations continue to satisfy the properties of operations, particularly the distributive property, leading to products such as (-1)(-1) = 1 and the rules for multiplying signed numbers. Interpret products of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.
  2. understand that integers can be divided, provided that the divisor is not zero, and every quotient of integers (with non-zero divisor) is a rational number. If p and q are integers, then -(p/q) = (-p)/q = p/(-q). Interpret quotients of rational numbers by describing real world contexts.
  3. apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide rational numbers.
  4. convert a rational number to a decimal using long division; know that the decimal form of a rational number terminates in 0s or eventually repeats.

FAA2767C94964B729268B4724D404CE2.description:
apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers; represent addition and subtraction on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram.
  1. describe situations in which opposite quantities combine to make 0. For example, a hydrogen atom has 0 charge because its two constituents are oppositely charged.
  2. understand p + q as the number located a distance |q| from p, in the positive or negative direction depending on whether q is positive or negative. Show that a number and its opposite have a sum of 0 (are additive inverses). Interpret sums of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.
  3. understand subtraction of rational numbers as adding the additive inverse, p - q = p + (-q). Show that the distance between two rational numbers on the number line is the absolute value of their difference and apply this principle in real-world contexts.
  4. apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract rational numbers.

A73D064BAB8E4B079283DA3404780DE0.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with fractions to add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational numbers.

6C9D7232A0EB44D39C6E924D690164BD.description: use proportional relationships to solve multi-step ratio and percent problems.
comments: Examples: simple interest, tax, markups and markdowns, gratuities and commissions, fees, percent increase and decrease, percent error.

03D56B70D30A49EE97A2F7C34A4FC174.description:
recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.
  1. decide whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship, e.g., by testing for equivalent ratios in a table or graphing on a coordinate plane and observing whether the graph is a straight line through the origin.
  2. identify the constant of proportionality (unit rate) in tables, graphs, equations, diagrams and verbal descriptions of proportional relationships.
  3. represent proportional relationships by equations. For example, if total cost t is proportional to the number n of items purchased at a constant price p, the relationship between the total cost and the number of items can be expressed as t = pn.
  4. explain what a point(x, y) on the graph of a proportional relationship means in terms of the situation, with special attention to the points (0,0) and (1,r ) where r is the unit rate.

CC22608274E340CEA77B06CBC84D3C90.description: compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas and other quantities measured in like or different units.
comments: For example, if a person walks 1/2 mile in each 1/4 hour, compute the unit rate as the complex fraction 1/2/1/4 miles per hour, equivalently 2 miles per hour.

D70057F1E4104F1A837F48BC687F351D.description: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

4531DC42CD8B464BA668613A0E5045B0.description: solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, volume and surface area of two- and three-dimensional objects composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, cubes, and right prisms.

3E5469E295074CADA72B37D0E8CBE598.description: use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles in a multi-step problem to write and solve simple equations for an unknown angle in a figure.

4B15A96C33AE4AECA3C1F4AD32F218DE.description: know the formulas for the area and circumference of a circle and use them to solve problems; give an informal derivation of the relationship between the circumference and area of a circle.

F0ED2E1FBC9541519CF39623172FE638.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume.

6490F89C8E0F475284498A62D969DDD6.description: describe the two-dimensional figures that result from slicing three-dimensional figures, as in plane sections of right rectangular prisms and right rectangular pyramids.

3C285379F43743E4874B54C27A704D1D.description: draw (freehand, with ruler and protractor, and with technology) geometric shapes with given conditions. Focus on constructing triangles from three measures of angles or sides, noticing when the conditions determine a unique triangle, more than one triangle, or no triangle.

3934524B49334211908FAD12C9A37E11.description: solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures, including computing actual lengths and areas from a scale drawing and reproducing a scale drawing at a different scale.

C1B332E5E9AC461498EC8BD4A4F93F87.description: Draw, construct and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them.

376EC3C0055C4F04AA932978491399EF.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

470E66C2689E43BFBFED3E868D80D620.description: Look for and make use of structure.

5E5DBF75D67940DAB0E1F3B91AD602A0.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

665A1C17AA3E4592A007E9A1765D9E7F.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: 21st Century Science 9-12 Content Standards and Objectives for West Virginia Schools

ADF90AE9269C4262A68B2E1BC2482439.description: differentiate between stable and unstable nuclei, and if the nucleus is unstable predict the type(s) of nuclear decay.

4A5D5F41B40F41948F628D38CCCA6474.description: calculate an atom's binding energy as related to Einstein's special theory of relativity, and interpret the nuclear forces present.

C1A6D3DA9647432AAB05BA2B928B5F99.description:
examine evidence for the historical development of the quantum mechanical theory:
  • Planck's blackbody radiation
  • Einstein's photoelectric effect
  • deBroglie's duality.

15461A8D98D14C0C9DF039E6868917B2.description:
critique the role of technology in the development of historical models of the atom:
  • radioactivity
  • atomic spectra
  • particle accelerators, etc.

E1BB784B7DEA41B4996FDA72C4CEB3DA.description: evaluate the application of wave properties to the development of optical and acoustical devices.

78B97013DA7D4D698222FACE21F2C7B9.description:
examine wave properties and their interactions:
  • reflection
  • refraction
  • dispersion
  • total internal deflection
  • interference
  • diffraction
  • Doppler Shift
  • beats
  • polarization.

0575EBE7C645421A88488B8A45BF23A4.description:
apply knowledge of simple harmonic motion - to calculate the kinetic and potential energies of the oscillating system:
  • springs
  • pendulums
  • other oscillating objects.

9C31F1553DE941309EE689D99C5F5CF6.description: investigate, analyze, and evaluate the concepts of solid-state physics and the application of semiconductors and superconductors in the advancement of electronics through the development of diodes, transistors, and integrated circuits.

B1D275ADB277483C83BBB07F6F82F913.description: critique electromagnetic induction and evaluate its application to electric circuits and various devices.

C102BDD8D33D43B48BA697430EDCB52C.description: predict and interpret magnetic forces and magnetic fields, and apply their effect on the motion of a point charge and to the electric current in a wire or coil.

07217084BBD444D9BAC73F316CBE3929.description: construct, diagram and evaluate complex electrical circuits.

72BD3C34C2A44D5B84423DDB5FDE5B76.description:
deduce the relative values of electric force and field strength based on the magnitude of and the distance from the point charge:
  • Coulomb's Law
  • inverse square law.

8EC0D25838E44DAABE36FE234EA1EFEE.description:
interpret and apply concepts of thermal physics:
  • distinction of heat and temperature
  • thermal expansion
  • properties of Ideal Gases
  • Kinetic Theory
  • specific heat
  • energy transfer.

889729BAC41C43D0919CC5CEF352D602.description: predict and verify the effect of variables on the properties and dynamics of fluids.

583E229853F945E3BC9433C02C3231BF.description:
using knowledge of linear motion equations, synthesize concepts of rotational motion:
  • angular speed and acceleration
  • centripetal acceleration
  • Newtonian gravitation
  • Kepler's Laws
  • torque.

DCE993D6FC564D9C97C7F13DCAD5BED1.description:
experimentally verify laws of motion including:
  • Newton's Laws
  • Conservation of Momentum (linear and angular)
  • Conservation of Energy.

C84EE4064E9F4CA7891BE07071B9A2C0.description: use data to deduce mathematical relationships involving one and two dimensional motion.

27F304E1EF2D44C7B4D06AE05BF50F2D.description:
apply graphical analysis to interpret motion in terms of:
  • position
  • velocity
  • acceleration
  • time.

E74E08DF06094701AEA720283B197BF4.description:
Students will
  • demonstrate knowledge, understanding, and applications of scientific facts, concepts, principles, theories, and models as delineated in the objectives.
  • demonstrate an understanding of the interrelationships among physics, chemistry, biology, and the earth and space sciences.
  • apply knowledge, understanding, and skills of science subject matter/concepts to daily life experiences.

5EAF358D047545D498E7C8B69C7459FD.description: synthesize concepts across various science disciplines to better understand the natural world (e.g., form and function, systems, or change over time).

2065565104094D58A2FA5D24665A15D2.description: relate societal, cultural and economic issues to key scientific innovations.

96BADAA4DBEA47C294B484209907E167.description: given current science-technology-societal issues, construct and defend potential solutions.

7D2B1F5B99BC4FF18C5D6A7DC4CD4C47.description: investigate, compare and design scientific and technological solutions to address personal and societal problems.

27D6936C9EAA4B8EA633CE8A483846B7.description: draw conclusions from a variety of data sources to analyze and interpret systems and models (e.g., use graphs and equations to measure and apply variables such as rate and scale, evaluate changes in trends and cycles, or predict the influence of external variances such as potential sources of error, or interpret maps).

2CFEAD205A134E26A13C1A26B3642BC1.description: design, conduct, evaluate and revise experiments (e.g., compose a question to be investigated, design a controlled investigation that produces numeric data, evaluate the data in the context of scientific laws and principles, construct a conclusion based on findings, propose revisions to investigations based on manipulation of variables and/or analysis of error, or communicate and defend the results and conclusions).

8D3E8D36016D405E9B7E548ABC673416.description: conduct and/or design investigations that incorporate the skills and attitudes and/or values of scientific inquiry (e.g., established research protocol, accurate record keeping, replication of results and peer review, objectivity, openness, skepticism, fairness, or creativity and logic).

47936250DBF04AA4A35ABFCC4A6F05F8.description: formulate scientific explanations based on historical observations and experimental evidence, accounting for variability in experimental results.

18E87587A626454AACCCA6F75521344E.description: implement safe procedures and practices when manipulating equipment, materials, organisms, and models.

09D99BDDA7864B24A163033EB394AF85.description:
Students will
  • demonstrate an understanding of history and nature of science as a human endeavor encompassing the contributions of diverse cultures and scientists.
  • demonstrate the ability to use the inquiry process to solve problems.
  • relate science-technology-societal issues while using a variety of sources to construct and defend their solutions.

DC5750FB3ED549EB805634156CD09E7C.description: distinguish between direct current and alternating current circuits and describe how AC is converted to DC.

387A7B839AA2409B86E4DAA3F9188DB9.description: analyze simple direct current circuits using Ohm's Law.

DC3275646FD949308655619E6209BE6E.description: illustrate the applications of colored lights and pigments.

03367031A95543E5BD5FE1EB3B56F247.description:
diagram image location:
  • plane and spherical mirrors
  • concave and convex lenses.

8823EEA9FFC044FFA811404D2B8E9B0D.description: compare the Doppler shift effect for sound and light and point out examples of its occurrences and applications.

F571EE98564B43CCA8D5C2E99D6F6356.description: model the production of a standing wave and propose a practical application of such a wave.

AA67633D522548B79AB8795747D8A74B.description: solve problems involving wave speed, frequency and wavelength; determine factors that affect the speed of sound; recognize that the speed of light is a constant.

5ACED2F304074AA78040C712E725E5A2.description: compare and contrast sound and light waves using the concepts of reflection, refraction, and interference.

5BE31F8941B94D86A6BFBBDA0B6AA397.description: relate the first law of thermodynamics to energy conservation.

091B20B176204686BE099045898EB041.description: apply the mechanism of heat transfer and relate to environmental and energy conservation issues.

09DAAF7F1F49412F902C5FBD28189B11.description: compare and contrast the common temperature scales, convert from one temperature scale to another and evaluate temperature in terms of kinetic energy.

391AFE29546F46E0914BCB579BA3F469.description: recognize the effects of Bernoulli's principle on fluid motion.

C21C257B09E0489BA161EC310647F6CA.description: analyze Archimedes' and Pascal's principles to solve problems involving equilibrium and stability of floating systems.

66E9439ABF234729901D15F60C6F49C6.description: deduce work, energy, power and efficiency in mechanical systems.

613537F0C3654E4287496C6655AA2CA7.description: compare and contrast kinetic and potential energies and recognize situations where mechanical energy is conserved.

9F475199EDEE4E49ADA5987FB8E2A151.description: interpret Newton's Laws in terms of natural phenomena.

9A9A200EC955407A984DDA1A1231E155.description: illustrate forces acting on objects with free body diagrams.

60FACCC420C54C4E88BD00B8E87468CA.description: analyze the motion of a projectile.

CA40F68DA81F48E48EED525B2BED22B5.description: compare and contrast distance, velocity and acceleration of moving objects to describe accelerated and non-accelerated motions of a particle from textbook or lab collected data.

9C47953F548C4A8C88F94F91AE66752B.description: solve right triangle vector problems both graphically and algebraically.

37FD643637AE4B96A3885F4ADA12645F.description:

2FD303C59D5C4BFC862D517DF1D311BE.description: Demonstrate an understanding of Middle Age societies and the influence of those societies on the history of the world in areas of social, political and economic change.

2AA9DB812B054D398EB7D671C4508349.description: examine and explain the impact and lasting effects of classical philosophy (e.g., Socrates, Plato, Aristotle, Confucianism, Daoism and Legalism) including effects at the point of origin as well as effects on the world throughout history.

9D64B36AF6034C5EAE1EA1A1AB142F9F.description: analyze the impact of the religion on classical civilizations, including rise and growth of Christianity, Hinduism and the effects of its beliefs and practices on daily life, changes that occurred as a result of Buddhist teachings, and the influence of a variety of religions (e.g., Judaism and Zoroastrianism) on culture and politics.

D21BEC4F54E444A19C2ADC9DA8F5FD3F.description: compare and contrast the causes and effects of the rise and decline of classical civilizations.

B1C2869D4B904A66B93EE6652DAF9142.description: Demonstrate an understanding of classical civilizations and the influence of those civilizations across time and space.

100C8D3552874D16B349A047D77D8A2F.description: investigate and detail the various components of culture and civilization including customs, norms, values, traditions, political systems, economic systems, religious beliefs and philosophies in ancient river civilizations.

C6DAC992B5BE4B6280EF64D5E9200CB8.description: compare and contrast the causes and effects of the rise and decline of ancient river valley civilizations.

9E39D21A0AC2445EB421CDDE2275957B.description: Demonstrate an understanding of ancient river civilizations and the ways in which early civilizations evolve.

8027E35F74DB4EB6972314EB53B4C132.description: detail and predict the causes and effects of the Agricultural Revolution.

FA15B53D0C17435F915E23CF87AF39AE.description: analyze the interaction of early humans with their environment and evaluate their decisions (e.g., hunting, migration, shelter, food and clothing.)

7299667E37514F33B1F9FB466A05B3A5.description: Demonstrate an understanding of prehistory, the concept of change over time and the emergence of civilization.

comments: History organizes events and phenomena in terms of when they occurred and examines where, how and why they took place. Students study how individuals and societies have changed and interacted over time. They organize events through chronologies and evaluate cause-and-effect relationships among them. Students analyze how individuals, groups and nations have shaped cultural heritages. They gather historical data, examine, analyze and interpret this data, and present their results in a clear, critical manner. Students study origins and evolutions of culture hearths, settlements, civilizations, states, nations, nation-states, governments and economic developments. Through history, students understand the identity and origins of their families, communities, state and nation. Through history, students recognize the influence of world events on the development of the United States and they evaluate the influence of the United States on the world. Understanding the past helps students prepare for today and the events of the future.

83A3A41F9C514ED18A5A162ABB5659B4.description: write routinely over extended time frames (time for reflection and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

2E60B75467D540259DFC187648D5EE9F.description: draw evidence from informational texts to support analysis, reflection and research.

1A81BEC848BF4FEABF3D5C2C2428ABC6.description: conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem and narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

3DA9CD10B65345C28B6E4731AFD6C74F.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

F975F649BE124978A77B89BA7FE1D8D7.description: use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish and update individual or shared writing products, taking advantage of technology's capacity to link to other information and to display information flexibly and dynamically.

63A2467F4297442C86AE6A79317CDDE4.description: develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.

1ACEF1D7D63048448450759A16FEB235.description: produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization and style are appropriate to task, purpose and audience.

33874A59C8574EB2912084670C75630A.description:
write informative/explanatory texts, including the narration of historical events, scientific procedures/experiments, or technical processes.
  • introduce a topic and organize ideas, concepts, and information to make important connections and distinctions; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g. figures, tables) and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.
  • develop the topic with well-chosen, relevant and sufficient facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.
  • use varied transitions and sentence structures to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.
  • use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to manage the complexity of the topic and convey a style appropriate to the discipline and context as well as to the expertise of likely readers.
  • establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.
  • provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

48161A669B324496878B5D89E5613DE1.description:
write arguments focused on discipline-specific content.
  • introduce precise claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims and create an organization that establishes clear relationships among the claim(s), counterclaims, reasons and evidence.
  • develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly, supplying data and evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both claim(s) and counterclaims in a discipline-appropriate form and in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level and concerns.
  • use words, phrases and clauses to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence and between claim(s) and counterclaims.
  • establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.
  • provide a concluding statement or section that follows from or supports the argument presented.

1D033D279DDA4544B45261EC845204D4.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

comments: The Literacy Standards for History/Social Studies lay out a vision of what it means to be literate in social studies. The skills and understanding students are expected to demonstrate in both reading and writing have a wide applicability outside the classroom or workplace. Reading requires an appreciation of the norms and conventions of social studies, such as the kinds of evidence used in history; an understanding of domain-specific words and phrases; an attention to precise details; and the capacity to evaluate intricate arguments, synthesize complex information, and follow detailed descriptions of events and concepts in social studies. In writing students must take task, purpose, and audience into careful consideration, choosing words, information, structures, and formats deliberately. They have to become adept at gathering information, evaluating sources, and citing material accurately, reporting finding from their research and analysis of sources in a clear and cogent manner. Students who meet these standards demonstrate the reasoning and use of evidence that is essential to both private and responsible citizenship in a democratic society.

652B997F474440F0B2CEF8700449EAF3.description: use latitude, longitude, Prime Meridian and the Equator to describe locations.

9DCAA16C55F94DBB94802B2AF3B71A5D.description: use maps, charts and graphs to analyze the world to account for consequences of human/environment interaction, and to depict the geographic implications of world events.

40B7EA8CAFEB49DC80C70B11188726C6.description: explain how the uneven distribution of resources in the world can lead to conflict, competition or cooperation among nations, regions, and cultural groups.

6217690C238049C7B97205339B511286.description: explain how migration of people and movement of goods and ideas can enrich cultures, but also create tensions.

B9352325AEB24476A528EC04BFB18C21.description: explain how altering the environment has brought prosperity to some places and created environmental dilemmas for others.

comments: Geography encompasses physical and human systems and the interactions between them on local and global scales. People interact with the natural world in culturally distinct ways to produce unique places, which change over time. New technologies and perspectives of geography provide students with an understanding of the world, and the ability to evaluate information in spatial terms. The geography standard stresses the world in which we live and the role of the U.S. in the global community. Students use geographic perspectives and technology to interpret culture, environment and the connection between them. Students collaborate with one another and work individually using geographic skills and tools to ask geographic questions based on the five themes of geography (location, place, human-environmental interaction, movement and regions). They acquire the necessary information, organize and analyze the information and respond to those geographic questions. Students examine the varying ways in which people interact with their environments and appreciate the diversity and similarities of cultures and places created by those interactions.

CEAFC53C0214414D808951FB796DF364.description: examine the costs of government policies in relation to the rise and fall of civilizations (e.g., Roman Empire, the Crusades and Imperialism).

1A075E72B5DE4616B5EB7CA8CBED2B5F.description: identify types of exchange systems (e.g., barter, money) and the role forms of currency play in acquiring goods and services.

2A7902D00AE64139B3CE15BA5F34AA7A.description: analyze the importance of family, labor specialization and regional commerce in the development of global trade systems.

81B97492A51745949E649A201FEB4514.description: examine and illustrate the trade patterns (e.g., resource allocation, mercantilism and other economic systems) of regions of the world across time and explain their significance to the evolution of global economics.

745BDF0FB0C24412B0B03FEA734565AB.description: define scarcity and demonstrate the role of opportunity costs in decision making.

comments: Economics analyzes the production, allocation, distribution and use of resources. The economic principles include an understanding of scarcity and choice, productivity, markets and prices, supply and demand, competition, role of government, international trade factors and consumer decisions in a global economy. Understanding economic principles, whole economies and the interactions between different types of economies helps students comprehend the exchange of information, capital and products across the globe. Learners investigate economic principles and their application to historical situations. Learners will work cooperatively and individually to analyze how basic economic principles affect their daily lives. Students become financially responsible by examining the consequences of and practicing personal financial decision-making.

B3FB3DB047C945F2B1944820F1742CFF.description: explain how individuals and organizations use nonviolent protests, boycotts, riots and other measures as tools in the struggle for civil rights and freedom.

F5767CAE4EE34058ADA2784183EDC121.description: compare and contrast political ideologies in order to analyze the evolving role of government in world affairs prior to the year 1900 (e.g., democracies, republics, dictatorships, various types of monarchies, oligarchies, theocracies and parliamentary systems).

33585A76B7F74A15974C05E6BB061D70.description: examine conflicts and resolutions between groups throughout history and use past outcomes to hypothesize the outcomes of modern conflicts.

383548BCC33643249DE649E4A2DC130D.description: analyze and evaluate various ways of organizing systems of government in order to illustrate the continuity and change in the role of government over time (e.g., Hammurabi's Code, the Twelve Tables of Rome, Justinian Code, Magna Carta, English Bill of Rights, Articles of Confederation and the United States Constitution).

EBF9AB44252D4B8A9C824435B5966DB1.description: analyze and connect the status, roles and responsibilities of free men, women, children, slaves and foreigners across time in various civilizations.

934917F10C5E44D59249A8412C83020F.description: analyze and connect the status, roles and responsibilities of free men, women, children, slaves and foreigners across time in various civilizations.

D261965B4FE64243AA0294798D36CF81.description: describe the roles of citizens and their responsibilities (e.g., prehistoric societies, river civilizations, classical civilizations, feudal systems, developing nation states and neo-feudal systems).

comments: Civics addresses both citizenship and political systems. Citizenship education prepares students to be informed, active and effective citizens who accept their responsibilities, understand their privileges and rights and participate actively in society and government. To be successful participants in society, students must understand how to build social capital (a network of social relationships) that encourages reciprocity and trust, two characteristics of civic virtue and good citizenship. Students must be able to research issues, form reasoned opinions, support their positions and engage in the political process. Students exercise tolerance and empathy, respect the rights of others, and share a concern for the common good while acting responsibly with the interests of the larger community in mind. Students must learn and practice intellectual and participatory skills essential for an involved citizenry. To develop these skills, the curriculum must extend beyond the school to include experiences in the workplace and service in the community. While studying political systems, students develop global awareness and study the foundations of various world governments and the strategies they employ to achieve their goals. With respect to the United States, students learn the underlying principles of representative democracy, the constitutional separation of powers and the rule of law. The students learn the origins and meaning of the principles, ideals and core democratic values expressed in the foundational documents of the United States. Students recognize the need for authority, government and the rights and responsibilities of citizens.

3C7B79F0DFE80131DD7268A86D17958E.description: use geometric forms in a three-dimensional artwork, e.g., architecture.

3C7B35D0DFE80131DD7168A86D17958E.description: use color to communicate different ideas, e.g., calm; stormy; warm; cool.

3C7AEA80DFE80131DD7068A86D17958E.description: compare sizes of objects and use in their artwork.

3C7A1F10DFE80131DD6E68A86D17958E.description: compare shape versus form, e.g., circle/sphere; square/cube; triangle/pyramid.

3C79DC10DFE80131DD6D68A86D17958E.description: use shapes and overlapping shapes in their own artworks.

3C799A90DFE80131DD6C68A86D17958E.description: create art using line quality with a variety of materials and tools.

3C791860DFE80131DD6A68A86D17958E.description: experiment with primary, secondary, neutral, warm, and cool color.

3C78D1C0DFE80131DD6968A86D17958E.description:
Students will:
  • identify selected elements and principles of design as they relate to art and the environment;
  • understand qualities of elements of art and principles of design as they apply to two-dimensional and three-dimensional objects and artworks;
  • apply elements of art and principles of design as they relate to problem-solving skills in the creation of art; and
  • communicate expressive ideas that demonstrate an understanding of structures and functions in art.

3C7886D0DFE80131DD6868A86D17958E.description: Elements of Art and Principles of Design

3C7846E0DFE80131DD6768A86D17958E.description: use materials, tools and technologies in a safe and responsible manner.

3C780940DFE80131DD6668A86D17958E.description: construct three-dimensional objects using a variety media to communicate ideas, experiences, and stories.

3C77CB80DFE80131DD6568A86D17958E.description: produce two-dimensional art using a variety media to communicate ideas, experiences, and stories.

3C778D00DFE80131DD6468A86D17958E.description: describe the differences in kinds of paper.

3C774BF0DFE80131DD6368A86D17958E.description: compare how the different techniques and processes of sculpture cause different appearances and responses, e.g., additive, subtractive, assemblage.

3C770780DFE80131DD6268A86D17958E.description: Identify the media, tools, techniques, and processes used in sculpting, e.g., clay; paper.

3C76B410DFE80131DD6168A86D17958E.description: discover how the different techniques and processes of painting cause different effects and responses, e.g., wet on wet and dry brush.

3C764770DFE80131DD6068A86D17958E.description: identify the media, tools, techniques and processes used in painting, e.g., tempera, and its character on paper.

3C760290DFE80131DD5F68A86D17958E.description:
Students will:
  • identify media and materials used in creating art;
  • understand processes and techniques in creating art;
  • apply problem-solving skills in creating two-dimensional and three-dimensional works of art; and
  • use materials and tools in a safe and responsible manner.

document.title: 21st Century Physical Education 5-12 Content Standards and Objectives for West Virginia Schools

5848FC5286194B22961A334A55940680.description: practice behaviors that are supportive and inclusive in physical activity.

66788DB57FF84AC9BAD20103E4398EFD.description: make appropriate decisions when applying rules, procedures, etiquette, and safety.

B63091CF16BB464EB3ED6CA12409CF88.description: work cooperatively and productively in a group to accomplish a set goal/task.

1D93BC0A2CF14B959B1222082C0997CB.description: Students will Identify and apply responsible, personal and social behaviors in physical activity settings.

comments: The intent of this standard is achievement of self- initiated behaviors that promote personal and group success in activity settings. These include safe practices, adherence to rules and procedures, etiquette, cooperation and teamwork, ethical behavior in sport, and positive social interaction. Key to this standard is developing respect for individual similarities and differences through positive interaction among participants in physical activity. Similarities and differences include characteristics of culture, ethnicity, motor performance, disabilities, physical characteristics.

570C9AC2D46749FEB9FB27B95D9888D4.description: practice the F.I.T.T. principle to achieve physical fitness

5171F21FA5364CC1ADAED3B08A69C760.description: describe the necessity of warm-up and cool-down activities.

F4EADFC4929E4A419BF8588D7580CF3C.description: examine the fitness benefits of a variety of physical activities (e.g., stretching, walking).

D726230FB0C74F289F242433A1A2BF08.description: define the five components of FITNESSGRAM.

4EB55292E0ED4F56BD20930CCC97091B.description: perform at the gender and age-appropriate health-related fitness standards as defined in FITNESSGRAM.

746EDEB61A944352AA149E7A028EB7B7.description: Students will apply physical fitness concepts to achieve and maintain a health-enhancing level of physical fitness.

comments: The intent of this standard is for students to have both the ability and willingness to accept responsibility for personal fitness leading to an active, health lifestyle. Students develop higher levels of basic fitness and physical competence as needed for many work situations and active leisure participation. Health-related fitness components include cardiorespiratory endurance, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, and body composition.

DC8C532E3AEC49C28C7E11DBA6DB8C10.description: identify lifestyle behaviors to increase physical activity (e.g., taking stairs, walk/ride bike to school).

F3E0D7A5EB3340E5AE7EC1C332FDEA14.description: participate in games, sports, dance and outdoor pursuits both in and outside school to improve performance and fitness (e.g., DDR).

6A981654535F41AFB1C5FFBECEAA5E06.description: participate in physical activity in addition to physical education class (e.g., maintain an activity log, activity gram).

655A6FDA91AB411C959A7BC13F8675B1.description: Students will exhibit a physically active lifestyle that provides the opportunity for enjoyment, challenge, self-expression, and social interaction.

comments: The intent of this standard is to develop an awareness of the intrinsic values and benefits of participation in physical activity that provides personal meaning. Physical activity provides opportunities for self-expression and social interaction and can be enjoyable, challenging, and fun. These benefits develop self-confidence and promote positive self image, thereby enticing people to continue participation in activity throughout the life span.

DAC4BDA4AEB1405A9A2DB0A50DDFF58F.description: perform basic body mechanics necessary to develop new motor skills (e.g., opposite hand-opposite foot, head-up, follow-through).

304DA6B3D5574EF383D24839D2B36B2F.description: identify proper techniques necessary to perform a variety of movement forms (e.g., catching, running, throwing, striking, kicking).

DE687C9534CF4FBCB8754A7481E3954E.description: Students will apply concepts and principles of human movement to the development of motor skills and learning of new skills.

comments: The intent of this standard is for students to establish patterns of regular participation in meaningful physical activity. This standard connects what is done in the physical education class with the lives of students outside of the classroom. While participation within the physical education class is important, what the student does outside the physical education class is critical to developing an active, healthy lifestyle that could help prevent a variety of health problems among future generations of adults. Students make use of the skills and knowledge learned in physical education class as they engage in regular physical activity outside of the physical education class.

6B732DD94C3C4A97BD99A1BCA6DE653F.description: perform lead-up activities that encompass elements of individual, dual, team, and lifetime activities.

EEFE2D8614E9486E98127F86A6F8BE44.description: perform basic skills necessary to participate in individual, dual, team, and lifetime activities.

D7146B4EC2384F0899EAB33FA16E0D8F.description: perform independently in physical activity and/or exercise to improve skill/fitness.

2AEB37DF6C244E30BB1570619853F456.description: Students will demonstrate movement patterns and motor skills needed to perform a variety of physical activities.

comments: The intent of this standard is development of the movement/physical skills needed to enjoy participation in physical activities. Mastering movement fundamentals establishes a foundation to facilitate continued motor skill acquisition and gives students the capacity for successful and advanced levels of performance to further the likelihood of participation on a daily basis.

document.title: Next Generation Health Education 5-12 Content Standards and Objectives for West Virginia Schools

C828250227334844B124598A662F59A0.description: explain why making positive health choices will influence others.

BE85C7E8D9FF47B69E53E18CBAB67E0F.description: advocate to their family to work cooperatively for healthy lifestyles (e.g., exercise together, diet plans, food preparation, spend time together).

D0266AD3812744C58EBC29EE6A117D9B.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to advocate for personal, family, and community health.

comments: Advocacy skills help students promote healthy norms and healthy behaviors. This standard helps students develop important skills to target their health enhancing messages and to encourage others to adopt healthy behaviors.

DD8012C80C3D4FDB808040E5113B7977.description: identify good health practices to improve personal and family health (e.g., hygiene, nutrition, food preparation).

C8B52246B73D45F7BA51A753C8F4C3F5.description: identify strategies to reduce stress, anxiety and depression.

E9B2F1ACE6A84391ADFE56C9F7C2491E.description: dramatize protective behaviors used to avoid and reduce threatening situations (e.g., anger, bullying, harassment).

5F074E10178C48C395CBAF85F138E649.description: analyze the differences between safe and risky behaviors, including methods for preventing pregnancy and STDs, including HIV/AIDS and HBV (e.g., abstinence , birth control, disease control).

F5B452ADAC8B4970BBD556DDE855CBE8.description: recognize risky or harmful behaviors that may occur in relationships (e.g., abuse, date rape, sexual activity).

7672A1AB58BB4987AF713131D1DBB554.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to advocate for personal, family, and community health.

comments: Research confirms that practicing health enhancing behaviors can contribute to a positive quality of life. In addition, many diseases and injuries can be prevented by reducing harmful and risk taking behaviors. This standard promotes accepting personal responsibility for health and encourages the practice of healthy behaviors.

8592A41DC77547A1BCDCB69F8187C0E5.description: discuss how time may change personal health goals. (e.g., change of schools, getting older, new interests, family alteration).

3D0A00BE4D7441D191D7594302B1388F.description: create and develop a personal health goal.

C90DE81DD9D64283A2AEEFFC0ED2F06B.description: explain how the goal setting process is important when planning future events (e.g., college, marriage, job).

033AF09A72D54F1CA52297FE97043101.description: develop a personal health plan to address strengths, weaknesses and health risks.(e.g., diet, exercise, sleep, relationships).

4E8781438CE345AD9E3BD3ACA15977BB.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to use goal-setting skills to enhance health.

comments: Goal-setting skills are essential to help students identify, adopt and maintain healthy behaviors. This standard includes the critical steps needed to achieve both short-term and long-term health goals. These skills make it possible for individuals to have aspirations and plans for the future.

B3B69418D3134068A6B839C7EC22EFF4.description: differentiate between healthy and unhealthy alternatives when making decisions.

5E69EE5E428A455FA31B2D318018FB5D.description: apply the steps of a decision-making process to solve a problem.

6A0D882FA2AA45709483F6248CD5B160.description: illustrate situations and practice skills requiring decisions with alcohol, tobacco and other drugs.

AED4A3B300424A3FB4F7D7172FAA3C80.description: discuss the consequences of poor nutritional choices (e.g., eating disorders) for self and others (e.g., families, babies).

50D5E282BBD4499995DFBDD85DF41598.description: apply the USDA Dietary Guidelines in meal planning.

50B168F6EB8F4C029C36BB1126EC6296.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to use decision-making skills to enhance health.

comments: Decision-making skills are needed in order to identify, implement and sustain health enhancing behaviors. This standard includes the essential steps needed to make healthy decisions as prescribed in the performance indicators. When applied to health issues, the decision-making process enables individuals to collaborate with others to improve quality of life.

46EE446500874397AA34794CF0459AC5.description: list communication skills to build and maintain healthy relationships (e.g., listening, body language, patience).

50DB241B6D7D49789A6D83D1824A15B9.description: demonstrate the value of assertive strategies when asking for help in an emergency (e.g. 911, 211, police, fire, teacher).

7822D7A16EB7489392DA5F27171FFC3C.description: list steps that can be taken to improve dysfunctional family relationships (e.g., Alanon, counselor, trusted adults, try to get along).

CE15C89006094163951A2ECC803C69BA.description: discuss ways one can develop healthful family relationships (e.g., share with siblings, chores, spend time together).

0C9A36A3B29944CF90A7815205214C8E.description: give examples of refusal and negotiation skills to avoid health risks (e.g., say no, avoid risks, give excuses).

65C5782CD5FA4D998DDFD114D8637FCC.description: analyze the effectiveness of a variety of positive coping mechanisms/conflict resolution skills (e.g., peer mediation, non-violent strategies to deal with upset feelings and difficult situations).

29A85493A0FD4E8AAC9A17B292E5B6E1.description: explain how character and personality affect the perception of one's ability to communicate (e.g., confident = aggressive; shy = passive).

D7BF6155CC9B4F77B868D6C7BF562113.description: analyze effective verbal and non-verbal communication skills to enhance health (e.g., body language, restating, individual/group conversation).

FBDCE846AABC4A6EB7D204A757F861ED.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to use interpersonal communication skills to enhance health and avoid or reduce health risk.

comments: Effective communication enhances personal, family, and community health. This standard focuses on how responsible individuals use verbal and non-verbal skills to develop and maintain healthy personal relationships. The ability to organize and to convey information and feelings is the basis for strengthening interpersonal interactions and reducing or avoiding conflict.

7DB01168919E4021BF38EB1BCD17FA2F.description: identify myths, misinformation and stereotyping associated with health services (e.g., quackery, false advertising).

6A6E8D0D23C94F38B78D5243D4EEDC01.description: utilize personal and hereditary data to determine medical care needs (e.g., health screenings, nutritional guidelines).

C4144AC9FC8F4ECDA50DC2795FDC7D07.description: list situations that require professional and community health services (e.g., accidents, illnesses, health maintenance).

EFE2370E3D70461EA6A55C65060E742E.description: appraise the accessibility of products that enhance health (e.g., age requirements, internet, community access).

75C5381626974689AB5C9B46B02A4A79.description: recognize valid health information found in the home, school, community and the internet (e.g. literature, hospital brochures, websites).

29CAA9C9D3C04B679B93E0B5C187BAF8.description: evaluate the costs of health information, products and services (e.g., compare/contrast products, internet purchases).

9893D5D809F34B86B8A2B46355CC5BAC.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to access valid information and products and services to enhance health.

comments: Accessing valid health information and health-promoting products and services is critical in the prevention, early detection, and treatment of health problems. This standard focuses on how to identify and access valid health resources and to reject unproven sources. Applying the skills of analysis, comparison and evaluation of health resources empowers students to achieve health literacy.

ADE362BC73FC460FBE73A16E6F2B60FB.description: examine the influence of the family on the health of adolescents (e.g., smoking, drinking, drug use, meal plans).

A9433E2403EC49F581EB3D1AACE8D74A.description: evaluate how peers, schools, and communities can impact personal health practices and behaviors (e.g., PTA, scouting and other youth organizations).

D3E06A070B4C4EF0A4789AEF6604F0F1.description: analyze the influence that advertisers have on consumer choices (e.g., tobacco and alcohol use, clothing styles, makeup).

44A13FE8C1764A69A695E0DBDA6C5D85.description: analyze media messages about alcohol, tobacco, and other drugs (e.g., alcoholic beverage commercials, prescription and OTC drugs).

D7BA0B09B0A84B019BE43B8BB9B2C0EA.description: recognize the importance of respecting individual differences (e.g., race, religion, size, age, sex).

BE455689F9A14CB1B485B24369DB6974.description: describe the impact of bullying (e.g., physical, verbal, cyber) and identify necessary coping skills.

40469E997F5642648B531A64F1E17799.description: debate how messages from the media can influence health behaviors (e.g., advertising techniques).

FEE39861ACF14720AC6EDDFBA22BE492.description: compare and contrast the influence of cultural beliefs on health behaviors (e.g., nutrition, hygiene, medical treatment, alcohol, tobacco, and other drugs.

788DF6649FB64EFFA87CEC4CF5E3EFDF.description: Students will analyze the influence of family, peers, culture, media, technology and other factors on health behaviors.

comments: Health is impacted by a variety of positive and negative influences within society. This standard focuses on identifying and understanding the diverse internal and external factors that influence health practices and behaviors among youth including personal values, beliefs and perceived norms.

0FB3626660BE4C2FA6E2CC18589CAED9.description: describe ways to maintain and improve the components of health (emotional, physical, social, intellectual, spiritual, environmental (e.g., total wellness, positive thinking).

51A707D11AC44C70B50EAE46A28CDE1B.description: demonstrate first aid procedures (e.g., CPR, control bleeding, airway obstructions, fractures).

8982AC6CF9C94F74BA30D6A21634A765.description: identify general symptoms and potentially long-term health consequences of STDs (e.g., opportunistic infections, infertility, death)

27F5819406C2471183AD7FA187D4536F.description: describe the anatomy and functions of the reproductive system.

FE2699EF026C407DB5B5F2B4C1BFA7DA.description: analyze the effects of risky behaviors on body systems and general wellness (e.g., substance abuse, smoking).

A7C0EA8A70F44271A51261E5EB5BC6B2.description: list the six essential nutrients; determine their sources and functions.

E63CBDCCD581405A8B3980980D6215FC.description: Students will comprehend concepts related to health promotion and disease prevention to enhance health.

comments: The acquisition of basic health concepts and functional health knowledge provides a foundation for promoting health-enhancing behaviors among youth. This standard includes essential concepts that are based on established health behavior theories and models. Concepts that focus on both health promotion and risk reduction are included in the performance indicators.

document.title: Next Generation Standards and Objectives for Science in West Virginia Schools

20A056ACE2104DF1BD60B8890BD1373B.description: write routinely over extended time frames (time for reflection and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

FC84D3016D844545BDBDBFFB4969EA1B.description: draw evidence from informational texts to support analysis, reflection and research.

CE1D78583294401CA4CE5D7C28AB7BE0.description: gather relevant information from multiple authoritative print and digital sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the usefulness of each source in answering the research question and integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

6508D407BE3C4A5BA1B04E720424BFCE.description: conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem and narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

BBB36AB45F084D918FE8C9194CE8FC77.description: Writing - Research to Build and Present Knowledge

FB8CDC4E204C4BB288DE02B237DC9649.description: use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish and update individual or shared writing products, taking advantage of technology's capacity to link to other information and to display information flexibly and dynamically.

3A8DD0EB0D20436D8EBD7E204702B8CD.description: develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.

4144317EF3E7409895992DE145E23EF9.description: produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization and style are appropriate to task, purpose and audience.

6E6BB6FF944D498488DC1D61E2D49923.description: Writing - Production and Distribution of Writing

3FD13DF0F8654E92922B4414A52CB246.description:
write informative/explanatory texts, including the narration of historical events, scientific procedures/experiments, or technical processes:
  • introduce a topic and organize ideas, concepts, and information to make important connections and distinctions; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g. figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.
  • develop the topic with well-chosen, relevant and sufficient facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.
  • use varied transitions and sentence structures to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.
  • use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to manage the complexity of the topic and convey a style appropriate to the discipline and context as well as to the expertise of likely readers.
  • establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.
  • provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

AF85D785E5C4497181C91C72468EE3C3.description:
write arguments focused on discipline-specific content:
  • introduce precise claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims and create an organization that establishes clear relationships among the claim(s), counterclaims, reasons and evidence.
  • develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly, supplying data and evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both claim(s) and counterclaims in a discipline-appropriate form and in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level and concerns.
  • use words, phrases and clauses to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence and between claim(s) and counterclaims.
  • establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.
  • provide a concluding statement or section that follows from or supports the argument presented.

2DF73889E7FC4B9ABE852DED48CAA8A9.description: by the end of grade 10, read and comprehend science/technical texts in the grades 9–10 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

7B55E495DAE74501ABA30458992FF457.description: Reading - Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

FDCEFEF512614199AABE13FC7DF9E336.description: compare and contrast findings presented in a text to those from other sources (including their own experiments), noting when the findings support or contradict previous explanations or accounts.

06512D796F1040FBA649C16375EA6229.description: assess the extent to which the reasoning and evidence in a text support the author's claim or a recommendation for solving a scientific or technical problem.

AB29EE8CDCF645A2B01F30120EDF2195.description: translate quantitative or technical information expressed in words in a text into visual form (e.g., a table or chart) and translate information expressed visually or mathematically (e.g., in an equation) into words.

C080ABF3F62B45F79C596FF5CCA7F534.description: Reading - Integration of Knowledge and Ideas

C600B63DD5424C9E901A1CB8D7D1DF63.description: analyze the author's purpose in providing an explanation, describing a procedure, or discussing an experiment in a text, defining the question the author seeks to address.

ED63A838FE0E40ACBADD18CC375ED196.description: analyze the structure of the relationships among concepts in a text, including relationships among key terms (e.g., force, friction, reaction force, energy).

C6CCD889102143C8A66DA5F8FD9D1D25.description: determine the meaning of symbols, key terms, and other domain-specific words and phrases as they are used in a specific scientific or technical context relevant to grades 9–10 texts and topics.

1CB4897195A9408EBB3A4DC1AE97F402.description: follow precisely a complex multistep procedure when carrying out experiments, taking measurements, or performing technical tasks, attending to special cases or exceptions defined in the text.

BC043791AC22412F959DF5A925379810.description: determine the central ideas or conclusions of a text; trace the text's explanation or depiction of a complex process, phenomenon, or concept; provide an accurate summary of the text.

F485595E154443D19C90F7FB56E22886.description: cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of science and technical texts, attending to the precise details of explanations or descriptions.

9C09911AA6CB468C8E30B7E85B888E73.description: use a computer simulation to model the impact of proposed solutions to a complex real-world problem with numerous criteria and constraints on interactions within and between systems relevant to the problem.

36DEB004050C457FAA9740F07223D9F2.description: evaluate a solution to a complex real-world problem based on prioritized criteria and trade-offs that account for a range of constraints, including cost, safety, reliability, and aesthetics, as well as possible social, cultural, and environmental impacts.

7321D178BA2343A38325BC51762902B8.description: design a solution to a complex real-world problem by breaking it down into smaller, more manageable problems that can be solved through engineering.

D26E2F5EF2DD41A7A9718A75C689657D.description: analyze a major global challenge to specify qualitative and quantitative criteria and constraints for solutions that account for societal needs and wants.

AE428413249E4157AB5343A51D4EBE2D.description: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science

A87080167E9C4423A2D862BD854D4A4F.description: research disease causative factors, symptoms, prevention and treatment.

7679819261C749F1B2F832A6C51702D0.description: assess the role of components of the immune system in defending the body.

BA44FB6B8E324038BA0C120CD5E557B7.description: outline the events of reproduction for the formation of gametes through fertilizations and embryological development.

F6E6888F10114D9391FD259787659C80.description: compare and contrast the structure and function of male and female reproductive systems.

D66BE8C45AD143E8AD297918A630C6F0.description: integrate the functions of the excretory system to the maintenance of the other body systems.

B03E99505AA84CFDA04DF467A1F36DA6.description: compare the compatibility of blood types and assess the molecular basis for blood functions.

EFF2806B9A654D5599BA02B1315EF5BB.description:
illustrate the structures of the circulatory and lymphatic systems and the function of blood to the role of:
  • transportation
  • cellular support
  • defense.

4493D9F299684D4C8F1466383713C62D.description: explain how structures of the respiratory system are essential to cellular respiration, gas exchange and communication.

CFF8C1FA070E4914BC02294BD07F8EB3.description: analyze the role of components and processes of the digestive system in supplying essential nutrients.

BD3440ADC3554B0886D4B22066467631.description: incorporate the role of endocrine glands and their hormones into the overall functions and dysfunctions of the body.

F794853F82084E5D8CF0E47152F2EF0A.description: apply the action of specific enzymes to their roles in bodily functions.

42EC77924CF540A2ABB716350D6339D5.description: apply the structure of the ear and eye to their function/dysfunction in relation to environmental perception.

27A75457C7984E7886C94E149C13BFAD.description: compare and contrast the parts and functions of the central and peripheral nervous system including the autonomic portions.

B8D8FC28880641E1B16B059729F4FA08.description: model the mechanism of a nerve impulse at the cellular and molecular levels.

13BEC469E1A84829A1080E15156DC3F7.description: classify the various types of neurons emphasizing the relationship of structure and function.

6B01A85A09174BDDA64A7039377C3C79.description:
model the muscular system including:
  • locations
  • origins
  • insertions
  • muscle groups
  • types of muscles.

075FB64463774D9E8D9FE9F1169188AA.description: integrate the skeletal, muscular and nervous systems to the functioning of the organism.

5B2E3DF506B64D25929EBE2F5D3E86A1.description: model the mechanisms of muscular contraction on the cellular and molecular levels.

9E550EDB2AB34C3385F1E4C729E37C8B.description:
correlate the structure and function of the elements of the skeletal system:
  • bone
  • articulations
  • insertions.

01F878BF65864FDC8AE03FA17685936F.description: relate how bone tissue is important to the development of the human skeleton.

BB256D7F9A7441A084BC809E32D6CD5E.description:
relate the structure of the integumentary system to its function as a/an:
  • sensory organ
  • environmental barrier
  • temperature regulator.

9642312669AE4D22A5362B1ABFD42A32.description:
categorize, by structure and function, the various types of human tissue:
  • muscle
  • epithelial
  • connective
  • nervous.

5732B784397B4393A5046B4147BA5041.description:
describe the organizational levels, interdependency and the interaction of:
  • cells
  • tissues

94EF9582794D4D43AAEA212110D9AA9B.description:
write informative/explanatory texts, including the narration of historical events, scientific procedures/experiments, or technical processes:
  • introduce a topic and organize complex ideas, concepts and information so that each new element builds on that which precedes it to create a unified whole; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures and tables), and multimedia when useful to aid comprehension.
  • develop the topic thoroughly by selecting the most significant and relevant facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.

6CC398A1CFBC4010977F31290599D49F.description: Demonstrate basic knowledge of one-to-one letter-sound correspondences by producing the primary or many of the most frequent sounds for each consonant.

F27914712895484DAE703733EA0011A9.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.
