document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for English Language Arts

FD47CBD6A32945E091A0DAC579041560.description: Acquire and accurately use general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college- and career-readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

A43B9A2E39B44FB58113CA1DC7600251.description: Analyze nuances in the meaning of words with similar denotations.

F030C6E2DB684887BD5C609AC7A8020F.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., euphemism or oxymoron) in context and analyze their role in the text.

781A316DEE594E9FA5AEC08BC58E356D.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

AF8BCB95F828476DA720099302BAD528.description: Verify the initial determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

00B13D3C133D48DCBAAFF06F78F89F74.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, and/or thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning, its part of speech, or its etymology.

87E7232E3EA443029BF548B72EF9C9F2.description: Identify and correctly use patterns of word changes that indicate different meanings or parts of speech (e.g., analyze, analysis, analytical, advocate, or advocacy).

4995D47782F7485CB3FCAC63BC9E8C25.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence, paragraph or text or a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

65E11E78C0B241B694594E1FA8C46318.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 9 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

687D1A8F105648EBB628CCA71FC7F2EA.description: Write and edit work so that it conforms to the guidelines in a style manual (e.g., MLA Handbook or APA Handbook) appropriate for the discipline and writing type.

3F4D639AC78C4CE4BB2DE03B4EB40ADC.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

278E1FECD662445D9FBFE389E6A6BDC8.description: Use a colon to introduce a list or quotation.

6806EC15045F41D3A591BFD5AC670CE6.description: Use a semicolon (and perhaps a conjunctive adverb) to link two or more closely related independent clauses.

95B803397377409E8A6AC40F867EEC79.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

AE8DBB180F8B47708FD1707C0F435081.description: Use various types of phrases (noun, verb, adjectival, participial, prepositional, and absolute) and clauses (independent, dependent, noun, relative, and adverbial) to convey specific meanings and add variety and interest to writing or presentations.

C5A7863427684D9483E1330BF33C06B3.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

9A8084A730914699B3A3A7FF5604D939.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate. (See grade 9 Language standards for specific expectations.)

944C5A89248049F0BECAAA5A95FE8FF1.description: Make strategic use of digital media (e.g., textual, graphical, audio, visual, and interactive elements) in presentations to enhance understanding of findings, reasoning, and evidence and to add interest.

DA374155434C4CE08B2FC84BCC36BCD2.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence clearly, concisely, and logically, such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, substance, and style are appropriate to purpose, audience, and task.

34325128F68547E999B21E01157E932E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric, identifying any fallacious reasoning or exaggerated or distorted evidence.

FB9694600F2D4DC581201CB0EE20FC8D.description: Integrate multiple sources of information presented in diverse media or formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, and/or orally), evaluating the credibility and accuracy of each source.

84834AA3740945278C5BD24360B7D724.description: Respond thoughtfully to diverse perspectives; summarize points of agreement and disagreement and, when warranted, qualify or justify views and understanding and make new connections in light of the evidence and reasoning presented.

BD4AACCA47424A7199C35A054AC590CC.description: Propel conversations by posing and responding to questions that relate the current discussion to broader themes or larger ideas; actively incorporate others into the discussion; and clarify, verify, or challenge ideas and conclusions.

7BD481EC03EF41C38EBBAAA4E3E733D8.description: Work with peers to set rules for collegial discussions and decision-making (e.g., informal consensus, taking votes on key issues, or presentation of alternate views); set clear goals, deadlines, and individual roles as needed.

2D341F8773554C109D2D44E2B999591D.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read and researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence from texts and other research on the topic or issue to stimulate a thoughtful, well-reasoned exchange of ideas.

E7DE3045FC9C488DBF683BF6F46857E5.description: Initiate and effectively participate in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 9 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing ideas clearly and persuasively.

08F6E9BF789445188C7E98FC00CDFC9F.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

DC031D1ECB024D269C77FD7D8BE41AAF.description: Apply grade 9 Reading standards to nonfiction and other informational texts (e.g., "Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is valid and the evidence is relevant and sufficient; identify false statements and fallacious reasoning").

7C9C912E0ABD4858B50D602558494D01.description: Apply grade 9 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Analyze how an author draws on and transforms source material in a specific work [e.g., how Shakespeare treats a theme or topic from Ovid or the Bible, or how a later author draws on a play by Shakespeare]").

F0380205EC114FB0B3450AA39A3D1806.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

05A320CDD866409D99C6D23B04261816.description: Gather relevant information from multiple authoritative print and digital sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the usefulness of each source in answering the research question; integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation (e.g., MLA or APA).

F1C322EC60A5452888F832055232C694.description: Conduct short, as well as more sustained, research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

815114200F2E4A1F98BAE709DBCE219B.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

3F15A7DD52C648B2BE40F721B7CB3946.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products, taking advantage of technology's capacity to link to other information and to display information flexibly and dynamically.

73664B0DD35B42D3B1180C5A7401D557.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience. (Editing for conventions should demonstrate command of all Language standards up to and including grade 9.)

4C97573E968947638B68A63393E25C99.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in Text Types and Purposes.)

10CD3C6D7690483AB794AA14632CD97D.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on what is experienced, observed, or resolved over the course of the narrative.

267CC561EAF641E0877778F549CFF500.description: Use precise words and phrases, effective details, and sensory language to convey a vivid picture of the experiences, events, setting, and/or characters.

B862DD73EB9A4D739E4C4691A5F4FBAC.description: Use a variety of techniques to sequence events so that they build on one another to create a coherent whole.

6D5758D2C7A84F089F5CE11932F81321.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple plot lines, to develop experiences events and/or characters.

65156336A04A43D7BDECF6C6C429C678.description: Engage and orient the reader by setting out a problem, situation, or observation, establishing one or multiple point(s) of view and introducing a narrator and/or characters; create a smooth progression of experiences or events.

F23A25415AD741D69E744BDD23A338A9.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

E11920FAF0B3478FA3810D0254C1E4A5.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

B1ED55BF580341FF8F256E60F818C128.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline.

C63C09BA553D474DA59688DCE9246AC1.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to manage the complexity of the topic.

B5E6B44E706A4B42AA78944145EC116E.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.

E12448AE89C545CA8A36B19DE75C2B6E.description: Develop the topic with well-chosen, relevant and sufficient facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.

4ED01A1932CF4A618376A2371A54369E.description: Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, and information to make important connections and distinctions; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures and/or tables), and multimedia when useful to aid comprehension.

9C28B80BCB8D4C55A4585AE646D97262.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

4FA7BB11EE604B03B7A858F542F34BA4.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

0F1FEC1774DE4B1A9ADFF254A76ECE29.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline.

E3E508CEC8714B478A51FE98293F283C.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence, and between claim(s) and counterclaims.

80B22C16FE2945D79A7C1C7E64E6EDC7.description: Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly, supplying evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level and concerns.

72B6AAF5A3704E46A9A0B60F46F03536.description: Introduce precise claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that establishes clear relationships among claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

B80C4ACEA58D4481AA9A1F350A550F39.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

FB58177CB1924C96B75D44412174D5DD.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend nonfiction and other informational texts in the grades 9-10 text complexity range proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

918EC0E3C08347BAB0AB37CFCAED2D6E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, in the grade 9-10 text complexity range proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

54247A84FBBC4B9BB4ED6EB3263D90F6.description: Range of Reading and Text Complexity

7F1530D0E8C040CEA60AD3200D2A5776.description: Analyze influential U.S. documents of historical and literary significance (e.g., Washington's Farewell Address or The Gettysburg Address), including how they address related themes and concepts.

05C43B5E458E42CF9929F93F66A8BC01.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in an informational text, assessing whether the reasoning is valid and the evidence is relevant and sufficient; identify false statements and fallacious reasoning.

7F5042E25AC14DDA825B0C0C61525300.description: Analyze various accounts of a subject told in different mediums of informational texts (e.g., a person's life story in both print and multimedia), determining which details are emphasized in each account.

37EE540C80184AA99678166DDE0B7065.description: Analyze how an author draws on and transforms source material in a specific literary work (e.g., how Shakespeare treats a theme or topic from Ovid or the Bible, or how a later author draws on a play by Shakespeare).

72E4EDA07BEB4BDE9A3C707BD32F4F78.description: Analyze the representation, in a literary text, of a subject or a key scene in two different artistic mediums, including what is emphasized or absent in each treatment (e.g., Auden's "Musée des Beaux Arts" and Breughel's Landscape with the Fall of Icarus).

399B1AFB1819427189EAC8234C8F3AF6.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in an informational text and analyze how the author uses rhetoric to advance that point of view or purpose.

DFFA0BD942B84204B6F1F8497F658BDA.description: Analyze in detail how an author's ideas or claims are developed and refined by particular sentences, paragraphs, or larger portions of an informational text (e.g., a section or chapter).

42A6C52589C74F3983D5BAF64C44D284.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in an informational text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze the cumulative impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone (e.g., how the language of a court opinion differs from that of a newspaper).

E55B0FEAEDE649049F0EE71D80D5ECC7.description: Analyze a particular point of view or cultural experience reflected in a work of literature from outside the United States, drawing on a wide reading of world literature.

366CDA359E334B6B8A847C7691FA6E88.description: Analyze how an author's choices concerning how to structure a literary text, order events within it (e.g., parallel plots), and manipulate time (e.g., pacing or flashbacks) create such effects as mystery, tension, or surprise.

F83673EA2E9445A7A460F16FC99EC442.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in the literary text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the cumulative impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone (e.g., how the language evokes a sense of time and place or how it sets a formal or informal tone).

C94A0354332A463286F51CC5B9A4E123.description: Analyze how the author unfolds an analysis or series of ideas or events in an informational text, including the order in which the points are made, how they are introduced and developed, and the connections that are drawn between them.

578C6FAAE7FF453BBC8C1098BE68D011.description: Determine a central idea of an informational text and analyze its development over the course of the informational text, including how it is developed and refined by specific details; provide an objective summary of the informational text.

4EF52624B3F1418BBE732334000E7D53.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the informational text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the informational text.

D4123A8AC6A74AA597BD14CB9468DE63.description: Analyze how complex characters (e.g., those with multiple or conflicting motivations) develop over the course of a literary text, interact with other characters, and advance the plot or develop the theme.

AF28BBBD3D644A868847717F527373C6.description: Determine a theme or central idea of a literary text and analyze in detail its development over the course of the literary text, including how it emerges and is shaped and refined by specific details; provide an objective summary of the literary text.

274C7D5410FE4220A84223E84F6DF53C.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the literary text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the literary text.

D363EAD6CE564A36AA6F799A87114399.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in an informational text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze how an author uses and refines the meaning of a key term or terms over the course of a text (e.g., how Madison defines "faction" in Federalist No. 10).

C362611EC4D240EE832B1DB0137AAA3F.description: Analyze how an author's choices concerning how to structure specific parts of a literary text (e.g., the choice of where to begin or end a story, and the choice to provide a comedic or tragic resolution) contribute to its overall structure and meaning as well as its aesthetic impact.

75C12B0561E24DA49BD91CE56EAD6290.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a variety of literary texts, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including words with multiple meanings or language that is particularly fresh, engaging, or beautiful. (Include Shakespeare as well as other authors.)

D2CC2C1BDAA54474A7ACF144789D7D53.description: Analyze a complex set of ideas or sequence of events and explain how specific individuals, ideas, or events interact and develop over the course of the informational text and media.

3801C6B5626B4B5E81A2E801F32BDB41.description: Determine two or more central ideas of an informational text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to provide a complex analysis; provide an objective summary of the informational text.

36F87A13555B49C6B260619D224920B5.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the informational text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where the informational text leaves matters uncertain.

4F691D649E044BEA9ACB781D9D39B38B.description: Analyze the impact of the author's choices regarding how to develop and relate elements of a story or drama (e.g., where a story is set, how the action is ordered, and how the characters are introduced and developed).

BBDAA6EBCB5B41109DE178C040347A63.description: Determine two or more themes or central ideas of a literary text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to produce a complex account; provide an objective summary of the literary text.

D1EF855E37B649C6ACD3DD36E71198BE.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the literary text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where the literary text leaves matters uncertain.

5F2B72D5656549608E4D8914B5DEC488.description: Transition English Language Arts for Seniors

1CC338F12EFE4B7A91F96D1ABD943759.description: Acquire and accurately use general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college- and career-readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

F47BB61F1A254F23BC26B3B3EBEF8B09.description: Analyze nuances in the meaning of words with similar denotations.

ED338FB90D0444ADABAECE266A32EF03.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., hyperbole and paradox) in context and analyze their role in the text.

1B4CD34154F74983852104CDBD953650.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

A7FDFF096AB84442B3858BA0F69AB735.description: Verify the initial determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

F154A540AF4344679CFDAD4025E7E23C.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, and/or thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning, its part of speech, its etymology, or its standard usage.

82E92F85EC4F4A0B975B37AD89E0E4A0.description: Identify and correctly use patterns of word changes that indicate different meanings or parts of speech (e.g., conceive, conception, or conceivable).

EFB74DC11579425684D35B788690B8A7.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence, paragraph, or text; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

6649A3172A7D46A8801FD021CF95C107.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 12 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

628DE41FFD834710A2C80670409D90F7.description: Vary syntax for effect, consulting references (e.g., Tufte's Artful Sentences) for guidance as needed; apply an understanding of syntax to the study of complex texts when reading.

9709BC359937461390821FC8296DD78F.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

CDBFCB0E78CB4D589E27972C04ADA6E5.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

72A6C1BE4AED4D0E91235207A2ED50A4.description: Resolve issues of complex or contested usage, consulting references (e.g., Merriam-Webster's Dictionary of English Usage or Garner's Modern American Usage) as needed.

FCCD4225EEEC4E4BB2806ADFFF115CD6.description: Apply the understanding that usage is a matter of convention, can change over time, and is sometimes contested.

82FE9DC9A35044F988DCD58A57B307AC.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

53B6060B77BA4FAFAE2E0F201350106B.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating a command of formal English when indicated or appropriate. (See grade 12 Language standards for specific expectations.)

2F19783386F94DE9BCB36250A357C5FA.description: Make strategic and engaging use of digital media (e.g., textual, graphical, audio, visual, and interactive elements) in presentations to enhance understanding of findings, reasoning, and evidence and to add interest.

09BC41BDB98745B3833C07A8B5123907.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence, conveying a clear and distinct perspective, such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning; address alternative or opposing perspectives and determine if the organization, development, substance, and style are appropriate to purpose, audience and a range of formal and informal tasks.

CA510242114D4BCB962E28EB6C9951DF.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and uses of evidence and rhetoric, in order to assess the stance, premises, links among ideas, word choice, points of emphasis, and tone used among multiple speakers.

84A1E3B337DD44F3827133B8C168749A.description: Integrate multiple sources of information presented in diverse formats and media (e.g., visually, quantitatively, and/or orally) in order to make informed decisions and solve problems, evaluating the credibility and accuracy of each source and analyzing any discrepancies among the data.

482AAE9DFC6A46D6B1170D1A95E64556.description: Respond thoughtfully to diverse perspectives; synthesize and evaluate comments, claims, and evidence made on all sides of an issue; resolve contradictions when possible; and determine what additional information or research is required to deepen the investigation or complete the task.

20ACC3FE03834A6C9D96448240BFCD54.description: Propel conversations by posing and responding to questions that probe reasoning and evidence; ensure a hearing for a full range of positions on a topic or issue; clarify, verify, or challenge ideas and conclusions; and promote divergent and creative perspectives.

1CE250FA82C04588B7804610CD04EF86.description: Work with peers to promote civil, democratic discussions and decision-making; set clear goals and deadlines; establish norms and experience various individual roles.

336E1AE7A3AC4440B23A9194CABE9CDB.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read and researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence from texts and other research on the topic or issue to stimulate a thoughtful, well-reasoned exchange of ideas.

63E167F0511D40A79988A7F0DFBAE44A.description: Initiate and effectively participate in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 12 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing ideas clearly and persuasively.

F5F494FB29B64454B2FAF32B6F869529.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

5214ADD43F27438198EA28F97A873D2D.description: Apply grade 12 Reading standards to nonfiction and other informational texts (e.g., "Delineate and evaluate the reasoning in influential U.S. texts, including the application of constitutional principles [e.g., in U.S. Supreme Court Case majority opinions and dissents] and the premises, purposes and arguments in works of public advocacy [e.g., The Federalist Papers or presidential addresses]").

DFF7462E607C4F7C9746FAD9AFB5D03A.description: Apply grade 12 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Demonstrate knowledge of eighteenth-, nineteenth-, and early-twentieth-century foundational works of American literature, including how two or more texts from the same period treat similar themes or topics").

94FEEF99755840078E854F3EA22EE703.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

49A859EE13AE4F6E9EDB766B195C3C8B.description: Gather and synthesize relevant information from multiple authoritative print and digital sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the strengths and limitations of each source in terms of the task, purpose, and audience; integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and overreliance on any one source and following a standard format for citation (e.g., MLA or APA).

23319835478141069CBF4BE0EF21708E.description: Conduct sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

13D517E9633B44FE865FBCA1696E1A19.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

C77B9E3748D74FAA8F5C5A18428D7F87.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products in response to ongoing feedback, including new arguments or information.

F91AD140F41E4EABA78407164176D756.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience. (Editing for conventions should demonstrate command of all Language standards up to and including grade 12.)

3CFBED657A244813BAF2B58AACC8570D.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in Text Types and Purposes.)

5C69CB13C10A422C9460959D97CB9B6B.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on what is experienced, observed, or resolved over the course of the narrative.

AEE50F84D40241088BD065384859597C.description: Use precise words and phrases, effective details, and sensory language to convey a vivid picture of the experiences events, setting, and/or characters.

3F821FD8A9B642D0B196A702439F37F9.description: Use and evaluate a variety of techniques to sequence events so that they build on one another to create a coherent whole and build toward a particular tone and outcome (e.g., a sense of mystery, suspense, growth, or resolution).

4E7B22635E9E427D9045AC4C460F259B.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple plot lines, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

4E8E2CA5C62645B5B45836EEAB7E7D6A.description: Engage and orient the reader by setting out a problem, situation, or observation and its significance, establishing multiple point(s) of view and introducing a narrator and/or characters; create a smooth progression of experiences or events.

C435535526C94B2495B2232A6C91E35E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

D079CF9BADA64AD18A938D24FDD143B8.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

798531B519E848C9B11A64792346E599.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline.

31FDAAB706FA439481F4024C57814778.description: Use precise language, domain-specific vocabulary, and techniques such as metaphor, simile, and analogy to manage the complexity of the topic.

4409DFA2358948E19DB4D7F647692EEC.description: Use and evaluate appropriate and varied transitions and syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.

A73681E2D9A44D6980441B2E78813120.description: Evaluate the topic thoroughly by selecting the most significant and relevant facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.

A9185D08807A418DAC17E8106376EFB3.description: Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, and information so that each new element builds on that which precedes it to create a unified whole; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures and/or tables), and multimedia when useful to aid comprehension.

133059F8F91D4C9793697EE3824BD25F.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

6B5F6644AA234FFBA508613318C0D263.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

8683E2C4B60647D1A44E7ABFF24B20B1.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline.

40FFA83216964AEFBE48D7E0AFBEB9DD.description: Analyze words, phrases, and clauses as well as varied syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence, and between claim(s) and counterclaims.

25537AA18D3F401DB6F65B691FB49F86.description: Develop and justify claim(s) and counterclaims fairly and thoroughly, supplying the most relevant evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level, concerns, values, and possible biases.

05EBF6346A9B4818BC5A24E80A70299F.description: Introduce precise, knowledgeable claim(s); establish the significance of the claim(s); distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims and create an organization that logically sequences claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

00293628283F43C6AD7E8C073B0E6E13.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

DECA561C5FB24A4894A54D58E9E5B96C.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend nonfiction and other informational texts independently and proficiently at the high end of the grades 11-12 text complexity range.

C230F00085CA436988180D4416E81DD6.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, independently and proficiently at the high end of the grades 11–12 text complexity range.

8E194827055447829EE6E134302811DE.description: Range of Reading and Text Complexity

F5A61F43D9274EEB80D7B58E64F65172.description: Analyze seventeenth-, eighteenth-, and nineteenth-century foundational U.S. informational documents of historical and literary significance (e.g., The Declaration of Independence, the Preamble to the Constitution, the Bill of Rights and Lincoln's Second Inaugural Address) for their themes, purposes, rhetorical features, and current relevancy.

771D42F363B547A8B5A95472D7708E44.description: Delineate and evaluate the reasoning in influential U.S. informational texts, including the application of constitutional principles (e.g., in U.S. Supreme Court majority opinions and dissents) and the premises, purposes, and arguments in works of public advocacy (e.g., The Federalist Papers or presidential addresses).

937DD23A1C5F4E6E90AD4680A80127CA.description: Integrate, evaluate, and synthesize multiple sources of information presented in different media or formats (e.g., visually and/or quantitatively) as well as in words in order to address a question or solve a problem.

7408034DC80642249A5B31D4A7E2EBA1.description: Demonstrate a deep knowledge of eighteenth-, nineteenth-, and early-twentieth-century foundational works of American literature, including how multiple literary texts from the same period treat similar themes or topics.

24F5D16CFFA749C09D1CB7CA8B287975.description: Analyze multiple interpretations of a story, drama, or poem (e.g., recorded or live production of a play or recorded novel or poetry), critically evaluating how each version interprets the source text. (Include at least one play by Shakespeare and one play by an American dramatist.)

28E08EBF46E244ECBF6FE48D41B16061.description: Determine an author's point of view, purpose, and tone in an informational text in which the rhetoric is particularly effective, analyzing how style and content contribute to the power, persuasiveness, or beauty of the text.

255D2660A89B4974952D03ED8F11532A.description: In informational text, analyze and evaluate the effectiveness of the structure an author uses in his or her exposition or argument, including how the author uses structure to make points clear, convincing, and engaging.

EED487DBB65C4A24B65C8A699397A3FA.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in an informational text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze how and why an author uses and refines the meaning of a key term or terms over the course of an informational text (e.g., how Madison defines "faction" in Federalist No. 10).

0C668FBD51D14B4CA4395B13E136D23D.description: Analyze and defend a case in which grasping a point of view requires distinguishing what is directly stated in a literary text from what is really meant (e.g., satire, sarcasm, irony, or understatement).

6D4431B2684A4BB5BCC240DC42564085.description: Analyze how an author's choices concerning how to structure specific parts of a literary text (e.g., the choice of where to begin or end a story, or the choice to provide a comedic or tragic resolution) contribute to its overall structure and meaning as well as its aesthetic impact.

C299FFB4AEE84D49AD96A9DFCC5B37DD.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a variety of literary texts, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including words with multiple meanings or language that is particularly fresh, engaging, or beautiful. (Include Shakespeare as well as other authors.)

707A4D1ECF3F4225B30EC0332FD218CD.description: Analyze a complex set of ideas or sequence of events and explain how specific individuals, ideas, or events interact and develop over the course of the informational text and media.

498F1B563AFA4FB5994825C4F4513D53.description: Determine two or more central ideas of an informational text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to provide a complex and critical analysis; provide an objective summary of the informational text.

592320B0DC5045818AE0E97C764B577C.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the informational text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where and why the informational text leaves matters uncertain.

11B3D855F2734CEF905BDCB1D5EA337E.description: Analyze the impact of the author's choices regarding how to develop and relate elements of a story or drama (e.g., where a story is set, how the action is ordered, and/or how the characters are introduced and developed).

5030B2B018C343F1B983386C54F71378.description: Determine two or more themes or central ideas of a literary text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to produce a complex account; provide an objective and critical analysis of the literary text.

19FB3FA16D3F4BE89D50DF5497DAB9CB.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the literary text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text and a variety of other sources, including determining where and why the literary text leaves matters uncertain.

document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Mathematics

A107C806CE734281A4A77E482CA3FC03.description: Relating the choice of measures of center to the shape of the data distribution and the context in which the data were gathered.

C2192F116EE848BA8AE92DAA4FA8105C.description: Giving quantitative measures of center (median and/or mean), as well as describing any overall pattern and any striking deviations from the overall pattern with reference to the context in which the data were gathered.

CFAA982D9A7346B9928F1959DB737862.description: Describing the nature of the attribute under investigation, including how it was measured and its units of measurement.

7CDCD9928E014DE18F8D3FC01368A446.description: Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context, such as by:

29CAA04F19B34ADAAB239EC632250996.description: Display numerical data in plots on a number line, including dot plots, histograms and box plots.

3FDCD98D5EB34674B99983ADABA3A0CD.description: Recognize that a measure of center for a numerical data set summarizes all of its values with a single number.

F8A7761E8D22470890C1C9B52E02B157.description: Through informal observation, understand that a set of data collected to answer a statistical question has a distribution which can be described by its center (mean/median), spread (range), and overall shape.

DC70970987094AA9A5994006E4E25E92.description: Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data related to the question and accounts for it in the answers. (e.g., "How old am I?" is not a statistical question, but "How old are the students in my school?" is a statistical question because one anticipates variability in students' ages.)

E0B4CF1DC7AB4A1AAE79B741C9686DC3.description: Use variables to represent two quantities in a real-world problem that change in relationship to one another; write an equation to express one quantity, thought of as the dependent variable, in terms of the other quantity, thought of as the independent variable. Analyze the relationship between the dependent and independent variables using graphs and tables, and relate these to the equation. (e.g., In a problem involving motion at constant speed, list and graph ordered pairs of distances and times, and write the equation d = 65t to represent the relationship between distance and time.)

D9C6895DB79342A8B5996A8D8B54047E.description: Represent and analyze quantitative relationships between dependent and independent variables.

2CC5C744C904405C96308F50A41A4C6D.description: Write an inequality of the form x > c or x < c to represent a constraint or condition in a real-world or mathematical problem. Recognize that inequalities of the form x > c or x < c have infinitely many solutions; represent solutions of such inequalities on number line diagrams.

DBC7DFCD26B749178E3C8CF8ED69640A.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations of the form x + p = q and px = q for cases in which p, q and x are all nonnegative rational numbers.

1384E7D9036C44059C92665786D565D9.description: Use variables to represent numbers and write expressions when solving a real-world or mathematical problem; understand that a variable can represent an unknown number or depending on the purpose at hand, any number in a specified set.

716485779E9A4157ACEFDECC85C213C3.description: Understand solving an equation or inequality as a process of answering a question: which values from a specified set, if any, make the equation or inequality true? Use substitution to determine whether a given number in a specified set makes an equation or inequality true.

AE4BDC6C12F34D3991545F8B9A241935.description: Reason about and solve one-variable equations and inequalities.

9558E332EDE646A6BA77093B880A2812.description: Identify when two expressions are equivalent; i.e., when the two expressions name the same number regardless of which value is substituted into them. (e.g., The expressions y + y + y and 3y are equivalent because they name the same number regardless of which number y stands for.)

D3584BECAC654628ACCAAA044372A96B.description: Apply the properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions (e.g., apply the distributive property to the expression 3 (2 + x) to produce the equivalent expression 6 + 3x; apply the distributive property to the expression 24x + 18y to produce the equivalent expression 6 (4x + 3y); apply properties of operations to y + y + y to produce the equivalent expression 3y).

F2036BBEF30A46BC8A88A89C840B6049.description: Evaluate expressions at specific values of their variables. Include expressions that arise from formulas used in real-world problems. Perform arithmetic operations, including those involving whole number exponents, in the conventional order when there are no parentheses to specify a particular order: Order of Operations (e.g., use the formulas V = s³ and A = 6 s² to find the volume and surface area of a cube with sides of length s = ½).

80FE188E5AF44632A9C2BCF9FE3FC8ED.description: Identify parts of an expression using mathematical terms (sum, term, product, factor, quotient, coefficient); view one or more parts of an expression as a single entity. (e.g., Describe the expression 2 (8 + 7) as a product of two factors; view (8 + 7) as both a single entity and a sum of two terms.)

C8A01BB8807C4024A1406D48290F2158.description: Write expressions that record operations with numbers and with letters standing for numbers. (e.g., Express the calculation, "Subtract y from 5" as 5 – y.)

FF10526E6F7F4E7A9BBFA31BEA88CC36.description: Write, read and evaluate expressions in which letters stand for numbers.

2524DA1644D8425F8CDD672C25B45BFE.description: Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents.

452A1481F9DC4ED98BA509E72831FFCD.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of arithmetic to algebraic expressions.

45500A4C1BA74ECC971A61A76586EEE1.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane. Include use of coordinates and absolute value to find distances between points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate.

F929D7CACEE44913BD39E0339E33A923.description: Distinguish comparisons of absolute value from statements about order. (e.g., recognize that an account balance less than –30 dollars represents a debt greater than 30 dollars.)

C7CA3AA3843B47E7A194380D4BA6C29F.description: Understand the absolute value of a rational number as its distance from 0 on the number line; interpret absolute value as magnitude for a positive or negative quantity in a real-world situation. (e.g., for an account balance of –30 dollars, write jrc–30jrc = 30 to describe the size of the debt in dollars).

D6C7B3C98F094F94A34A928FB5763100.description: Write, interpret, and explain statements of order for rational numbers in real-world contexts (e.g., write –3<sup>o</sup> C > –7<sup>o</sup> C to express the fact that –3<sup>o</sup> C is warmer than –7<sup>o</sup> C).

425F514F6356487185022B570F0D465D.description: Interpret statements of inequality as statements about the relative position of two numbers on a number line diagram. (e.g., interpret –3 > –7 as a statement that –3 is located to the right of –7 on a number line oriented from left to right.)

106859D2906B45BCA97C31BEC83CA809.description: Understand ordering and absolute value of rational numbers.

623130E2C5E646A8AB204E910D606378.description: Find and position integers and other rational numbers on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram; find and position pairs of integers and other rational numbers on a coordinate plane.

26E232F18E834F23B66FBBB498D5AB8C.description: Understand signs of numbers in ordered pairs as indicating locations in quadrants of the coordinate plane; recognize that when two ordered pairs differ only by signs, the locations of the points are related by reflections across one or both axes.

CF25B68E01A54382A44747F53E06DEBE.description: Recognize opposite signs of numbers as indicating locations on opposite sides of 0 on the number line; recognize that the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself, e.g., –(–3) = 3, and that 0 is its own opposite.

7164405990014F90A7F95B97EC04F655.description: Understand a rational number as a point on the number line. Extend number line diagrams and coordinate axes familiar from previous grades to represent points on the line and in the plane with negative number coordinates.

D21CD2788476439D9B7C2612EDC7A23D.description: Understand that positive and negative numbers are used together to describe quantities having opposite directions or values (e.g., temperature above/below zero, elevation above/below sea level, credits/debits, positive/negative electric charge); use positive and negative numbers to represent quantities in real-world contexts, explaining the meaning of 0 in each situation.

45BCCABE423F4A87A52BD33C62B0972C.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of numbers to the system of rational numbers.

29BEC5B00AC74054A4274328FA1D0B68.description: Find the greatest common factor of two whole numbers less than or equal to 100 and the least common multiple of two whole numbers less than or equal to 12. Use the distributive property to express a sum of two whole numbers 1–100 with a common factor as a multiple of a sum of two whole numbers with no common factor (e.g., express 36 + 8 as 4 (9 + 2)).

5B4B85039A924BA481858B904CF43645.description: Fluently add, subtract, multiply and divide multi-digit decimals using the standard algorithm for each operation.

DE18A390C4664216B199688D23AAF987.description: Fluently divide multi-digit numbers using the standard algorithm.

DA0DB76BFEE24C0C989EFBD5E536F260.description: Compute fluently with multi-digit numbers and find common factors and multiples.

BC92880BFB274E7BBB773A87C044BD5A.description: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions and solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem. (e.g., Create a story context for (2/3) ÷ (¾) and use a visual fraction model to show the quotient; use the relationship between multiplication and division to explain that (2/3) ÷ (¾) = 8/9 because ¾ of 8/9 is 2/3. (In general, (a/b) ÷ (c/d) = ad/bc.) How much chocolate will each person get if 3 people share ½ lb of chocolate equally? How many ¾-cup servings are in 2/3 of a cup of yogurt? How wide is a rectangular strip of land with length ¾ mi and area ½ square mi?)

F14F865692DE473BB584979AD468D6C5.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to divide fractions by fractions.

6CD2CC00EE374BCCB89ACDEBDE6F7E2F.description: Use ratio reasoning to convert measurement units; manipulate and transform units appropriately when multiplying or dividing quantities.

6B353425C8B049E8B467A438E0B3E59E.description: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100 (e.g., 30% of a quantity means 30/100 times the quantity); solve problems involving finding the whole, given a part and the percent.

2A1079249A984061A7BBFB619FB2B165.description: Solve unit rate problems including those involving unit pricing and constant speed. (e.g., If it took 7 hours to mow 4 lawns, then at that rate, how many lawns could be mowed in 35 hours? At what rate were lawns being mowed?)

417C1B3E99C343F093386E08F8083821.description: Make tables of equivalent ratios relating quantities with whole number measurements, find missing values in the tables, and plot the pairs of values on the coordinate plane. Use tables to compare ratios.

76A228A00BAA4E2BACD408DF41E89459.description: Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems, e.g., by reasoning about tables of equivalent ratios, tape diagrams, double number line diagrams, or equations.

C0347D3F9D76467B9ADADF47432FE1D7.description: Understand the concept of a unit rate a/b associated with a ratio a:b with b ≠ 0, and use rate language in the context of a ratio relationship. (e.g., "This recipe has a ratio of 3 cups of flour to 4 cups of sugar, so there is ¾ cup of flour for each cup of sugar." "We paid $75 for 15 hamburgers, which is a rate of $5 per hamburger.")
comments: Instructional Note: Expectations for unit rates in this grade are limited to non-complex fractions.

62EAA085025C4ADA97E3159ECCED2B94.description: Understand the concept of a ratio and use ratio language to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities. (e.g., "The ratio of wings to beaks in the bird house at the zoo was 2:1, because for every 2 wings there was 1 beak." "For every vote candidate A received, candidate C received nearly three votes.")

0681F58DA8E6406E9FA878FDFD3CB5E7.description: Understand ratio concepts and use ratio reasoning to solve problems.

2F8CFB98CCB14C018B1B9297765E1C2F.description: Represent three-dimensional figures using nets made up of rectangles and triangles, and use the nets to find the surface area of these figures. Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

0FC74163D08247519F493289858AEE8E.description: Draw polygons in the coordinate plane given coordinates for the vertices; use coordinates to find the length of a side joining points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate. Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

129274719BFF4BF5B1989FB8C6DCE6FF.description: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with fractional edge lengths by packing it with unit cubes of the appropriate unit fraction edge lengths and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths of the prism. Apply the formulas V = l w h and V = B h to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with fractional edge lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

DA5A9B773FB041A98BAF6977E210C4A7.description: Find the area of right triangles, other triangles, special quadrilaterals and polygons by composing into rectangles or decomposing into triangles and other shapes; apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

CF42F7AF5BB4409C9FFC9BFC714083E0.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, surface area, and volume.

01DB610054184754AB704D26082C0505.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

ABBC8651D3314874BABA3BDEFFC0749D.description: Look for and make use of structure.

F7D05860C6A84ACAB6677D36F312B718.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

ED6C43B96C654EEE94A0D00BF5E1F4EE.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Mathematics

EDC8A3A4A14A453BAA8814C827BF47FE.description: Compose simple shapes to form larger shapes (e.g., "Can these two triangles, with full sides touching, join to make a rectangle?").

4792BA52B1A840099C3F15EAA242A038.description: Model shapes in the world by building shapes from components (e.g., sticks and clay balls) and drawing shapes.

37A809E562A54A85B2C194588C4922FE.description: Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes, in different sizes and orientations, using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, parts (e.g., number of sides and vertices/"corners"), and other attributes (e.g., having sides of equal length).
comments: Instructional Note: Student focus should include real-world shapes.

B401B12F80154050A49D7230A4EDCBCC.description: Analyze, compare, create and compose shapes.

4437537679364B4E94098D60A385A69F.description: Through the use of real-life objects, identify shapes as two-dimensional (lying in a plane, "flat") or three-dimensional ("solid").

D91C91EED0AD46B19E6AD350913D4C55.description: Correctly name shapes regardless of their orientations or overall size.

6E945CE0F04240949171E72812444C03.description: Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes and describe the relative positions of these objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind and next to.

254483374BD74B169499D744D9A20F6F.description: Identify and describe shapes (squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres).

A568840BF3DC4B28BDC9668418116562.description: Classify objects into given categories, count the numbers of objects in each category, and sort the categories by count. Category counts should be limited to less than or equal to 10.
comments: e.g., Identify coins and sort them into groups of 5s or 10s.

203D941BFBB44620900330F3E5910E1B.description: Classify objects and count the number of objects in each category.

345ED56D0C884ACDBFA6A6843DD260ED.description: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common, to see which object has "more of" or "less of" the attribute, and describe the difference.

63CBBF2AB7BB48ABB2D900DE45A6489F.description: Describe measurable attributes of objects, such as length or weight and describe several measurable attributes of a single object.

9ED76E8FDB99414A9237A3A765F56E67.description: Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones and some further ones by using objects or drawings, and record each composition or decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 18 = 10 + 8); understand that these numbers are composed of ten ones (one ten) and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.

D47D616C8D13475095FF9E8568414CF2.description: Work with numbers 11-19 to gain foundations for place value.

F77C554706AB4BA299942CA01B508131.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

233671B3E20B48ABA1FDCB910F94166C.description: For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number by using objects or drawings, and record the answer with a drawing or equation.

EF7C5ED3C09A4775A90F004B2168A5A0.description: Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way by using objects or drawings, and record each decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 5 = 2 + 3 and 5 = 4 + 1).

1CAB0F070F4546239D6EAA84572C213B.description: Solve addition and subtraction word problems and add and subtract within 10 by using objects or drawings to represent the problem.

1C54539A170946B2BC717DD2520BE862.description: Represent addition and subtraction with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds (e.g., claps), and acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.

C7A1406CE65B48F389BDD8CD584852F8.description: Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and understand subtraction as taking apart and taking from.

205ABE647C9D411A85716FC980D5A7D2.description: Compare two numbers between 1 and 10 presented as written numerals.

F861F6FCAE7B41589581BE31F2ED70BC.description: Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to the number of objects in another group (e.g., by using matching and counting strategies).

0B1789BC2DA147ACA537B16B59A0F436.description: Count to answer questions (e.g., "How many?") about as many as 20 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, a circle, or as many as 10 things in a scattered configuration; given a number from 1–20, count out that many objects.

DA90034B8E0841B3B3F5638E10536782.description: Understand that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one larger.

305FE46F151E4314A619A7B8E4C298FC.description: Understand that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted and the number of objects is the same regardless of their arrangement or the order in which they were counted.

315831BD704441078F6501E3EE20A1A1.description: When counting objects, say the number names in the standard order, pairing each object with one and only one number name and each number name with one and only one object.

7E0C2A3752CD478C9E00FFE6E8AEF0F3.description: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities; connect counting to cardinality.

45DD7E33C33A4A6DBF8028D29B43F8CD.description: Count to tell the number of objects.

A14633DD3A714BB39DCE53BD2AE1392E.description: Write numbers from 0 to 20. Represent a number of objects with a written numeral 0-20 (with 0 representing a count of no objects).

D2534C2967204CE083E31BC094061083.description: Count forward beginning from a given number within the known sequence (instead of having to begin at 1).

D9BC798D2B2F48EFB68673A578312D9F.description: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.

AB386554C7234B68B60520312B3687E6.description: Know number names and the count sequence.

EF2A97E74F114B1596E53A3016B36BFB.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

E2CE0D4161A346C0B1FF3E79EAA6FA08.description: Look for and make use of structure.

13C054EF2C174E039AB270FDEFFED016.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

51F51E4F140B43C6A83C47812EA9CFE0.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Mathematics

811F0933121541E5999DAA8F12EF90F3.description: Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts (e.g., product testing, medical testing, and/or pulling a hockey goalie at the end of a game).
comments: Instructional Note: Extend to more complex probability models. Include situations such as those involving quality control, or diagnostic tests that yield both false positive and false negative results.

918F487194D5447AA58FB64FFEBB8B3F.description: Use probabilities to make fair decisions (e.g., drawing by lots or using a random number generator).
comments: Instructional Note: Extend to more complex probability models. Include situations such as those involving quality control, or diagnostic tests that yield both false positive and false negative results.

6F1D13E96418438C87CC662A5634940C.description: Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions.

comments: Instructional Note: In earlier grades, students are introduced to different ways of collecting data and use graphical displays and summary statistics to make comparisons. These ideas are revisited with a focus on how the way in which data is collected determines the scope and nature of the conclusions that can be drawn from that data. The concept of statistical significance is developed informally through simulation as meaning a result that is unlikely to have occurred solely as a result of random selection in sampling or random assignment in an experiment.

0D4B5BE433C5465B86DE4B9338285F8F.description: Use data from a randomized experiment to compare two treatments; use simulations to decide if differences between parameters are significant.
comments: Instructional Note: In earlier grades, students are introduced to different ways of collecting data and use graphical displays and summary statistics to make comparisons. These ideas are revisited with a focus on how the way in which data is collected determines the scope and nature of the conclusions that can be drawn from that data. The concept of statistical significance is developed informally through simulation as meaning a result that is unlikely to have occurred solely as a result of random selection in sampling or random assignment in an experiment. Focus on the variability of results from experiments—that is, focus on statistics as a way of dealing with, not eliminating, inherent randomness.

818FA337213A40D39E4CFE552D04E4D0.description: Use data from a sample survey to estimate a population mean or proportion; develop a margin of error through the use of simulation models for random sampling.
comments: Instructional Note: In earlier grades, students are introduced to different ways of collecting data and use graphical displays and summary statistics to make comparisons. These ideas are revisited with a focus on how the way in which data is collected determines the scope and nature of the conclusions that can be drawn from that data. The concept of statistical significance is developed informally through simulation as meaning a result that is unlikely to have occurred solely as a result of random selection in sampling or random assignment in an experiment. Focus on the variability of results from experiments—that is, focus on statistics as a way of dealing with, not eliminating, inherent randomness.

A2E40F03D0444811B80D0B23BA1ABE7B.description: Recognize the purposes of and differences among sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies; explain how randomization relates to each.
comments: Instructional Note: In earlier grades, students are introduced to different ways of collecting data and use graphical displays and summary statistics to make comparisons. These ideas are revisited with a focus on how the way in which data is collected determines the scope and nature of the conclusions that can be drawn from that data. The concept of statistical significance is developed informally through simulation as meaning a result that is unlikely to have occurred solely as a result of random selection in sampling or random assignment in an experiment.

2282031623A648D5BE7A9A85C46468B4.description: Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies.

9F656B1F38F24CA884595CC3BEDF6D34.description: Decide if a specified model is consistent with results from a given data-generating process, e.g., using simulation. (e.g., A model says a spinning coin falls heads up with probability 0.5. Would a result of 5 tails in a row cause you to question the model?)

DD0F855823BA477FB618DE8653CA7B3D.description: Understand statistics as a process for making inferences about population parameters based on a random sample from that population.
comments: Instructional Note: Include comparing theoretical and empirical results to evaluate the effectiveness of a treatment.

20349776B2B345D4A4D5835DE2DBEC5F.description: Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments.

AE8A8D4154CE4F3C8D10D1F04648F74D.description: Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution and to estimate population percentages. Recognize that there are data sets for which such a procedure is not appropriate. Use calculators, spreadsheets, and tables to estimate areas under the normal curve.
comments: Instructional Note: While students may have heard of the normal distribution, it is unlikely that they will have prior experience using it to make specific estimates. Build on students' understanding of data distributions to help them see how the normal distribution uses area to make estimates of frequencies (which can be expressed as probabilities). Emphasize that only some data are well described by a normal distribution.

F4654E31043C48BBAB81995E2E4A7A20.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.

177DA91F98BC4CFEA63B7D0B6A5C1943.description: For exponential models, express as a logarithm the solution to a b<sup>ct</sup> = d where a, c, and d are numbers and the base b is 2, 10, or e; evaluate the logarithm using technology.
comments: Instructional Note: Consider extending this unit to include the relationship between properties of logarithms and properties of exponents, such as the connection between the properties of exponents and the basic logarithm property that log xy = log x +log y.

D929D11992E347128DF298B2F5989436.description: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems.

7871E6E0FE4C49F98578C2390CFABC62.description: Find inverse functions. Solve an equation of the form f(x) = c for a simple function f that has an inverse and write an expression for the inverse. (e.g., f(x) = 2 x³ or f(x) = (x+1)/(x-1) for x ≠ 1.)
comments: Instructional Note: Use transformations of functions to find models as students consider increasingly more complex situations. Extend this standard to simple rational, simple radical, and simple exponential functions; connect this standard to M.A2HS.34.

F1CDE1DBA21E43D195F52A68CEC0E386.description: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology. Include recognizing even and odd functions from their graphs and algebraic expressions for them.
comments: Instructional Note: Use transformations of functions to find models as students consider increasingly more complex situations. Observe the effect of multiple transformations on a single graph and the common effect of each transformation across function types.

5BB11D48A4654C7DB9BC61A4A2E980F8.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

83521A51E81745EA9B1D9BCBBA810866.description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities. Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations. (e.g., Build a function that models the temperature of a cooling body by adding a constant function to a decaying exponential, and relate these functions to the model.)
comments: Instructional Note: Develop models for more complex or sophisticated situations than in previous courses.

411FB52D472F4FA38B3F4DBE5A37DE2E.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

AC88B6D0675D49D49B196A29A016CE8F.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). (e.g., Given a graph of one quadratic function and an algebraic expression for another, say which has the larger maximum.)
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on applications and how key features relate to characteristics of a situation, making selection of a particular type of function model appropriate.

6DF86E93C95D4B8CB4E3519CC20A9D8F.description: Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on applications and how key features relate to characteristics of a situation, making selection of a particular type of function model appropriate.

049192D2F56B420F8F4A5CC31A9AB0C4.description: Graph exponential and logarithmic functions, showing intercepts and end behavior, and trigonometric functions, showing period, midline, and amplitude.

254EEF861C3847E2936128A257DB329B.description: Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value functions.

8D7F9797867045EB9A5C145AAFD8D40B.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on applications and how key features relate to characteristics of a situation, making selection of a particular type of function model appropriate.

BC127DC5D6C3482296E5259F9E0DDF4F.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.
comments: Note: Emphasize the selection of a model function based on behavior of data and context.

0145074CE4C047AF82EFDE22C5878D19.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes. (e.g., If the function h(n) gives the number of person-hours it takes to assemble n engines in a factory, then the positive integers would be an appropriate domain for the function.)
comments: Note: Emphasize the selection of a model function based on behavior of data and context.

4E4DFF13C71348B6A00B6F2386387912.description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship. Key features include: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.
comments: Instructional Note: Emphasize the selection of a model function based on behavior of data and context.

CFCC4146154349088FA1C841E98A88CF.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of a context.

8892036FB3004AD4A23EAE9A7BBD8999.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations. (e.g., Rearrange Ohm's law V = IR to highlight resistance R.) While functions will often be linear, exponential, or quadratic the types of problems should draw from more complex situations than those addressed in Algebra I.
comments: For example, finding the equation of a line through a given point perpendicular to another line allows one to find the distance from a point to a line. This example applies to earlier instances of this standard, not to the current course.

1C03A5F3AF504DA4BC54527F65C3F680.description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or non-viable options in a modeling context. (e.g., Represent inequalities describing nutritional and cost constraints on combinations of different foods.)
comments: Instructional Note: While functions will often be linear, exponential, or quadratic the types of problems should draw from more complex situations than those addressed in Algebra I.
For example, finding the equation of a line through a given point perpendicular to another line allows one to find the distance from a point to a line.

CCF0DCBB141C4E16ADF3FEA93C7348F9.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.
comments: Instructional Note: While functions will often be linear, exponential, or quadratic the types of problems should draw from more complex situations than those addressed in Algebra I. (e.g., Finding the equation of a line through a given point perpendicular to another line allows one to find the distance from a point to a line).

025A2B4EC5854EBB8394FFB91BC52F63.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems.
comments: Instructional Note: Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.

DB2279B533EB4415891D30D99613A59F.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

91EA479F8ABE48C1913131437450A204.description: Prove the Pythagorean identity sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1 and use it to find sin (θ), cos (θ), or tan (θ), given sin (θ), cos (θ), or tan (θ), and the quadrant of the angle.
comments: Instructional Note: An Algebra II course with an additional focus on trigonometry could include the standard "Prove the addition and subtraction formulas for sine, cosine, and tangent and use them to solve problems." This could be limited to acute angles in Algebra II.

9CA81DFF3FAE4303B10B44883CE24581.description: Choose trigonometric functions to model periodic phenomena with specified amplitude, frequency, and midline.

4DD3A460D8A541B0A6302702E0269D47.description: Model periodic phenomena with trigonometric functions.

744241766A1749E1B27DDD1CFCD7DA43.description: Explain how the unit circle in the coordinate plane enables the extension of trigonometric functions to all real numbers, interpreted as radian measures of angles traversed counterclockwise around the unit circle.

F56765535BA84447B88D29A270B8185F.description: Understand radian measure of an angle as the length of the arc on the unit circle subtended by the angle.

E64472E04F684EE2B28B50B73F3A3B9E.description: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle.

105A66C7729744D5AC27FA8302A3DFB7.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases. Graph polynomial functions, identifying zeros when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.
comments: Instructional Note: Relate this standard to the relationship between zeros of quadratic functions and their factored forms.

C6F9C53DE72D4FD8989C325883B2EBDF.description: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations.
comments: Instructional Note: Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.
Instructional Note: Include combinations of linear, polynomial, rational, radical, absolute value, and exponential functions.

E5FC3AD092A645D789DCEB32D5C6D855.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.

A8DD76F49E594034A4A2E5F804BF5603.description: Solve simple rational and radical equations in one variable, and give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise.
comments: Instructional Note: Extend to simple rational and radical equations.

A9C812DC85B34600B712D358101BA370.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.

78CBC96D75CE4482B5AC259BCF2ACEF2.description: Understand that rational expressions form a system analogous to the rational numbers, closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by a nonzero rational expression; add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational expressions.
comments: Instructional Note: This standard requires the general division algorithm for polynomials.

2E164D0001BE4FCAB65C647146292710.description: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x)/b(x) in the form q(x) + r(x)/b(x), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x), using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.
comments: Instructional Note: The limitations on rational functions apply to the rational expressions.

E2C3D0C050D14E7280CA3B47F59E80E5.description: Know and apply the Binomial Theorem for the expansion of (x + y)<sup>n</sup> in powers of x and y for a positive integer n, where x and y are any numbers, with coefficients determined for example by Pascal's Triangle.
comments: Instructional Note: This cluster has many possibilities for optional enrichment, such as relating the example in M.A2HS.10 to the solution of the system u² + v² = 1, v = t(u+1), relating the Pascal triangle property of binomial coefficients to (x + y)<sup>n+1</sup> = (x + y)(x + y)n, deriving explicit formulas for the coefficients, or proving the binomial theorem by induction.

9A08D43866F444C0ABE1249306740F6B.description: Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships.
comments: For example, the polynomial identity (x² + y²)² = (x² – y²)² + (2xy)² can be used to generate Pythagorean triples.

Instructional Note: This cluster has many possibilities for optional enrichment, such as relating the example in M.A2HS.10 to the solution of the system u² + v² = 1, v = t(u+1), relating the Pascal triangle property of binomial coefficients to (x + y)<sup>n+1</sup> = (x + y)(x + y)<sup>n</sup>, deriving explicit formulas for the coefficients, or proving the binomial theorem by induction.

B1A2EB7237EF4ECB8333F1ADA76C44EE.description: Use polynomial identities to solve problems.

E7E32E5E8B4D4628B5880B6834B97B26.description: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.
