003645F08E5B4C80A462A641FFF26174.description: Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the remainder on division by x – a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if (x – a) is a factor of p(x).

7F6EC91D5E064F1A885DD2242DB23430.description: Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials.

2D89CDD8A0F149E6981681C8AA5A1A03.description: Understand that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.
comments: Instructional Note: Extend beyond the quadratic polynomials found in Algebra I.

BA981EE12A3B4D32AF0F80619C5164F6.description: Derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series (when the common ratio is not 1), and use the formula to solve problems.
comments: For example, calculate mortgage payments.
Instructional Note: Consider extending this standard to infinite geometric series in curricular implementations of this course description.

F37237CE4894470EB3498E15ACF9B595.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems.

7E81EA64EB0E4D35A349D7B6CA8058F9.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.
comments: For example, see x<sup>4</sup> – y<sup>4</sup> as (x²)² – (y²)², thus recognizing it as a difference of squares that can be factored as (x² – y²)(x² + y²).
Instructional Note: Extend to polynomial and rational expressions.

D5704E3F71B2430C8124B06F55921309.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.
comments: For example, interpret P(1 + r)<sup>n</sup> as the product of P and a factor not depending on P.

A6654FB65DC34710AA4076FB6C4C4388.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

71ACA8519F2744FA82685518EB13E61A.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.
comments: Instructional Note: Extend to polynomial and rational expressions.

321B2DBD23B64EBF90728E661B78C5ED.description: Know the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra; show that it is true for quadratic polynomials.
comments: Instructional Note: Limit to polynomials with real coefficients.

ECE2151F74984D50AA181C86DE5F3A90.description: Extend polynomial identities to the complex numbers.
comments: For example, rewrite x² + 4 as (x + 2i)(x – 2i).
Instructional Note: Limit to polynomials with real coefficients.

9C971C79252241BCA0196ED49AB4E1C0.description: Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients that have complex solutions.
comments: Instructional Note: Limit to polynomials with real coefficients.

87E66E30FFD2496CAFACF482BE9851A9.description: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations.

D5EBB68EAB944CDDB52E83C4240598CF.description: Use the relation i² = –1 and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties to add, subtract, and multiply complex numbers.

13A37808BBA6489C8235F44C32570350.description: Know there is a complex number i such that i² = −1, and every complex number has the form a + bi with a and b real.

40CDEF2672E848E4A9BE522ACE83E8DF.description: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers.

679D80D9A698468EBB938222B576DD30.description: Apply geometric methods to solve design problems (e.g., designing an object or structure to satisfy physical constraints or minimize cost; working with typographic grid systems based on ratios).

1FB72EFBFDB747FABF131F29AB7BB84D.description: Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in modeling situations (e.g., persons per square mile, BTUs per cubic foot).

8A9A2F7EA6114500A040F5E5FAE56577.description: Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe objects (e.g., modeling a tree trunk or a human torso as a cylinder).

BD236A17FF8047E4BF3A53FC938BCCBA.description: Visualize relationships between two dimensional and three-dimensional objects and apply geometric concepts in modeling situations.

8B9F93A749D4490E98D4617302FCE67F.description: Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts (e.g., product testing, medical testing, and/or pulling a hockey goalie at the end of a game).

8F1BE84550814E56B1BAD400F45D45ED.description: Use probabilities to make fair decisions (e.g., drawing by lots and/or using a random number generator).

8F5B6AE01BA541F88C232D07FDEB6141.description: Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions.
comments: Instructional Note: This unit sets the stage for work in Algebra II, where the ideas of statistical inference are introduced. Evaluating the risks associated with conclusions drawn from sample data (i.e. incomplete information) requires an understanding of probability concepts.

50ECFAF80AC9412FA7DBF0B63580FBCE.description: Use permutations and combinations to compute probabilities of compound events and solve problems.

A4DACC08283340E39FDAA6C0C6978C36.description: Apply the general Multiplication Rule in a uniform probability model, P(A and B) = P(A)P(BjrcA) = P(B)P(AjrcB), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

041229EEA01A48049E789CF8D2CB131E.description: Apply the Addition Rule, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) – P(A and B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

E14B178B00FF4369AEAA0858F98416A1.description: Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B's outcomes that also belong to A, and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

152C3EA002D147B1B7E3C8075D128721.description: Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model.

F7DC2A7425F243CE8A5029ACA5C93942.description: Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in everyday language and everyday situations.
comments: For example, compare the chance of having lung cancer if you are a smoker with the chance of being a smoker if you have lung cancer.

ABC6EB6C5788401B8C32A270E0076F76.description: Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data when two categories are associated with each object being classified. Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities.
comments: For example, collect data from a random sample of students in your school on their favorite subject among math, science, and English. Estimate the probability that a randomly selected student from your school will favor science given that the student is in tenth grade. Do the same for other subjects and compare the results.
Instructional Note: Build on work with two-way tables from Algebra I to develop understanding of conditional probability and independence.

EF05D9987C8343799555A3270EF5EFB8.description: Recognize the conditional probability of A given B as P(A and B)/P(B), and interpret independence of A and B as saying that the conditional probability of A given B is the same as the probability of A, and the conditional probability of B given A is the same as the probability of B.
comments: Instructional Note: Build on work with two-way tables from Algebra I to develop understanding of conditional probability and independence.

6B5C3C7CDB364A168EACAE2B240B989D.description: Understand that two events A and B are independent if the probability of A and B occurring together is the product of their probabilities, and use this characterization to determine if they are independent.

5D60A240D6774EB3B6884E7F95227E85.description: Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events ("or," "and," "not").

8E04A54E3EC342C7A3EEBD693428A244.description: Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data.

60F8F0BDED78437790F74B7BE6A4C468.description: Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe objects (e.g., modeling a tree trunk or a human torso as a cylinder).
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on situations in which the analysis of circles is required.

EF59F672A90A456792E4CFE7EFFB4E08.description: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations.

5573E3B9DAE4466287F9E705C2A6D1D7.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically. (e.g., Prove or disprove that a figure defined by four given points in the coordinate plane is a rectangle; prove or disprove that the point (1, √3) lies on the circle centered at the origin and containing the point (0, 2).)
comments: Instructional Note: Include simple proofs involving circles.

DDBC4FBDED16495CBE830A57B31841F2.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

D713597BDFF649EC8B4A13CA44F7D538.description: Derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius using the Pythagorean Theorem; complete the square to find the center and radius of a circle given by an equation.

1F413A85BE3B4BC1AAF0C8144B3F2D9B.description: Translate between the geometric description and the equation for a conic section.

C8EAA3FC92A84C599BD69FCDD28A2664.description: Derive using similarity the fact that the length of the arc intercepted by an angle is proportional to the radius, and define the radian measure of the angle as the constant of proportionality; derive the formula for the area of a sector.
comments: Instructional Note: Emphasize the similarity of all circles. Reason that by similarity of sectors with the same central angle, arc lengths are proportional to the radius. Use this as a basis for introducing radian as a unit of measure. It is not intended that it be applied to the development of circular trigonometry in this course.

FAA3400802FC418298336ABB577F789A.description: Find arc lengths and areas of sectors of circles.

1D5E63C4E4D64FD6A379E37A012094E2.description: Construct a tangent line from a point outside a given circle to the circle.

C32C548F7FD1471084F64040A1024D8C.description: Construct the inscribed and circumscribed circles of a triangle, and prove properties of angles for a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle.

17FAB59862584627B47CE81C0916EAAE.description: Identify and describe relationships among inscribed angles, radii, and chords. Include the relationship between central, inscribed, and circumscribed angles; inscribed angles on a diameter are right angles; the radius of a circle is perpendicular to the tangent where the radius intersects the circle.

77F642BA31E0447ABD407B3590E8514B.description: Prove that all circles are similar.

5B69777546264802A72BCCA9441C28C3.description: Understand and apply theorems about circles.

FE2A4FF3B8924479970512D2404548C3.description: Derive the equation of a parabola given a focus and directrix.
comments: Instructional Note: The directrix should be parallel to a coordinate axis.

5FDFAC86167D4AC9B730B55E258C1AE6.description: Translate between the geometric description and the equation for a conic section.

9B9828EF80CB49A08A9735573CC01E4F.description: Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and rectangles, e.g., using the distance formula. This standard provides practice with the distance formula and its connection with the Pythagorean theorem.

AC6AA7AD154A487E9CA7009039111235.description: Find the point on a directed line segment between two given points that partitions the segment in a given ratio.

272553339CB148DDA3E46E64C2BDCB84.description: Prove the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines and uses them to solve geometric problems. (e.g., Find the equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line that passes through a given point.)
comments: Instructional Note: Relate work on parallel lines to work in High School Algebra I involving systems of equations having no solution or infinitely many solutions.

A42FB99779014040B3D7BCBFDDBC662D.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically. (e.g., Prove or disprove that a figure defined by four given points in the coordinate plane is a rectangle; prove or disprove that the point (1, √3) lies on the circle centered at the origin and containing the point (0, 2).

E36AF7C96DFD46D28CAB5ECB16E97D0B.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

1B34CC1F8E0F40AB849DA5B6896888C8.description: Connecting Algebra and Geometry Through Coordinates

A569EAFF5F3540DB8E13E6160A7D3937.description: Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe objects (e.g., modeling a tree trunk or a human torso as a cylinder).
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on situations that require relating two- and three-dimensional objects, determining and using volume, and the trigonometry of general triangles.

531AF94ABE2A4A6F963C210DEEA61E79.description: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations.

21CD32104F604359BE099458095EFC3B.description: Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of three-dimensional objects, and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects.

278A57D763B441E2843BA78C5E1558F4.description: Visualize the relation between two dimensional and three-dimensional objects.

16FF72EDF81B41FD9BCCD9268A574DA8.description: Use volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to solve problems.
comments: Instructional Note: Informal arguments for area and volume formulas can make use of the way in which area and volume scale under similarity transformations: when one figure in the plane results from another by applying a similarity transformation with scale factor k, its area is k² times the area of the first. Similarly, volumes of solid figures scale by k³ under a similarity transformation with scale factor k.

118BC7A346BF440F92F533A64FDB8700.description: Give an informal argument for the formulas for the circumference of a circle, area of a circle, volume of a cylinder, pyramid, and cone. Use dissection arguments, Cavalieri's principle, and informal limit arguments.
comments: Instructional Note: Informal arguments for area and volume formulas can make use of the way in which area and volume scale under similarity transformations: when one figure in the plane results from another by applying a similarity transformation with scale factor k, its area is k² times the area of the first. Similarly, volumes of solid figures scale by k³ under a similarity transformation with scale factor k.

6C2A23B74AAA4DD5AE6212F03397BBAC.description: Explain volume formulas and use them to solve problems.

AF4DCB5119AD4E40B55CAECF44050221.description: Understand and apply the Law of Sines and the Law of Cosines to find unknown measurements in right and non-right triangles.
comments: Instructional Note: With respect to the general case of the Laws of Sines and Cosines, the definitions of sine and cosine must be extended to obtuse angles.

16C043A08F6B4A748F13A61D3052E019.description: Prove the Laws of Sines and Cosines and use them to solve problems.
comments: Instructional Note: With respect to the general case of the Laws of Sines and Cosines, the definitions of sine and cosine must be extended to obtuse angles.

A98C1F5EE87D4E56BB6512A3A80FAC88.description: Derive the formula A = ½ ab sin(C) for the area of a triangle by drawing an auxiliary line from a vertex perpendicular to the opposite side.

892E49ACE1B947EBB09600014D913D64.description: Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles in applied problems.

1B21ED42C1EB4FEC9EC778DB609242F3.description: Explain and use the relationship between the sine and cosine of complementary angles.

78CF900D4F004A609D8D77006EBFCEDA.description: Understand that by similarity, side ratios in right triangles are properties of the angles in the triangle, leading to definitions of trigonometric ratios for acute angles.

C6D581971A464C22B47B04573260BAC1.description: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles.

D48ECFA9D9DE4DA499AA16F08A5D3987.description: Use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to solve problems and to prove relationships in geometric figures.

D3A264A652764CD3B88BAF782A90BF97.description: Prove theorems about triangles. Theorems include: a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two proportionally, and conversely; the Pythagorean Theorem proved using triangle similarity.

4900567C21C9456FA5349771D1730927.description: Use the properties of similarity transformations to establish the AA criterion for two triangles to be similar.

6AB58D068A8C4F18BCAA0E0CF8E3F2A7.description: Given two figures, use the definition of similarity in terms of similarity transformations to decide if they are similar; explain using similarity transformations the meaning of similarity for triangles as the equality of all corresponding pairs of angles and the proportionality of all corresponding pairs of sides.

7ED1EA8B0F36452FAD2974B75992B234.description: The dilation of a line segment is longer or shorter in the ratio given by the scale factor.

DC38B84981B548E4BDA1874F57A088A0.description: A dilation takes a line not passing through the center of the dilation to a parallel line, and leaves a line passing through the center unchanged.

E7D8612E7B7D489194E8C85E2457971D.description: Verify experimentally the properties of dilations given by a center and a scale factor.

28CC6718C7974BCD9B362C86B0234FF3.description: Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations.

A5B1C7C4D50E4B59924518AB832D595D.description: Construct an equilateral triangle, a square, and a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle.
comments: Instructional Note: Build on prior student experience with simple constructions. Emphasize the ability to formalize and explain how these constructions result in the desired objects. Some of these constructions are closely related to previous standards and can be introduced in conjunction with them.

D2853AF9036B4F04B73283F905F3FCAD.description: Make formal geometric constructions with a variety of tools and methods (compass and straightedge, string, reflective devices, paper folding, dynamic geometric software, etc.). Copying a segment; copying an angle; bisecting a segment; bisecting an angle; constructing perpendicular lines, including the perpendicular bisector of a line segment; and constructing a line parallel to a given line through a point not on the line.
comments: Instructional Note: Build on prior student experience with simple constructions. Emphasize the ability to formalize and explain how these constructions result in the desired objects. Some of these constructions are closely related to previous standards and can be introduced in conjunction with them.

6406151C74B64B4A9F4B72EF68FAB0E8.description: Prove theorems about parallelograms. Theorems include: opposite sides are congruent, opposite angles are congruent, the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, and conversely, rectangles are parallelograms with congruent diagonals.
comments: Instructional Note: Encourage multiple ways of writing proofs, such as in narrative paragraphs, using flow diagrams, in two-column format, and using diagrams without words. Students should be encouraged to focus on the validity of the underlying reasoning while exploring a variety of formats for expressing that reasoning.

7107ADCBDB394A37AEE3CFECA15B2FAB.description: Prove theorems about triangles. Theorems include: measures of interior angles of a triangle sum to 180°; base angles of isosceles triangles are congruent; the segment joining midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half the length; the medians of a triangle meet at a point.
comments: Instructional Note: Encourage multiple ways of writing proofs, such as in narrative paragraphs, using flow diagrams, in two-column format, and using diagrams without words. Students should be encouraged to focus on the validity of the underlying reasoning while exploring a variety of formats for expressing that reasoning. Implementation of this standard may be extended to include concurrence of perpendicular bisectors and angle bisectors as preparation for M.GHS.36.

A2979810B86146818CAAE5B27899E7CD.description: Prove theorems about lines and angles. Theorems include: vertical angles are congruent; when a transversal crosses parallel lines, alternate interior angles are congruent and corresponding angles are congruent; points on a perpendicular bisector of a line segment are exactly those equidistant from the segment's endpoints.
comments: Instructional Note: Encourage multiple ways of writing proofs, such as in narrative paragraphs, using flow diagrams, in two-column format, and using diagrams without words. Students should be encouraged to focus on the validity of the underlying reasoning while exploring a variety of formats for expressing that reasoning.

D771302EAE7343FD825D36CD4D931CCD.description: Explain how the criteria for triangle congruence (ASA, SAS, and SSS) follow from the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions.
comments: Instructional Note: Rigid motions are at the foundation of the definition of congruence. Students reason from the basic properties of rigid motions (that they preserve distance and angle), which are assumed without proof. Rigid motions and their assumed properties can be used to establish the usual triangle congruence criteria, which can then be used to prove other theorems.

430BF320B4664F6FAEF7329D6FF51CCB.description: Use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to show that two triangles are congruent if and only if corresponding pairs of sides and corresponding pairs of angles are congruent.
comments: Instructional Note: Rigid motions are at the foundation of the definition of congruence. Students reason from the basic properties of rigid motions (that they preserve distance and angle), which are assumed without proof. Rigid motions and their assumed properties can be used to establish the usual triangle congruence criteria, which can then be used to prove other theorems.

C2559A0C60B943599CBE04D20DCA8DD5.description: Use geometric descriptions of rigid motions to transform figures and to predict the effect of a given rigid motion on a given figure; given two figures, use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to decide if they are congruent.
comments: Instructional Note: Rigid motions are at the foundation of the definition of congruence. Students reason from the basic properties of rigid motions (that they preserve distance and angle), which are assumed without proof. Rigid motions and their assumed properties can be used to establish the usual triangle congruence criteria, which can then be used to prove other theorems.

75E7C24A24B84376BD887CDC5F23AFC1.description: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions.

6D336167C2BA4029BA75BA823C9FE45C.description: Given a geometric figure and a rotation, reflection, or translation, draw the transformed figure using, for example, graph paper, tracing paper, or geometry software. Specify a sequence of transformations that will carry a given figure onto another.
comments: Instructional Note: Build on student experience with rigid motions from earlier grades. Point out the basis of rigid motions in geometric concepts, (e.g., translations move points a specified distance along a line parallel to a specified line; rotations move objects along a circular arc with a specified center through a specified angle)

56E6D8F1DC6B4250AC3389E1FC149E91.description: Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, and translations in terms of angles, circles, perpendicular lines, parallel lines, and line segments.
comments: Instructional Note: Build on student experience with rigid motions from earlier grades. Point out the basis of rigid motions in geometric concepts (e.g., translations move points a specified distance along a line parallel to a specified line; rotations move objects along a circular arc with a specified center through a specified angle).

F052F845232E449D898DC88734BE92FD.description: Given a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular polygon, describe the rotations and reflections that carry it onto itself.
comments: Instructional Note: Build on student experience with rigid motions from earlier grades. Point out the basis of rigid motions in geometric concepts, (e.g., translations move points a specified distance along a line parallel to a specified line; rotations move objects along a circular arc with a specified center through a specified angle).

FCE86BA4C7B44429B7A141C87F1FA714.description: Represent transformations in the plane using, for example, transparencies and geometry software; describe transformations as functions that take points in the plane as inputs and give other points as outputs. Compare transformations that preserve distance and angle to those that do not (e.g., translation versus horizontal stretch).
comments: Instructional Note: Build on student experience with rigid motions from earlier grades. Point out the basis of rigid motions in geometric concepts, (e.g., translations move points a specified distance along a line parallel to a specified line; rotations move objects along a circular arc with a specified center through a specified angle).

EBA8F41A74D2408D84A624969D9575BE.description: Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line segment, based on the undefined notions of point, line, distance along a line, and distance around a circular arc.

9F3760E125C04F7D8D81D6741201B02B.description: Experiment with transformations in the plane.

129E89C8F5DC470C89795FD0A608EA64.description: Observe using graphs and tables that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing linearly, quadratically, or (more generally) as a polynomial function.
comments: Instructional Note: Compare linear and exponential growth to quadratic growth.

01B405B1B2FA4B958EF2C0FA7509DAEC.description: Construct and compare linear, quadratic and exponential models and solve problems.

CC2D8D66B80940A3B3D6A130490B5475.description: Find inverse functions. Solve an equation of the form f(x) = c for a simple function f that has an inverse and write an expression for the inverse.
comments: For example, f(x) = 2 x3 or f(x) = (x+1)/(x-1) for x ≠ 1.
Instructional Note: Focus on linear functions but consider simple situations where the domain of the function must be restricted in order for the inverse to exist, such as f(x) = x², x > 0.

9D9C29836EF24A758A0CE69E61A2514E.description: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology. Include recognizing even and odd functions from their graphs and algebraic expressions for them.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on quadratic functions, and consider including absolute value functions.

365C6EAC147C4E17AC9F48AF1E002D51.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

FF28E9A9B589489887CC34F6BA625F4B.description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations.
comments: For example, build a function that models the temperature of a cooling body by adding a constant function to a decaying exponential, and relate these functions to the model.

A2429C1291FE4827BFB1E65D689145E4.description: Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context.

7D06EE958D4E4E10B0F571D7C22B5F0D.description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on situations that exhibit a quadratic relationship.

38FAAB06753249D79E1851B4DAED4951.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

96E696ED46BF43888E21820C6DA0ACA5.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).
comments: For example, given a graph of one quadratic function and an algebraic expression for another, say which has the larger maximum.

Instructional Note: Highlight issues of domain, range, and usefulness when examining piecewise-defined functions. Extend work with quadratics to include the relationship between coefficients and roots, and that once roots are known, a quadratic equation can be factored.

CA68ACADAEAA4CCFAEAD0F97F1774D1A.description: Use the properties of exponents to interpret expressions for exponential functions.
comments: For example, identify percent rate of change in functions such as y = (1.02)<sup>t</sup>, y = (0.97)<sup>t</sup>, y = (1.01)<sup>12t</sup>, y = (1.2)<sup>t/10</sup>, and classify them as representing exponential growth or decay.

FAB969F6D5EB468A964BC47C8323E35A.description: Use the process of factoring and completing the square in a quadratic function to show zeros, extreme values, and symmetry of the graph, and interpret these in terms of a context.

156B7CA4AE18473C8C29254443C1CEC3.description: Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.
comments: Instructional Note: Extend work with quadratics to include the relationship between coefficients and roots, and that once roots are known, a quadratic equation can be factored. This standard extends the work begun in the Linear and Exponential Relationships unit on exponential functions with integer exponents.

07710FDD38B847679BBADD8A8F0FB31E.description: Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value functions.

B8D76D00EB904D44B90B415419748B6C.description: Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima.

E4E5FC4B99644F9F89C39F4CD221E67F.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.
comments: Instructional Note: Compare and contrast absolute value, step and piecewise-defined functions with linear, quadratic, and exponential functions. Highlight issues of domain, range, and usefulness when examining piecewise-defined functions. Extend work with quadratics to include the relationship between coefficients and roots, and that once roots are known, a quadratic equation can be factored.

E167952855884E329CBBBFA249247AEA.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on quadratic functions; compare with linear and exponential functions studied in the Unit on Linear and Exponential Relationships.

60907FD36CFF400B814E38A8DFA4853F.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes.
comments: For example, if the function h(n) gives the number of person-hours it takes to assemble n engines in a factory, then the positive integers would be an appropriate domain for the function.
Instructional Note: Focus on quadratic functions; compare with linear and exponential functions studied in the Unit on Linear and Exponential Relationships.

8F391039FE6243459AE55BC4F67E98A2.description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship. Key features include: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on quadratic functions; compare with linear and exponential functions studied in the Unit on Linear and Exponential Relationships.

013B0B30F5934EFABCEC6F46C56D4A9B.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of a context.

B7E52BC7EA984AD383A76DC411C270A3.description: Explain why the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational; that the sum of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational; and that the product of a nonzero rational number and an irrational number is irrational.
comments: Instructional Note: Connect to physical situations (e.g., finding the perimeter of a square of area 2).

A8B2F1CBAB8D43B0ADAD156653BC519E.description: Use properties of rational and irrational numbers.

4983D1A224F14655A9E719293F7A56A6.description: Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically.
comments: For example, find the points of intersection between the line y = –3x and the circle x² + y² = 3.

Instructional Note: Include systems consisting of one linear and one quadratic equation. Include systems that lead to work with fractions. For example, finding the intersections between x² + y² = 1 and y = (x+1)/2 leads to the point (3/5, 4/5) on the unit circle, corresponding to the Pythagorean triple 3² + 4² = 5².

9EE86F9BA04D4D848B74EE9AC8A46CCC.description: Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x² = 49), taking square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula and factoring, as appropriate to the initial form of the equation. Recognize when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

7A3DB8BE2FDE4A3ABF920C3EBF499B01.description: Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x – p)² = q that has the same solutions. Derive the quadratic formula from this form.

822AF0C4841B4BA290DF46BB8CDEC998.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.
comments: Instructional Note: Students should learn of the existence of the complex number system, but will not solve quadratics with complex solutions until Algebra II.

65936F9066294D91BD8885389EE99A09.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

4597C046630B427AABB74590C3A0CDED.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations. (e.g., Rearrange Ohm's law V = IR to highlight resistance R.
comments: Instructional Note: Extend work on linear and exponential equations in the Relationships between Quantities and Reasoning with Equations unit to quadratic equations. Extend this standard to formulas involving squared variables.

FF1415B46EA94253AB0BC05FB90D8672.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.
comments: Instructional Note: Extend work on linear and exponential equations in the Relationships between Quantities and Reasoning with Equations unit to quadratic equations.

55F3CC90409943F6B5923ED07A00CB67.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.
comments: Instructional Note: Extend work on linear and exponential equations in the Relationships between Quantities and Reasoning with Equations unit to quadratic equations.

F35B1F0F8F8C41ABAABF468CE19AC01D.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

D4E260A5029E4F5AAEFE77C41B0BA43F.description: Recognize that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on polynomial expressions that simplify to forms that are linear or quadratic in a positive integer power of x.

5C8BEEC291BA4976B93CC9A151C4281B.description: Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions.
comments: For example the expression 1.15<sup>t</sup> can be rewritten as (1.15<sup>1/12</sup>)<sup>12t</sup> ≈ 1.012<sup>12t</sup> to reveal the approximate equivalent monthly interest rate if the annual rate is 15%.

9BCFC855B585455181CD1BC45A9DDA8A.description: Complete the square in a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function it defines.

F61CDD5C9A2B485388F7AFA31CBFB17F.description: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.

DDD7AC303D604589B4C5857DA45EBB16.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression.
comments: Instructional Note: It is important to balance conceptual understanding and procedural fluency in work with equivalent expressions. For example, development of skill in factoring and completing the square goes hand-in-hand with understanding what different forms of a quadratic expression reveal.

F444C3C774AA4EDB82D660BE6C776B54.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems.

4BDC49A8DD1A44D48C2F495D13532904.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.
comments: For example, see x<sup>4</sup> – y<sup>4</sup> as (x²)² – (y²)², thus recognizing it as a difference of squares that can be factored as (x² – y²)(x² + y²).
Instructional Note: Focus on quadratic and exponential expressions.

9C5ABCF84CA14046AD33B42EF9CBB108.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.
comments: For example, interpret P(1 + r)<sup>n</sup> as the product of P and a factor not depending on P.

Instructional Note: Exponents are extended from the integer exponents found in the unit on Relationships between Quantities and Reasoning with Equations to rational exponents focusing on those that represent square or cube roots.

DB1827BFB6964B10A95243B7E1537664.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

8DBF16697B8E4362AFCFCDD8E4C90065.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on quadratic and exponential expressions.
Instructional Note: The important distinction between a statistical relationship and a cause-and-effect relationship is the focus.

C4FC12447FBB452AB8083EF64F5F1BC0.description: Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.
comments: Instructional Note: Build on students' work with linear relationships in eighth grade and introduce the correlation coefficient. The focus here is on the computation and interpretation of the correlation coefficient as a measure of how well the data fit the relationship.

E150B25777A6448F8CB9095498D4D6C9.description: Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in the context of the data.
comments: Instructional Note: Build on students' work with linear relationships in eighth grade and introduce the correlation coefficient. The focus here is on the computation and interpretation of the correlation coefficient as a measure of how well the data fit the relationship.

16FE9C5F90EF410BBBF6401949374E9F.description: Fit a linear function for scatter plots that suggest a linear association.

1FAF7EC6AFB74BC786D5A99300DFFD74.description: Informally assess the fit of a function by plotting and analyzing residuals.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus should be on situations for which linear models are appropriate.

3D7A0C28FC974F168ACC7B6FB35564D1.description: Fit a function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data. Use given functions or choose a function suggested by the context. Emphasize linear and exponential models.

BEA391FC18E042FB8F61E9A1520BFA28.description: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related.
comments: Instructional Note: Students take a more sophisticated look at using a linear function to model the relationship between two numerical variables. In addition to fitting a line to data, students assess how well the model fits by analyzing residuals.

E36D690B46984684A05AFCA00EC0A392.description: Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal and conditional relative frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data.

C39CE1C464D94B12BE237CCF8B3FF7D5.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables.

20CB0B649AE04B49816A6BF3C2DCD8C6.description: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).
comments: Instructional Note: In grades 6 – 8, students describe center and spread in a data distribution. Here they choose a summary statistic appropriate to the characteristics of the data distribution, such as the shape of the distribution or the existence of extreme data points.

2E414DAD224249778A695704C6BD3F3F.description: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.
comments: Instructional Note: In grades 6 – 8, students describe center and spread in a data distribution. Here they choose a summary statistic appropriate to the characteristics of the data distribution, such as the shape of the distribution or the existence of extreme data points.

3259E4575866483ABC824A6D9F029507.description: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, and box plots).

EBBCC4E50B1C48EC98F5524B028DF9BE.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.

37C18A055C2C48E2BE3713F4897088DB.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function in terms of a context.
comments: Instructional Note: Limit exponential functions to those of the form f(x) = b<sup>x</sup> + k.

1A2A93B2B07E42C19CB2AEBDDE7F8175.description: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model.

8CEA6BFBFAC3414483CE7A014284E87D.description: Observe using graphs and tables that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing linearly, quadratically, or (more generally) as a polynomial function.
comments: Instructional Note: Limit to comparisons between exponential and linear models.

F202C8CC5DDF48DFA084D0EAE79735A4.description: Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a description of a relationship or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a table).
comments: Instructional Note: In constructing linear functions, draw on and consolidate previous work in Grade 8 on finding equations for lines and linear functions.

C5EC94A3059642D999213B7C0D08504B.description: Recognize situations in which a quantity grows or decays by a constant percent rate per unit interval relative to another.

B7D6BAEDB0F341C4B6406401F3162470.description: Recognize situations in which one quantity changes at a constant rate per unit interval relative to another.

0B0A242D5F61467891D416B797740191.description: Prove that linear functions grow by equal differences over equal intervals; exponential functions grow by equal factors over equal intervals.

ABC54DCE23664D93A14CFD3084688E71.description: Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions and with exponential functions.

2E9E5CD0B52046D294FA6C6936AAE63B.description: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems.

68FDFC53E83343FA8B5B2045EC8C10B8.description: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology. Include recognizing even and odd functions from their graphs and algebraic expressions for them.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on vertical translations of graphs of linear and exponential functions. Relate the vertical translation of a linear function to its y-intercept. While applying other transformations to a linear graph is appropriate at this level, it may be difficult for students to identify or distinguish between the effects of the other transformations included in this standard.

0E80D9791F5D40E896BB08867FD69DC8.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

7E160CF6B0CE46A88DDE681B2DD7050D.description: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula, use them to model situations, and translate between the two forms.
comments: Instructional Note: Limit to linear and exponential functions. Connect arithmetic sequences to linear functions and geometric sequences to exponential functions.

1B887CE42825423DBB55E7F177869253.description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations. (e.g., Build a function that models the temperature of a cooling body by adding a constant function to a decaying exponential, and relate these functions to the model.)

6A52DEFB306C4E41B9F0C72126C2DD19.description: Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context.

5EB1EBD9CA7149C7BB848CC15736A951.description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.
comments: Instructional Note: Limit to linear and exponential functions.

83E210EBD3CD431FB421050868D12065.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

CBC9AC3219814C388ADBCCF966B862A9.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). (e.g., Given a graph of one quadratic function and an algebraic expression for another, say which has the larger maximum.)
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on linear and exponential functions. Include comparisons of two functions presented algebraically. For example, compare the growth of two linear functions, or two exponential functions such as y = 3<sup>n</sup> and y = 100<sup>2n</sup>)

7040ABC5537C4C4CAF2ED7675EF1E9FC.description: Graph exponential and logarithmic functions, showing intercepts and end behavior and trigonometric functions, showing period, midline and amplitude.

AF17D4B912304CAD928F910D3DF0BD05.description: Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima.

C24938CE5B864CC6AE8F00445604B21E.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on linear and exponential functions. Include comparisons of two functions presented algebraically. For example, compare the growth of two linear functions, or two exponential functions such as y = 3<sup>n</sup> and y = 100<sup>2n</sup>)

78FD06C12D4F47E2A8749AAC628DDE83.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on linear functions and exponential functions whose domain is a subset of the integers. The Unit on Quadratic Functions and Modeling in this course and the Algebra II course address other types of functions.

B88F45761F544247A8982CBC0866B6F1.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes. (e.g., If the function h(n) gives the number of person-hours it takes to assemble n engines in a factory, then the positive integers would be an appropriate domain for the function.)
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on linear and exponential functions.

21550FC951F14788A3E1F94391FDDB01.description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship. Key features include: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on linear and exponential functions.

265ABB97C60344BF8BD168195BB6D4C6.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of a context.

7A288C27B31145A29FD38EB462183257.description: Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset of the integers. (e.g., The Fibonacci sequence is defined recursively by f(0) = f(1) = 1, f(n+1) = f(n)+ f(n-1) for n ≥ 1.
comments: Instructional Note: Students should experience a variety of types of situations modeled by functions. Detailed analysis of any particular class of function at this stage is not advised. Students should apply these concepts throughout their future mathematics courses. Draw examples from linear functions and exponential functions having integral domains. Draw connection to M.A1HS.27, which requires students to write arithmetic and geometric sequences. Emphasize arithmetic and geometric sequences as examples of linear and exponential functions.

ED933F85F4FF4C06A8BBC76F6EB15D35.description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.
comments: Instructional Note: Students should experience a variety of types of situations modeled by functions. Detailed analysis of any particular class of function at this stage is not advised. Students should apply these concepts throughout their future mathematics courses. Draw examples from linear functions and exponential functions having integral domains.

0E04D4D8F0B949F9A6F6772183514CC2.description: Recognize that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If f is a function and x is an element of its domain, then f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input x. The graph of f is the graph of the equation y = f(x).
comments: Instructional Note: Students should experience a variety of types of situations modeled by functions. Detailed analysis of any particular class of function at this stage is not advised. Students should apply these concepts throughout their future mathematics courses. Draw examples from linear functions and exponential functions having integral domains.

C1E6E3E5F76A4191A6776A53F8E71EB2.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation.

739A839858DB4F50924000F8FB765869.description: Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.

DE4E50F918B04210BD846DE4F9AB2190.description: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately (e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values or find successive approximations). Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential and logarithmic functions.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on cases where f(x) and g(x) are linear or exponential.

53E3B8BDD2234A0BA59E08EF00338714.description: Recognize that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on linear and exponential equations and be able to adapt and apply that learning to other types of equations in future courses.

66184CD2B1754059AF1528EB3B583E84.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.

D3B6240269A74F34877D81E01F598BF4.description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.
comments: Instructional Note: Build on student experiences graphing and solving systems of linear equations from middle school to focus on justification of the methods used. Include cases where the two equations describe the same line (yielding infinitely many solutions) and cases where two equations describe parallel lines (yielding no solution); connect to standards in Geometry which require students to prove the slope criteria for parallel lines.

7449C072C18F48A4957C9851EF416E40.description: Prove that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.

3D9898C2DED142E48C776A99E5E1C163.description: Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.
comments: Instructional Note: Address this standard before discussing exponential functions with continuous domains.

C3C6F2122A00412A99F057B864AE1A75.description: Explain how the definition of the meaning of rational exponents follows from extending the properties of integer exponents to those values, allowing for a notation for radicals in terms of rational exponents. (e.g., We define 5<sup>1/3</sup> to be the cube root of 5 because we want (5<sup>1/3</sup>)³ = 5(<sup>1/3</sup>)³ to hold, so (5<sup>1/3</sup>)³ must equal 5.)
comments: Instructional Note: Address this standard before discussing exponential functions with continuous domains.

7CFADEEF28E04245B830FE303A03415C.description: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents.

4985DE8A19B54B0ABF26643627A829A8.description: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.
comments: Instructional Note: Extend earlier work with solving linear equations to solving linear inequalities in one variable and to solving literal equations that are linear in the variable being solved for. Include simple exponential equations that rely only on application of the laws of exponents, such as 5<sup>x</sup> = 125 or 2<sup>x</sup> = 1 /16.

B63A7EA88C54452E9A8072C1E5F4D2D2.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

3978AD3219074ABD8B7A57CD1FFA2471.description: Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method.
comments: Instructional Note: Students should focus on and master linear equations and be able to extend and apply their reasoning to other types of equations in future courses. Students will solve exponential equations with logarithms in Algebra II.

C3544B0D7F66453C9979943ED06DA618.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.

72BD698FA8D64D5B8681FDB84A458CC8.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations. (e.g., Rearrange Ohm's law V = IR to highlight resistance R.)
comments: Instructional Note: Limit to formulas with a linear focus.

E6497095E5A742839EE319123142A35A.description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or non-viable options in a modeling context. (e.g., Represent inequalities describing nutritional and cost constraints on combinations of different foods.)
comments: Instructional Note: Limit to linear equations and inequalities.

DDFB32EAB3A14BA9A83EAB6C72A6778C.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.
comments: Instructional Note: Limit to linear and exponential equations, and, in the case of exponential equations, limit to situations requiring evaluation of exponential functions at integer inputs.

2754367975D64D7EB23C71995C05D4AC.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.
comments: Instructional Note: Limit to linear and exponential equations, and, in the case of exponential equations, limit to situations requiring evaluation of exponential functions at integer inputs.

755B13D2321540BE920ECD2862BF7824.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

D930972C57854FF6A0E7ACF585AAEBB0.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity. (e.g., Interpret P(1 + r)<sup>n</sup> as the product of P and a factor not depending on P.
comments: Instructional Note: Limit to linear expressions and to exponential expressions with integer exponents.

711F1D1A4604410788104623493D6D83.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

AB3065BD8FC04D3CAFABA3857AE674B8.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

91BC229D2B9F4E14ADA9D1CC159BA20A.description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

959A566B33CB47FB98CA2D7DA95709C9.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.
comments: Instructional Note: Working with quantities and the relationships between them provides grounding for work with expressions, equations, and functions.

C5B79813572040DA8021E17326D8B957.description: Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems; choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

9D20C517D2E84BB69905220EBCB279FA.description: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.

2E753BC7C1C941FE852DEECA40844FDB.description: Relationships between Quantities and Reasoning with Equations

B358AEA9776A44898F4B627DF7B4BBCF.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

5E4473BC0716446081327D4BDCA28970.description: Look for and make use of structure.

909A79D941CF46D2A5016B8E1F35DF7F.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

720F4AAB4BD445BF9B24B18CF1ABA2D9.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for English Language Arts

9B38BD3BD88440E88876D532B9938CBC.description: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading, being read to, and responding to texts; use adjectives and adverbs to describe (e.g., when other kids are happy, that makes me happy).

1F4D61670B754363837F9660FFB205FD.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among closely related verbs (e.g., toss, throw, and hurl) and closely related adjectives (e.g., thin, slender, skinny, and scrawny).

A40F80E7313D4685B847456908F36081.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe foods that are spicy or juicy).

CF6C671CFC0F4DFA911061649D29E82F.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

1D250DE1887C4DB189C113BF89FE50E7.description: Use glossaries and beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the meaning of words and phrases.

34464235590D40B9B1F0858CEA894260.description: Use knowledge of the meaning of individual words to predict the meaning of compound words (e.g., birdhouse, lighthouse, housefly; bookshelf, notebook, and bookmark).

0DA8F661B078401AA8AFFCE2028EF0DF.description: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., addition and additional).

10F9FA7F7CDF4B93A6512132F58629F5.description: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known prefix is added to a known word (e.g., happy/unhappy, and tell/retell).

1C8704CF5D8E423A98CB2CFBD3411A8D.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

4AD84E502BBC4F85A9092F917CC817FF.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 2 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.

9039FEFAF4C1445F8E9237FDD7AD61AB.description: Compare formal and informal uses of English.

3D8DB1B94A9842328DC98D0F706748EC.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

8385CA82BC4849239D82228131210545.description: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spellings.

70F9FEA8240D40758D2056EB2E76611B.description: Generalize learned spelling patterns when writing words (e.g., cage/badge; boy/boil).

1CCCB16EA59E4681B50A8B9A17D6FDF6.description: Use an apostrophe to form contractions and frequently occurring possessives.

A3175A5B56AD498699D9874D21937F33.description: Use commas in greetings and closings of letters.

A0A52ED38071438592166578248ECF19.description: Capitalize holidays, product names, and geographic names.

8CA6DDF7524F41B4A3616CB92D85DE57.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

38B6590123574DB88ACB3C2073EAFF42.description: Produce, expand, and rearrange complete simple and compound sentences (e.g., the boy watched the movies; the little boy watched the movie; the action movie was watched by the little boy).

42F1AFB14B8D4C28B9B3A0842235C65B.description: Use adjectives and adverbs and choose between them depending on what is to be modified.

1EC514495A12400E9FBFEB226362D0AA.description: Form and use the past tense of frequently occurring irregular verbs (e.g., sat, hid, or told).

0C74661A0A5E4405A109C35EA22ED171.description: Use reflexive pronouns (e.g., myself or ourselves).

5FDA87BDDBBA480A9F0358D69D2F5113.description: Form and use frequently occurring irregular plural nouns (e.g., feet, children, teeth, mice, and fish).

55D732CA24714524B42B12227A58CDC5.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

9F2DDC140B044D7FA71170DE7AA63617.description: Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.

07AC0E13178B4E1B9842FAAF77CE6202.description: Create audio recordings of stories or poems; add drawings or other visual displays to stories or recounts of experiences when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.

E9955A3F567043418371F633701A047C.description: Tell a story or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details; speaking audibly and coherently.

ED69EC852AF447169358C7B43B95CBF1.description: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to clarify comprehension, gather additional information, or deepen understanding of a topic or issue.

0AEDA75CB08545468B45B572121CADCD.description: Recount or describe key ideas or details from a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.

4397EE0161FA471CBF2F740C39EF9D14.description: Ask for clarification and further explanation as needed about the topics and texts under discussion.

B83D6B1733D740C8BE57BEBF5E585D83.description: Build on others' talk in conversations by linking comments to the remarks of others.

502DC4D5FCE14D85A4B529340E8970C6.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to others with care, and speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).

759D47BC48FB4075823DCE8D907871C1.description: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about grade 2 topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.

5E6A620354E64007A6A657D20522C47D.description: Recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.

10CF7A3519D04967A03C3AD9C379FEBE.description: produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization and style are appropriate to task, purpose and audience.

A48C08B15DD14E5A8F33A4EB0D02FCCC.description: Writing - Production and Distribution of Writing

4CCF0F11C3014D17979379BD46EE62BA.description:
write informative/explanatory texts, including the narration of historical events, scientific procedures/experiments or technical processes:
  • introduce a topic clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts and information into broader categories as appropriate to achieving purpose; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts and tables) and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.
  • develop the topic with relevant, well-chosen facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.
  • use appropriate and varied transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.
  • use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.
  • establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone.
  • provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented.

F823DEB9CE124F04B9CA61376F1B4C3A.description:
write arguments focused on discipline-specific content:
  • introduce claim(s) about a topic or issue, acknowledge and distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims and organize the reasons and evidence logically.
  • support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant, accurate data and evidence that demonstrate an understanding of the topic or text, using credible sources.
  • use words, phrases and clauses to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among claim(s), counterclaims, reasons and evidence.
  • establish and maintain a formal style.
  • provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

1028568C2C0B4C7EABBA74570BD3764A.description: by the end of grade 8, read and comprehend science/technical texts in the grades 6–8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

65982FDE303C4211BFCD8C99361C0214.description: gather and synthesize information that sensory receptors respond to stimuli by sending messages to the brain for immediate behavior or storage as memories.

9D94A508AB7643689B3187DE3751A809.description: use argument supported by evidence for how the body is a system of interacting subsystems composed of groups of cells.

170599436EF44342B764AC8318E94946.description: conduct an investigation to provide evidence that living things are made of cells, either one cell or many different numbers and types of cells.
