document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Mathematics

2C04A69E6FCE42E4BF1618D34BE84BCB.description: Design and use a simulation to generate frequencies for compound events. (e.g., Use random digits as a simulation tool to approximate the answer to the question: If 40% of donors have type A blood, what is the probability that it will take at least 4 donors to find one with type A blood?)

683935178FE24CAA84533633BAC46632.description: Represent sample spaces for compound events using methods such as organized lists, tables and tree diagrams. For an event described in everyday language (e.g., "rolling double sixes"), identify the outcomes in the sample space which compose the event.

FECDE0AFB8B5401DA191ED6762EABE5E.description: Understand that, just as with simple events, the probability of a compound event is the fraction of outcomes in the sample space for which the compound event occurs.

DB944BDF95B648F9BE2347A59B4F72BF.description: Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation.

C4DFF5FC4F7F44F0AA12405EDFBEF3C0.description: Develop a probability model (which may not be uniform) by observing frequencies in data generated from a chance process. (e.g., Find the approximate probability that a spinning penny will land heads up or that a tossed paper cup will land open-end down. Do the outcomes for the spinning penny appear to be equally likely based on the observed frequencies?)

859C78140AA34F69AB5ED8B83302A149.description: Develop a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events. (e.g., If a student is selected at random from a class, find the probability that Jane will be selected and the probability that a girl will be selected.)

5C4D369FBA154F829C395C4B18FE76A2.description: Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of events. Compare probabilities from a model to observed frequencies; if the agreement is not good, explain possible sources of the discrepancy.

1BEC9B88766945EB993724CCA6C1ED3C.description: Approximate the probability of a chance event by collecting data on the chance process that produces it and observing its long-run relative frequency, and predict the approximate relative frequency given the probability. (e.g., When rolling a number cube 600 times, predict that a 3 or 6 would be rolled roughly 200 times, but probably not exactly 200 times.)

6861EADC18AD4D1A903E10A2B6316292.description: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1 that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring. Larger numbers indicate greater likelihood. A probability near 0 indicates an unlikely event, a probability around ½ indicates an event that is neither unlikely nor likely and a probability near 1 indicates a likely event.

1A838A95C0474FEFB764D9E453A3B2E8.description: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models.

F9411C18536944B59D6795EDB1DE256A.description: Use measures of center and measures of variability for numerical data from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences about two populations. (e.g., Decide whether the words in a chapter of a seventh-grade science book are generally longer than the words in a chapter of a fourth-grade science book.)

74B4104F04384137B5BB73AF6020C666.description: Informally assess the degree of visual overlap of two numerical data distributions with similar variabilities, measuring the difference between the centers by expressing it as a multiple of a measure of variability. (e.g., The mean height of players on the basketball team is 10 cm greater than the mean height of players on the soccer team, about twice the variability (mean absolute deviation) on either team; on a dot plot, the separation between the two distributions of heights is noticeable.)

69ECABC16F364E1A98B2627D2A2235FC.description: Giving quantitative measures of center (median and/or mean) and variability (interquartile range and/or mean absolute deviation), as well as describing any overall pattern and any striking deviations from the overall pattern with reference to the context in which the data were gathered. Relating the choice of measures of center and variability to the shape of the data distribution and the context in which the data were gathered.

DC234E54DE0140A28478B2B869B340AC.description: Describing the nature of the attribute under investigation, including how it was measured and its units of measurement.

EE2C58AD2D4D499686F84D5CB0BD976F.description: Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context, such as by:

E170FE7646E342C9A68AE9331F1826E6.description: Recognize that a measure of center for a numerical data set summarizes all of its values with a single number, while a measure of variation describes how its values vary with a single number.

60FF1D0BF17C4D04B407C042DA79039F.description: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

1A64BEDE8ECE423EA2379C665D518F21.description: Use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest. Generate multiple samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation in estimates or predictions. (e.g., Estimate the mean word length in a book by randomly sampling words from the book; predict the winner of a school election based on randomly sampled survey data. Gauge how far off the estimate or prediction might be.)

B7FBB8B9484A4D619969439364FB3359.description: Understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by examining a sample of the population; generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative of that population. Understand that random sampling tends to produce representative samples and support valid inferences.

A99F87A4C02C41A9B8A4C0D78DB833FD.description: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population.

5AE04E2381CF43849F5F185B262BACD8.description: Solve word problems leading to inequalities of the form px + q > r or px + q < r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Graph the solution set of the inequality and interpret it in the context of the problem. (e.g., As a salesperson, you are paid $50 per week plus $3 per sale. This week you want your pay to be at least $100. Write an inequality for the number of sales you need to make, and describe the solutions.)

0AE989E27FCF4BE5B6A6D370B758E454.description: Solve word problems leading to equations of the form px + q = r and p(x + q) = r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Solve equations of these forms fluently. Compare an algebraic solution to an arithmetic solution, identifying the sequence of the operations used in each approach. (e.g., The perimeter of a rectangle is 54 cm. Its length is 6 cm. What is its width? An arithmetic solution similar to "54 – 6 – 6 divided by 2" may be compared with the reasoning involved in solving the equation 2w – 12 = 54. An arithmetic solution similar to "54/2 – 6" may be compared with the reasoning involved in solving the equation 2(w – 6) = 54.)

9C51AE29E2A44C1C91D4CD2431B93DEC.description: Use variables to represent quantities in a real-world or mathematical problem and construct simple equations and inequalities to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.

2C2965DD5AF943FA9ADCADED2D123D6B.description: Solve multi-step real-life and mathematical problems posed with positive and negative rational numbers in any form (whole numbers, fractions, and decimals), using tools strategically. Apply properties of operations to calculate with numbers in any form; convert between forms as appropriate; and assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies. (e.g., If a woman making $25 an hour gets a 10% raise, she will make an additional 1/10 of her salary an hour, or $2.50, for a new salary of $27.50. If you want to place a towel bar 9¾ inches long in the center of a door that is 27½ inches wide, you will need to place the bar about 9 inches from each edge; this estimate can be used as a check on the exact computation.)

CCB8405FA6BB423D9E7E727BC532124A.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions and equations.

C4B52DC5115049B886B59F5E108ADEFB.description: Understand that rewriting an expression in different forms in a problem context can shed light on the problem and how the quantities in it are related. (e.g., a + 0.05a = 1.05a means that "increase by 5%" is the same as "multiply by 1.05.")

352B62F228314AF58843640FA2771EA2.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add, subtract, factor and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.

94740944B7A0422FB2088111D34783C3.description: Use properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

747BB61CE934488AB239FD62556B0653.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations with rational numbers.
comments: Instructional Note: Computations with rational numbers extend the rules for manipulating fractions to complex fractions.

94626D2D6A794EAAA04BEA386A5D6A55.description: Convert a rational number to a decimal using long division; know that the decimal form of a rational number terminates in 0s or eventually repeats.

6062FB8666364A96BE68B2E764EAA0E1.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide rational numbers.

883947A6B96F44D4896B59D13F436863.description: Understand that integers can be divided, provided that the divisor is not zero, and every quotient of integers (with non-zero divisor) is a rational number. If p and q are integers, then –(p/q) = (–p)/q = p/(–q). Interpret quotients of rational numbers by describing real world contexts.

7B218F79AD6D4D9BAA4E823048082F81.description: Understand that multiplication is extended from fractions to rational numbers by requiring that operations continue to satisfy the properties of operations, particularly the distributive property, leading to products such as (–1)(–1) = 1 and the rules for multiplying signed numbers. Interpret products of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

DEDA1868A93D46BD887F51D14DCE8F02.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division and of fractions to multiply and divide rational numbers.

298380E7ABD4401494346E6141FFD085.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract rational numbers.

C6431CBA1208441D9D1B7E3DF5D9CF54.description: Understand subtraction of rational numbers as adding the additive inverse, p – q = p + (–q). Show that the distance between two rational numbers on the number line is the absolute value of their difference and apply this principle in real-world contexts.

3A9D5763D6044845B7BD846ABACBA134.description: Understand p + q as the number located a distance jrcqjrc from p, in the positive or negative direction, depending on whether q is positive or negative. (i.e., To add "p + q" on the number line, start at "0" and move to "p" then move jrcqjrc in the positive or negative direction depending on whether "q" is positive or negative.) Show that a number and its opposite have a sum of 0 (are additive inverses). Interpret sums of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

525D19C180BF498D8429E61ECC12D66D.description: Describe situations in which opposite quantities combine to make 0. (e.g., A hydrogen atom has 0 charge because its two constituents are oppositely charged.)

CEFFCF03BA904F1ABD39A9C634224C9A.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers; represent addition and subtraction on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram.

AE5D40C05AEE438AAC8CBD1DC7A8E476.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with fractions to add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational numbers.

E50CEDFE829C4665A3DA1E93D3984033.description: Use proportional relationships to solve multistep ratio and percent problems (e.g., simple interest, tax, markups and markdowns, gratuities and commissions, fees, percent increase and decrease, and/or percent error).

BCD2B1840CB845FE8231B0322AE8EA4C.description: Explain what a point (x,y) on the graph of a proportional relationship means in terms of the situation. Focus special attention on the points (0,0) and (1,r) where r is the unit rate.

915AABE2955B4E0D96F43F0116848FEC.description: Represent proportional relationships by equations. (e.g., If total cost t is proportional to the number n of items purchased at a constant price p, the relationship between the total cost and the number of items can be expressed as t = pn.)

5629AABA96BA40FAB6C4DB17F9589720.description: Identify the constant of proportionality (unit rate) in tables, graphs, equations, diagrams and verbal descriptions of proportional relationships.

41AD3A758F4B4492A56E1594DE5AF208.description: Decide whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship (e.g., by testing for equivalent ratios in a table or graphing on a coordinate plane and observing whether the graph is a straight line through the origin).

2AE373BAD5974F40AB3A38F0291827B3.description: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.

83B33661CEB042C6BA7C1078FE880FF8.description: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas and other quantities measured in like or different units. (e.g., If a person walks ½ mile in each ¼ hour, compute the unit rate as the complex fraction ½/¼ miles per hour, equivalently 2 miles per hour.)

63695C9EA2DD467699FFA7E2D03F78B3.description: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

8C3DBFD1638E47FCBAB781BA53AA0FC0.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, volume and surface area of two- and three-dimensional objects composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, cubes, and right prisms.

0EFA6F146AE34D48B2574547D2B1A611.description: Use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles in a multi-step problem to write and solve simple equations for an unknown angle in a figure.

04DD4B5E27E1497DA6F3998FFA4898F9.description: Know the formulas for the area and circumference of a circle and use them to solve problems; give an informal derivation of the relationship between the circumference and area of a circle.

8B570627C91D4AA4BB711250A5385A2E.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume.

ADCA60AC19004AE0A0DFFFE98273F087.description: Describe the two-dimensional figures that result from slicing three-dimensional figures, as in plane sections of right rectangular prisms and right rectangular pyramids.

51593C06B465457898CF4D1C386EEE44.description: Draw (freehand, with ruler and protractor, and with technology) geometric shapes with given conditions. Focus on constructing triangles from three measures of angles or sides, noticing when the conditions determine a unique triangle, more than one triangle, or no triangle.

8C123E9358DD477BAE27FC764AAA81CA.description: Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures, including computing actual lengths and areas from a scale drawing and reproducing a scale drawing at a different scale.

1FA92C8F5D934224920D2B122951963E.description: Draw, construct and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them.

4ADDB3181B7E4993B566C1C7B95FEB3B.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

15699F6AC7D34A418694D8F0537F75B9.description: Look for and make use of structure.

8DFE305DEF154EBF9346AA41DDC8A8DE.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

274710CCE13C43A6B6EEF0BEE0D8CBD8.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Mathematics

BB1F13A723304A849853B867A89D11EB.description: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.

9288509D4388453C83EE2EC8C35DCC8C.description: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles as a category, and identify right triangles.

1D418F406D004C4894C2E5248FD92D69.description: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse) and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.

3E8D7C8089ED44D2BC2A7BAED6C3307F.description: Draw and identify lines and angles and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.

F49683E9EF6A47C39ED292850699C86B.description: Recognize angle measure as additive. When an angle is decomposed into non-overlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts. Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real world and mathematical problems (e.g., by using an equation with a symbol for the unknown angle measure).

2172D1D6ADC541919BE861C7B82B2DF5.description: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor and sketch angles of specified measure.

47CA9C7526EA47A79C2E82F887727829.description: An angle that turns through b one-degree angles is said to have an angle measure of b degrees.

5AD11FEA090C462F9E98E297B6A3C286.description: An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays, by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through 1/360 of a circle is called a "one-degree angle," and can be used to measure angles.

05AA59DC607C4A11A0C6DACADD8BF1A9.description: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement:

1AB310A8A2D24CA7A4B797003A0FC80C.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles.

AFA91C3C78C64408B045CA57642C2A35.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (½, ¼, 1/8). Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots (e.g., from a line plot find and interpret the difference in length between the longest and shortest specimens in an insect collection).

D074D454C535411185D109D0B8F1132B.description: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems by viewing the area formula as a multiplication equation with an unknown factor. (e.g., find the width of a rectangular room given the area of the flooring and the length.)

B598ADB828E14714AAF354A236BB51C2.description: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as number line diagrams that feature a measurement scale.

4B68DF3E873043D4A2962F588C843FDD.description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within a system of units, including the metric system (km, m, cm; kg, g; l, ml), the standard system (lb, oz), and time (hr, min, sec.). Within a single system of measurement, express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Record measurement equivalents in a two-column table. (e.g., Know that 1 ft is 12 times as long as 1 in. Express the length of a 4 ft snake as 48 in. Generate a conversion table for feet and inches listing the number pairs (1, 12), (2, 24), (3, 36), …)

FA7BE98CBA834EB08A9AD2FE5A1C04A3.description: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit.

64EA2D1FD22043DAB81F89DEA74F556A.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, = or <, and justify the conclusions by using a visual model.

365A78B743A944FEA3F54B5CAF623B2D.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100 (e.g., rewrite 0.62 as 62/100; describe a length as 0.62 meters; locate 0.62 on a number line diagram).

EA5EA079D33C4CB18369059C9E0F3DB9.description: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators 10 and 100 (e.g., express 3/10 as 30/100, and add 3/10 + 4/100 = 34/100).
comments: Instructional Note: Students who can generate equivalent fractions can develop strategies for adding fractions with unlike denominators in general. But addition and subtraction with unlike denominators in general is not a requirement at this grade.

97FF442DA38942A990506761F1A8F1D7.description: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.

619BD45877F541FFA5C82A8EF946333D.description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem (e.g., If each person at a party will eat 3/8 of a pound of roast beef, and there will be 5 people at the party, how many pounds of roast beef will be needed? Between what two whole numbers does your answer lie?).

7558D1377535487C92ED070A95D0A94D.description: Understand a multiple of a/b as a multiple of 1/b, and use this understanding to multiply a fraction by a whole number (e.g., use a visual fraction model to express 3 × (2/5) as 6 × (1/5), recognizing this product as 6/5. In general, n × (a/b) = (n × a)/b).

5F50130C475C4740B3DE7471548EC50D.description: Understand a fraction a/b as a multiple of 1/b, (e.g., use a visual fraction model to represent 5/4 as the product 5 × (¼), recording the conclusion by the equation 5/4 = 5 × (¼)).

9ED6B96C2EFB4357A9B5C936EF11B410.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

CF2FB36D67FA44D094B741612F3BED25.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

67EB56F968984F5C809FA6FF0874BB2C.description: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

6CE2551C55C84AF8AFE6F9FBFFBF2A20.description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation and justify decompositions by using a visual fraction model (e.g., 3/8 = 1/8 + 1/8 + 1/8; 3/8 = 1/8 + 2/8; 2 1/8 = 1 + 1 + 1/8 = 8/8 + 8/8 + 1/8).

18EB7EDDCB0D402D95D92A51B09B1BC4.description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.

AEE1CC69FE6A4CF38215FBFAABF13AD7.description: Understand the fraction a/b, with a > 1, as the sum of a of the fractions 1/b.

0AD7B3EDFFDC4CFCA2DBEC3338FC3B9C.description: Build fractions from unit fractions by applying and extending previous understandings of operations on whole numbers.

B1C523E7C12646AAACA179F7DA7F02B4.description: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators (e.g., by creating common denominators or numerators, or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as ½). Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with symbols >, = or <, and justify the conclusions by using a visual fraction model.

622C2DEEDDB14C7188B58745980B8FFC.description: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction (n × a)/(n × b) by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.

C37C9B8F779045F3A6C95D9E2C96338F.description: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering.

2563FF35392642C19867703F548E7255.description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays and/or area models.

CF43DD6954EB44FF92F6412B1369355B.description: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations and illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays and/or area models.

9ED394D2A7AA4549BD23995E13A4DD05.description: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

333C666908E84E96BCF0196C9A43F8D9.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

5AC4396335174087B5E14D65E56639F9.description: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.

249732731B15435E9B6F6C57756EE9FD.description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, = and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

1A0C62A9F8A2406789270F1D432056A3.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right (e.g., recognize that 700 ÷ 70 = 10 by applying concepts of place value and division).

9307F1EF3FDD4110856598EB6CF55038.description: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.

4591A704876741BF911C37502AF3B8A8.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

0D494E3DA2B344109C990D1FD93E78F6.description: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself. (e.g., Given the rule "Add 3" and the starting number 1, generate terms in the resulting sequence and observe that the terms appear to alternate between odd and even numbers. Explain informally why the numbers will continue to alternate in this way.)

A308640F514B4716BEE04793E1DCBFB5.description: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1–100, recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1–100 is a multiple of a given one-digit number. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1–100 is prime or composite.

70B38AA666AD4E4FB5D2A691B19B22C4.description: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.

51436F336B77494DBB30D4696B9B5E7A.description: Solve multi-step word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

986D7C53B3DC40F38376EDD2529A0132.description: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison (e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem) and distinguish multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.

2C09B76F81B04B0DA4B68BDBDBA1FA5F.description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison (e.g., interpret 35 = 5 × 7 as a statement that 35 is 5 times as many as 7 and 7 times as many as 5). Represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.

BAE030AA9F13433488821BAF82BDC917.description: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

A14BD973C27548F49FA8021B7077A590.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

F0AEBEF22716410FB95E6D7A837F8A56.description: Look for and make use of structure.

5AF048388FFE4CD58BAB2809B8B966A7.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

6D9E654758E448279FE83F1511036A04.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for English Language Arts

14AE9D16106E4ADA9738D738D57E224D.description: Acquire and accurately use grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal precise actions, emotions, or states of being (e.g., quizzed, whined, and stammered) and that are basic to a particular topic (e.g., wildlife, conservation, and endangered when discussing animal preservation).

BE96016A72C44EE189D936387EC095C1.description: Demonstrate understanding of words by relating them to their opposites (antonyms) and to words with similar but not identical meanings (synonyms).

39F72387EFC1498B938C64CAF2E25912.description: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

1D18351F408C4F65A611F83B6AF25D7A.description: Explain the meaning of simple similes and metaphors (e.g., as pretty as a picture) in context.

D1F1B95C04314B17B85F27D53B130CE5.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

D736D066DF9A45C09AF173AA653C926C.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, and/or thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

3C691A744A64453492F57606187E2FA0.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., telegraph, photograph, and autograph).

7C9A2B92BC3F4175A23545F63F9887BF.description: Use context (e.g., definitions, examples, or restatements in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

8ACC5EBFA4D34AD48BB4E88D716F9846.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 4 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

BA193B9EAAFF466AB5B424DD70F346F7.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion).

0C7590EB416F440FAF996390BE847B6C.description: Choose words and phrases to convey ideas precisely.

A9016938BA644BCDAB1B695AEE72F785.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

274A96D2B6784922B738D5D55B25BA71.description: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.

94647BC15CFE4EEEB0EA9DDDF8F6DF3B.description: Use a comma before a coordinating conjunction in a compound sentence.

C18FF8B00472404A9C3D67EEC9DC0E4B.description: Use commas and quotation marks to mark direct speech and quotations from a text.

5B69ECD84EF64E008699DE36134744C7.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

D9247833F3DA47DAB0B52234239DFE26.description: Correctly use frequently confused words (e.g., to, too, and two; there and their).

F10020A89CDD4B348A2B1903DA9F14B0.description: Produce complete sentences, recognizing and correcting inappropriate fragments and run-ons.

EA363238583B48EAAC93ACDCAA23163A.description: Order adjectives within sentences according to conventional patterns (e.g., a small red bag rather than a red small bag).

9A07AD4D782D4ECEA871371998BDCCE2.description: Use modal auxiliaries (e.g., can, may, or must) to convey various conditions.

0FDEACC99A824E6DA5FF2F900D3C9164.description: Form and use the progressive (e.g., I was walking; I am walking; I will be walking) verb tenses.

5D0FDC75B4564798B46188E74D09F62C.description: Use relative pronouns (who, whose, whom, which, or that) and relative adverbs (where, when, or why).

0EADA5DB8BB04E419244319DD6E83658.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

7B7CDB64ADE044BF8301256EEB0C3ECA.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion); use formal English when appropriate to task and situation. (See grade 4 Language standards for specific expectations.)

97CF4B5FEC254E2A9E5193831BE04FB8.description: Add audio recordings and visual displays to presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.

C91B1CF8A0664F38800F36F265F2F59B.description: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience in an organized manner, using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly at an understandable pace.

ACC51190204542E38C4484D40440B1E3.description: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker provides to support particular points.

4582400D272943E78A55C656C2BA8304.description: Paraphrase portions of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

5C2C2D0DBEA24620A9D8F3669F2A344F.description: Review the key ideas expressed and explain ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.

7C29A8FB7C8141B0998AFA79D08EF8F7.description: Pose and respond to specific questions to clarify or follow up on information and make comments that contribute to the discussion and link to the remarks of others.

AF822AC5316C4202BF1C47599A16C9EC.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.

7D6D0490B5024BC3B79FA84552F4C88D.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

324295210C0F48A9B682CFF7B0AE10AB.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 4 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing ideas clearly.

07FA261B4B9C47849FD78F2CE1286DE0.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

15E27D2573484D21A052CB17ECE450A7.description: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to informational texts (e.g., "explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text.").

2A09BD6D7ED74889A816302DAE223D11.description: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "describe in depth a character, setting or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text [e.g., a character's thoughts, words, or actions].").

3D4C9B353759416696D37E25F7535CEC.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

F3E33BACE80E41FB8D56FCA8351BB09E.description: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital sources; take notes and categorize information and provide a list of sources.

4DE992A6D7F54BB18CC1A136EFEBC558.description: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.

9EE898FD74774A21AC4D77D7709BD284.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

DED2878CDEB740E294378DA5A8575758.description: With some guidance and support from adults, use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills.

1CEFBEDA029C4519A2C604E4C223EA15.description: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing. (Editing for conventions should demonstrate command of Language standards up to and including grade 4.)

E1223184FFB449FA904B77660ABBD82E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in Text Types and Purposes.)

9666EBD812534D72B39D73E212370C84.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.

9B4E34F7CE614CC38D6BB143F4C51484.description: Use concrete words and phrases and sensory details to convey experiences and events precisely.

0525A12C29C84E73BAE649FFF5AA4672.description: Use a variety of transitional words and phrases to manage the sequence of events.

4CC8EDFB5F524FEEBC69886F2B12F85E.description: Use dialogue and description to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.

00182537814B47F6BB56B67916E67691.description: Orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.

976F4DE2A103417AACAC7B17F79358E2.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.

9543085A70CA4781B878E7B99F7E0808.description: Introduce a topic clearly and group related information in paragraphs and sections; include formatting (e.g., headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

42499A9AA20B47178A0DB34ACF30A34D.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.

0BD09E228E0D4A97A66B777A75CC26D8.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the opinion presented.

BE63378D29DC4DFD93F11F08D48CCB9B.description: Provide reasons that are supported by facts and details.

D39EBFE934D34EAD8528B24323D469B4.description: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which related ideas are grouped to support the writer's purpose.

F1B8C1873D61412084D27C057464704B.description: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons and information.

72562C79D3BF485DB3215B1E864E7B96.description: Describe the overall structure (e.g., chronology, comparison, cause/effect, or problem/solution) of events, ideas, concepts, or information in all or part of an informational text.

9EBD795F34374E1C86784163954AAC0B.description: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words or phrases in an informational text relevant to a grade 4 topic or subject area.

CD3F01CAE8BD411DACEA7ABA68AE93D9.description: Compare and contrast the point of view from which different literary texts are narrated, including the difference between first- and third-person narrations.

870440831B5046A5B16BB1457A62BA1E.description: Explain major differences between poems, drama, and prose; refer to the structural elements of poems (e.g., verse, rhythm, and meter) and drama (e.g., casts of characters, settings, descriptions, dialogue, and stage directions) when writing or speaking about a literary text.

730C065240FD45F6902984254F3ABFAC.description: Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the literary text (e.g., a character's thoughts, words, or actions).

8C3619BCDDEF4FA0B650913C180C0645.description: Refer to details and examples in a literary text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

10B5ABFCA8624312AC8569266C0916C9.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

E75D6C53405B4FECBAF41544458800DA.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for English Language Arts

899C9FCE004A453B889AE0A6B4407C0C.description: With guidance and support from adults, demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

FF25D9AB236A41AC800429920AD020FC.description: Identify frequently occurring root words (e.g., look) and their inflectional forms (e.g., looks, looked, and looking).

62C2AE7AE3CA44AC86F3E5AA4FFC11A7.description: Use frequently occurring affixes as a clue to the meaning of a word.

F3F3DB150CE64AD7AF3DE1719C196597.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

A5FBF05673714F69AE0C558C75C8FD04.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 1 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.

B856684AC3374607AD986D7576CAE6AA.description: Use conventional spelling for words with common spelling patterns and for frequently occurring irregular words. Spell untaught words phonetically, drawing on phonemic awareness and spelling conventions.

347025A846174F10B39445D42C4A5272.description: Use commas in dates and to separate single words in a series.

554A1E1D139144B689DA2DC85524EDA8.description: Capitalize dates and names of people.

B22DB7E255EE473A8F7DB9C2FD6CE532.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

09B4541BA57B4F049E0ADDE13EBD2033.description: Produce and expand complete simple and compound declarative, interrogative, imperative, and exclamatory sentences in response to prompts.

B9C66285B2734813A93CA1A4D26AB032.description: Use frequently occurring prepositions (e.g., during, beyond, or toward).

7C42B056993F455DB055DA23D96ECEA5.description: Use frequently occurring conjunctions (e.g. and, but, or, so, or because).

273D63ECB39443ACBA09185E60E27C6D.description: Use verbs to convey a sense of past, present, and future (e.g., yesterday I walked home; today I walk home; tomorrow I will walk home).

808891A8E259448EAB63EBFC759B2863.description: Use common, proper, and possessive nouns.

6F1075B604DC4A04929CFBD0396038BD.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

87AF8A7669534DC89A29E9909BA9FD0A.description: Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation.

4BB05BBF5ED443DDB281C67BE22C7BAA.description: Describe people, places, things, and events with relevant details, expressing ideas and feelings clearly.

A0FD7551639F480B92D7BFFF1D02309B.description: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to gather additional information or clarify something that is not understood.

DA7B86565B6A420BA2954AE7BE2F65D4.description: Ask questions to clear up any confusion about the topics and texts under discussion.

1AE02A6A483C4A199E93390097155E48.description: Build on others' talk in conversations by responding to the comments of others through multiple exchanges.

409C0DD4C9104A0E96C98D3540C62B5C.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., listening to others with care and speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).

7EDB2928233948DC9C47448230D13656.description: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about grade 1 topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.

CA1A6353AA4E46228B511F28A446E189.description: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.

0743E0251F0F4A03B7BA9893DCE202F8.description: Participate in shared research and writing (e.g., explore a number of "how-to" books on a given topic and use them to write a sequence of instructions).

17A699B77DB24E26B42181DB2E77FCDE.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

0EA2F695008842DB9482342923E4B22D.description: With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including collaboration with peers.

6BF82B182EBB4AFAB257CFAEC377D02E.description: With guidance and support from adults and collaborative discussions, focus on a topic and add details to strengthen writing as needed.

0CA4228D59F347AFA142F237272B55E6.description: Write narratives to recount two or more appropriately sequenced events, include some details regarding what happened, use transitional words to signal event order, and provide some sense of closure.

06CCB5E846504DC3B85E0E81CA6671BC.description: Write informative/explanatory texts by naming a topic, supplying some facts about the topic, and providing some sense of closure.

B2902B27CBD444F1BA35BB8C6BD3E03C.description: Write opinion pieces by introducing the topic or name of the text being discussed, stating an opinion, supplying a reason for the opinion, and providing some sense of closure.

1A2AF6C04FF1450980628E949A347A54.description: With prompting and support, read informational texts appropriately complex for grade 1.

424FA567D5624DBAA15CABEA5412BC90.description: With prompting and support, read prose and poetry of appropriate complexity for grade 1 in literary texts.

03E2ABBF35804B9088EB23139998B7FB.description: Range of Reading and Text Complexity

9D372558CEC143759FCB137D8156D878.description: Identify basic similarities in and differences between two informational texts on the same topic (e.g., in illustrations, descriptions, or procedures).

21260ABF4EFB4CB19A3199667A19C52E.description: Identify the reasons an author gives to support points in an informational text.

B435987566484337BF84D640C2B88CE5.description: Use the illustrations and details in a text to describe its key ideas in informational texts.

6BC5447A635647BF8702608FDB1312E2.description: Compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in stories in literary texts.

F3BE6703C2B44EA2B625D14A65A562CC.description: Use illustrations and details in a story to describe its characters, setting, or events in literary texts.

BA6276E75B874764A40F0DD963614841.description: Distinguish between information provided by pictures or other illustrations and information provided by the words in an informational text.

BF55099403704576ABFA3AE02395F4BF.description: Know and use various text features (e.g., headings, tables of contents, glossaries, electronic menus, and/or icons) to locate key facts or information in an informational text.

3F286CCDDC80486795EC48F6ED57C209.description: Ask and answer questions to help determine or clarify the meaning of words and phrases in an informational text.

91C3B35837984C858DFED1EDE13C180C.description: Identify who is telling the story at various points in a literary text.

420B326901894AA6991ABCB2FC20EE18.description: Explain major differences between books that tell stories and books that give information, drawing on a wide reading of a range of literary text types.

DC306FFDF6C446108FC08EE3F861732A.description: In literary texts, identify words and phrases in stories or poems that suggest feelings or appeal to the senses.

BF0549C116FD4D2883DC9A9AD2F15F46.description: Describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in an informational text.

070CBDD072C1411BACE481307F0975FC.description: Identify the main topic and retell key details of an informational text.

6CB3CD4170214676831CC071210CA079.description: Ask and answer questions about key details in an informational text.

EE62CC9271BE43E881A617E21843B4FB.description: Describe characters, settings, and major events in a story, using key details in literary texts.

4931125924174B1CAA6C91B6B91FCAE5.description: Retell stories, including key details, and demonstrate understanding of their central message or lesson in literary texts.

7B370E6E9BAC499C985777AB3EB3A30A.description: Ask and answer questions about key details in a literary text.

02234DE1F4DF446CB615A5A4A5D38F3E.description: Recognize the distinguishing features of a sentence (e.g., first word, capitalization, and ending punctuation).

72972E591E3D4582AE72C88364BF985C.description: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.

A14DF0E2276C469F84020A17726BB1C1.description: Segment spoken single-syllable words into their complete sequence of individual sounds (phonemes).

40B677118ED2437A848D32EC7B2BE169.description: Isolate and pronounce initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes) in spoken single-syllable words.

84C3874D93614A27A96C0D40E4DAB972.description: Orally produce single-syllable words by blending sounds (phonemes), including consonant blends.

78C903FD3DFC4F6DA2521ADA39A0816F.description: Distinguish long from short vowel sounds in spoken single-syllable words.

5A62FB6B7A164F9C924F84A1995AD400.description: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).

100B224F5BED419E8526A7FCE406F9AB.description: Print all upper- and lowercase letters using proper letter formation and directionality.

8D37B54BD3324F1699B843796A4FAC3A.description: Recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.

4769808BD7024C2EA7A6D0C75BF55522.description: Use knowledge that every syllable must have a vowel sound to determine the number of syllables in a printed word.

235AA23135374CFBA3975B5AA2BA3D52.description: Know final -e and common vowel team conventions for representing long vowel sounds.
