document.title: Library Media Content Standards and Objectives for West Virginia Schools

FC65869B0400471E94C285A594845C0F.description: share information and ideas with others through individual responsibilities and work groups.

D56838CABE5746DF87D75B95694B7FB4.description: develop positive attitudes toward the social and ethical responsibilities (e.g., differentiating between copying and retelling in their own words).

76A09FF2468B4FC795DC7DEF3A435B53.description: recognize ethical policies in the use of information (e.g. Internet use and copyright issues).

5CDBB01C4F804552BE4BDE11C811FAF0.description: discuss situations or conditions where information is controlled or limited.

1CFACAFED1DC459581244AF944D34D80.description:
Students will develop social responsibility and contribute positively to the learning community and society by
  • being information literate and recognizing the importance of information to a democratic society;
  • practicing ethical behavior in regard to information and information technology;
  • participating effectively in groups to pursue and generate information.

16F793DEF4CC4D43A9CF0C7823F6211F.description: choose and read a variety of literature including award-winning selections (e.g. Caldecott Award).

69F2AD7FC08F492F8C3974BA97970B20.description: recognize author's purpose for writing stories (e.g. entertainment, information).

14483FD55EF540B29A76AE514996B41B.description: classify a variety of classic and contemporary literature from different genres (e.g. folklore, fairy tales, tall tales, legends, poetry, fiction, and nonfiction).

68D3847188144EB2BBC7FCC81FF0E154.description: state why an author or topic is of personal interest.

4951CA1705A54332892321396A87C4E0.description: apply story elements (e.g. setting, plot, characters and theme), make simple predictions and interpret meaning from literature and how it relates to his/her experience.

91CB90F9753A4AB6986315BDFB6060DD.description: demonstrate good library citizenship including rules of behavior and proper use and treatment of print materials and electronic resources.

26C7D2EAAE374501B6DD768B42A8C19B.description: recognize the automated or print catalog and its use to locate books.

FDD5AC8E35984AC38AF2291573295CCF.description: find appropriate fiction and nonfiction materials.

63073234E25245388C17BAC47C42574F.description: discuss the school library media center (LMC) arrangement and procedures.

80C9DD08F26C46988ACF9137524C460C.description:
Students will become independent learners by
  • being information literate and pursuing information related to personal interests;
  • appreciating literature and other creative expressions of information;
  • striving for excellence in information seeking and knowledge generation.

7FDDD37D69B14F2280E363EA609EC08E.description: alphabetize to the second letter and use simple guide words in a dictionary.

E0A453A1C89E4556B7A11C53E7D82AA4.description: identify and use print, non-print and electronic resources (e.g. books, newspapers, magazines, dictionaries, encyclopedias, CD-ROMs and the Internet).

8CDAB05D6BB043129172D570A7F7EC3E.description: identify and use parts of book (e.g. title page, table of contents, glossary, and index).

E2F2964063594DBFAE9D1BF7E2912081.description:
Students will become information literate by
  • accessing information efficiently and effectively;
  • evaluating information critically and competently;
  • using information accurately and creatively.

document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Mathematics

2D379959EF91452F8DD66776C1DE3CB7.description: Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on properties.

B4435BBB16B443009CFD8A77764BFC65.description: Understand that attributes belonging to a category of two dimensional figures also belong to all subcategories of that category (e.g., all rectangles have four right angles and squares are rectangles, so all squares have four right angles).

9FB4501B33FD4954A9D3BBDA790DCA10.description: Classify two-dimensional figures into categories based on their properties.

440C5CDB2E044F35A0579CDAD300FFA1.description: Represent real-world mathematical problems by graphing points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane and interpret coordinate values of points in the context of the situation.

EE76DE32EE9448C7B3654FB11A950A2D.description: Use a pair of perpendicular number lines, called axes, to define a coordinate system, with the intersection of the lines, the origin, arranged to coincide with the 0 on each line and a given point in the plane located by using an ordered pair of numbers, called its coordinates. Understand that the first number indicates how far to travel from the origin in the direction of one axis and the second number indicates how far to travel in the direction of the second axis, with the convention that the names of the two axes and the coordinates correspond (e.g., x-axis and x-coordinate, y-axis and y-coordinate).

451BE99F1654479BBE8BBA758389247D.description: Graph points on the coordinate plane to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

4D07B2E1503B40599CA0168C12677C02.description: Recognize volume as additive and find volumes of solid figures composed of two non-overlapping right rectangular prisms by adding the volumes of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real-world problems.

98F75470F1BC4C33ADDDDBCF846562EF.description: Apply the formulas V = l × w × h and V = b × h for rectangular prisms to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with whole number edge lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

8C68AE83C624456D817F68C70C293714.description: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with whole-number side lengths by packing it with unit cubes and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths, equivalently by multiplying the height by the area of the base. Represent threefold whole-number products as volumes (e.g., to represent the associative property of multiplication).

D443A07102E2408C85D9D853430FBEC1.description: Relate volume to the operations of multiplication and addition and solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume.

14E47E1096BB4ACF9E0FDAECE03EE883.description: Measure volumes by counting unit cubes, using cubic cm, cubic in, cubic ft, and improvised units.

6DDFE0E4A24949CFBFB28F4D0096224C.description: A solid figure which can be packed without gaps or overlaps using b unit cubes is said to have a volume of b cubic units.

5B7E531548764241AA77192C2FA91F6A.description: A cube with side length 1 unit, called a "unit cube," is said to have "one cubic unit" of volume and can be used to measure volume.

6BE772D9872B4904969B1BAD5FB0EE0F.description: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures and understand concepts of volume measurement.

85F76A63B5DA42838DA388F08655C73E.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition.

25F3BCB11174420FB62ADF99528C0C87.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (½, ¼, 1/8). Use operations on fractions for this grade to solve problems involving information presented in line plots. (e.g., Given different measurements of liquid in identical beakers, find the amount of liquid each beaker would contain if the total amount in all the beakers were redistributed equally).

F517041716FE4F108FC3816C0D52917B.description: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a given measurement system (e.g., convert 5 cm to 0.05 m) and use these conversions in solving multi-step, real-world problems.

1433D10DA4FC41819847A7DF9D93EA22.description: Convert like measurement units within a given measurement system.

106E2626C623424087719CE8C80F7140.description: Solve real-world problems involving division of unit fractions by non-zero whole numbers and division of whole numbers by unit fractions by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem. (e.g., How much chocolate will each person get if 3 people share ½ lb. of chocolate equally? How many ⅓-cup servings are in 2 cups of raisins?)

049A66424CD64F0BAB90BDF457C45F7D.description: Interpret division of a whole number by a unit fraction and compute such quotients. (e.g., Create a story context for 4 ÷ (⅕) and use a visual fraction model to show the quotient. Use the relationship between multiplication and division to explain that 4 ÷ (⅕) = 20 because 20 × (⅕) = 4.)

F84C4C4ADB384E8A8C3FEDA4FFBC1922.description: Interpret division of a unit fraction by a non-zero whole number and compute such quotients. (e.g., Create a story context for (⅓) ÷ 4 and use a visual fraction model to show the quotient. Use the relationship between multiplication and division to explain that (⅓) ÷ 4 = 1/12 because (1/12) × 4 = ⅓.)

AF5D85CBDD7F4B8BBC53BB1EEF682D1E.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of division to divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions.
comments: Instructional Note: Students able to multiply fractions in general can develop strategies to divide fractions in general, by reasoning about the relationship between multiplication and division, but division of a fraction by a fraction is not a requirement at this grade.

ED94839E72124ECC82A81C6FBC91A08A.description: Solve real-world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem.

775CE3F66AC64F898FB7413245AC89C8.description: Explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction greater than 1 results in a product greater than the given number (recognizing multiplication by whole numbers greater than 1 as a familiar case); explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction less than 1 results in a product smaller than the given number; and relating the principle of fraction equivalence a/b = (n×a)/(n×b) to the effect of multiplying a/b by 1.

CC00251C0F9049FD92168F910E920035.description: Comparing the size of a product to the size of one factor on the basis of the size of the other factor, without performing the indicated multiplication.

55F58D90BC2343AE9657563D9EC14CE6.description: Find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling it with unit squares of the appropriate unit fraction side lengths and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths. Multiply fractional side lengths to find areas of rectangles and represent fraction products as rectangular areas.

F83C65F88B3243B9AE1CA03EEAAB7FFC.description: Interpret the product (a/b) × q as a parts of a partition of q into b equal parts; equivalently, as the result of a sequence of operations a × q ÷ b. (e.g., Use a visual fraction model to show (⅔) × 4 = 8/3 and create a story context for this equation. Do the same with (⅔) × (⅘) = 8/15.)
comments: Instructional Note: In general, (a/b) × (c/d) = ac/bd.

B2DACD22305A495EBF8B7B05E8A67628.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction.

51F8F3728CAF4CE6BFC1C639F8A4F7D0.description: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator (a/b = a ÷ b). Solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions or mixed numbers by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem. (e.g., Interpret ¾ as the result of dividing 3 by 4, noting that ¾ multiplied by 4 equals 3 and that when 3 wholes are shared equally among 4 people each person has a share of size ¾. If 9 people want to share a 50-pound sack of rice equally by weight, how many pounds of rice should each person get? Between what two whole numbers does your answer lie?)

B29F78F5DA774431AF556F6B4858565F.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions.

F2A2322FCD544F30A626641B6E1EC7FA.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole, including cases of unlike denominators by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem. Use benchmark fractions and number sense of fractions to estimate mentally and assess the reasonableness of answers (e.g., recognize an incorrect result 2/5 + ½ = 3/7, by observing that 3/7 < ½).

BE85D13FA515430B9C62F5E16B7F80DD.description: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators, including mixed numbers, by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions in such a way as to produce an equivalent sum or difference of fractions with like denominators (e.g., ⅔ + 5/4 = 8/12 + 15/12 = 23/12).
comments: Instructional Note: In general, a/b + c/d = (ad + bc)/bd.

E9D3339C7DF34F20BF338F60FF73D482.description: Use equivalent fractions as a strategy to add and subtract fractions.

8A1521C6B4D94B558D5775E5D79AFDC0.description: Add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals to hundredths, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between related operations, relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.

BBB82981A8714DBFBEBEAD0F1F732770.description: Find whole-number quotients of whole numbers with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

7A2DA675FDE74E739E59F9C5423FD648.description: Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

1BD688A60F7F429C8313E5D2B3CCC0D8.description: Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and with decimals to hundredths.

138743442C534FFEAACFBA0961922FB6.description: Use place value understanding to round decimals to any place.

7391B7C29CF14CB5BC2465348F7DE21B.description: Compare two decimals to thousandths based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, = and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

5946F7FA73EA4DE8B642CE6C30DCDFFF.description: Read and write decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names and expanded form (e.g., 347.392 = 3 × 100 + 4 × 10 + 7 × 1 + 3 × (1/10) + 9 × (1/100) + 2 × (1/1000)).

1D5495F42A50451884A4261142D90A1E.description: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.

48E496DD45984077A4DFC1CDBE7B6247.description: Explain patterns in the number of zeros of the product when multiplying a number by powers of 10, explain patterns in the placement of the decimal point when a decimal is multiplied or divided by a power of 10. Use whole-number exponents to denote powers of 10.

AF44DC35B96F4FC6B2B76290C4995829.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right and 1/10 of what it represents in the place to its left.

1075B71876754E07905F6CFC92D5CE14.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

588047279BAD4844BE29D819BEC0FE63.description: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules. Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms. Form ordered pairs consisting of corresponding terms from the two patterns, and graph the ordered pairs on a coordinate plane. (e.g., Given the rule "Add 3" and the starting number 0 and given the rule "Add 6" and the starting number 0, generate terms in the resulting sequences and observe that the terms in one sequence are twice the corresponding terms in the other sequence. Explain informally why this is so.)

749E9A7345864FDCB5B3123CB2F8DBBF.description: Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them. (e.g., Express the calculation "add 8 and 7, then multiply by 2" as 2 × (8 + 7). Recognize that 3 × (18932 + 921) is three times as large as 18932 + 921, without having to calculate the indicated sum or product.)

242F29DF3CE34B2C9E750362FF410B01.description: Use parentheses, brackets or braces in numerical expressions and evaluate expressions with these symbols.

A8E4A1AB10054B4C892F116AD97DE682.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

ABB9BECFCF3C448BA2066860D2D715A4.description: Look for and make use of structure.

64C0126E14A34408B1F08536F71BF3EE.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

73EE8A134E284338A5D34F221583133D.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for English Language Arts

AF7A87F4C87D421CBC48AA5A9F5C2ED2.description: Acquire and accurately use grade-appropriate conversational, general academic, and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal spatial and transitional relationships (e.g., after dinner that night we went looking for them).

B34A38FB6AD043B39CFEE66BA2125C2C.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among related words that describe states of mind or degrees of certainty (e.g., knew, believed, suspected, heard, and wondered).

A23EBABA9A73467080F20E99AFDC40F3.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe people who are friendly or helpful).

DC877F0F07824E77952F364E6D9CC804.description: Distinguish the literal and nonliteral meanings of words and phrases in context (e.g., take steps).

F9D6F99F9FF74EBBAE8DF60CE7C1C302.description: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

141087A5464649AE974F4531837E5886.description: Use glossaries or beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

E22532FDB06947FEADED5613E414A933.description: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., company and companion).

9725C4A57B7C47BC989E238C21838AF9.description: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known affix is added to a known word (e.g., agreeable/disagreeable, comfortable/uncomfortable, care/careless, and heat/preheat).

44990AFA513748DEB07BEBA9082057EF.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

A5A7898AB82947D9A9A943E9566E24F6.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning word and phrases based on grade 3 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

9F14EA33B95E4CF4B57A76884935FFC5.description: Recognize and observe differences between the conventions of spoken and written Standard English.

4B2E49AC90974F199B28C0D52D1DBB68.description: Choose words and phrases for effect.

F9F217D914BC4D438F188249745AB699.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

FFE4DEF4B99E40E9817813AEA61FCC53.description: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spellings.

D42B306875E14A238DA67E5A961158E2.description: Use spelling patterns and generalizations (e.g., word families, position-based spellings, syllable patterns, ending rules, and meaningful word parts) in writing words.

667C7B809AF546DEA6A8C2841582889C.description: Use conventional spelling for high-frequency and other studied words and for adding suffixes to base words (e.g., sitting, smiled, cries, or happiness).

8BBE407841704786A10D16ACB2AEEB73.description: Use commas and quotation marks in dialogue.

49FCCFB2ACF84973B4116C75EF0E1739.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

0109AC22C9B045F98C693308DA48B1D2.description: Produce simple, compound, and complex sentences.

7A5AB1245DFA4CFD81B15F16D3816D83.description: Form and use comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs, and choose between them depending on what is to be modified.

9D7130C108BB434C99A50E015E434FA9.description: Form and use the simple (e.g., I walked; I walk; I will walk) verb tenses.

7ECFBB37950D4E46A4FA254FFC641E52.description: Form and use regular and irregular verbs.

0B746E2ED1D54B29814BD01E9CE0032A.description: Form and use regular and irregular plural nouns.

3D87FF506C3A4536821293946F773E2D.description: Explain the function of nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs in general and their functions in particular sentences.

C83E58AB64A24D77BF114AD675A71226.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

9E9E30C3D4C04A8889928EC0BCB1EB2F.description: Speak in complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.

A7A21D1C70C5414CBDF31BFD29333C67.description: Create engaging audio recordings of stories or poems that demonstrate fluid reading at an understandable pace; add visual displays when appropriate to emphasize or enhance certain facts or details.

13E82875EDDB4AFA84E83D8F382085A3.description: Report on a topic or text; tell a story or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking audibly and coherently.

A244243B641C4F51AB56B61B6A54268C.description: Ask and answer questions about information from a speaker, offering appropriate elaboration and detail.

F2366FCFFCE74686AC6D0FEFC916E0C4.description: Determine the main ideas and supporting details of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

5EFC1D2F5402470784B5429DD53A3B29.description: Explain ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.

F0608BE8BA004408BB58A578C46A4EE2.description: Ask questions to check understanding of information presented, stay on topic, and link comments to the remarks of others.

FC929ED11AB44D61B6A8D1DCEAED8480.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to others with care, and speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).

F7F318965A914D18AFE13EE545535E1B.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

86DFC59EBA374EEA96672E86710FE27B.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 3 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing ideas clearly.

62447642BBBA4D1480D371B9E8391481.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

3014089EEA054AAB9E647F585EEA7083.description: Recall information from experiences or gather information from print and digital sources; take brief notes on sources and sort evidence into provided categories.

AC0DF197BBA240949CB661E64A0FD7D3.description: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge about a topic.

99A117C436D94B518DA848FCB05258F2.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

D7055C9D34B34CE395A358D0AD4AE0EE.description: With guidance and support from adults, use technology to produce and publish writing (using keyboarding skills) as well as to interact and collaborate with others.

DAA07A5C452E48C1BAEADF703BB8F74F.description: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing. (Editing for conventions should demonstrate command of Language standards up to and including grade 3).

BFF8E982BCFC461D8A8CDBF5B6034493.description: With guidance and support from adults, produce writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task and purpose. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in Text Types and Purposes.)

7F27AE067A7D4D08B920769896FCAB8C.description: Use transitional words and phrases to signal event order.

27548B476570470CA87F894C00F09E24.description: Use dialogue and descriptions of actions, thoughts, and feelings to develop experiences and events or show the response of characters to situations.

1AE6B11175EF4E359CEE5ADC2C5B591B.description: Establish a situation and introduce a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.

EC341241C0304A648F2144CF7D6CA3B0.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.

D9D17B1F3BAB4B7FA377E98502A8C3F2.description: Provide a concluding statement or section.

A5CD1EBF267948DD8693B85DF92F84B3.description: Use linking words and phrases (e.g., also, another, and, more, or but) to connect ideas within categories of information.

758C01D4948B464CBA0894E11D077F62.description: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, and details.

B63F3DAED8974023BB06B68C5D7F9749.description: Introduce a topic and group related information together; include illustrations when useful to aid comprehension.

F0D497F54DF64FC48233657F332F0733.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.

9F0831126D1243A4A3C15710B6963ABD.description: Provide a concluding statement or section.

C32568BBA5A1413BB22A47F7EC905A36.description: Use linking words and phrases (e.g., because, therefore, since, or for example) to connect opinion and reasons.

8A69479473A448AFA201E688C6C10243.description: Provide reasons that support the opinion.

75128097DB4842A2B3B4246DCCA44801.description: Introduce the topic or text being discussed, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure that lists reasons.

EECA34728C7A47B9B8A7FBF63075BDE7.description: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons.

DA718CE1F925425AA740E324AC20E2C1.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend informational texts, including social studies, science, and technical texts, at the high end of the grades 2–3 text complexity range independently and proficiently.

75776BB7B68F4B5AA78A8C11845E1946.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas and poetry, at the high end of the grades 2–3 text complexity range independently and proficiently.

A8364ED8F7D44292A32AF5109F2C676D.description: Range of Reading and Text Complexity

072066DF15AB4E0992009048C6381277.description: Compare and contrast the most important points and key details presented in two informational texts on the same topic.

E8DE0834FB904008BB418F74EC5EAED5.description: Describe the logical connection between particular sentences and paragraphs in an informational text (e.g., comparison, cause/effect, or first/second/third in a sequence).

4E71860CE2E2450AA845D2A20ADEEE27.description: Use information gained from illustrations (e.g., maps or photographs) and the words in an informational text to demonstrate understanding of the text (e.g., where, when, why, and how key events occur).

A40CE66C9EAA4796B3990A16F0A91936.description: Compare and contrast the themes, settings, and plots of literary stories written by the same author about the same or similar characters (e.g., in books from a series).

C03DE6D912EE4C54B1073173C102EBB0.description: Explain how specific aspects of a literary text's illustrations contribute to what is conveyed by the words in a story (e.g., create mood or emphasize aspects of a character or setting).

D4EC7FAE94B3430C92DE6867B2E5FA75.description: Distinguish one's own point of view from that of the author of an informational text.

135E50508F1E48C295717D57D99AA628.description: Use informational text features and search tools (e.g., key words, sidebars, and hyperlinks) to locate information relevant to a given topic efficiently

2B0B50FA59864296A0477578EBB2F181.description: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in an informational text relevant to a grade 3 topic or subject area.

7AF8EDDEB2934D7EBC18CBFF2676E6F2.description: Distinguish one's point of view from that of the narrator or those of the characters in a literary text.

8F61E13B9AA74745B0C2C5B14EEE8F52.description: Refer to parts of stories, dramas, and poems when writing or speaking about a literary text, using terms such as chapter, scene, and stanza; describe how each successive part builds on earlier sections.

E7FCE0F549B042DFA8B2A05B3F3A9C55.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a literary text, distinguishing literal from nonliteral language.

3A7FDC16C3B84A8887AA177D9C6363F9.description: Describe the relationship between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in technical procedures in an informational text, using language that pertains to time, sequence, and cause/effect.

361243DEA7364561B015A8E2A75D35C6.description: Determine the main idea of an informational text; recount the key details and explain how they support the main idea.

5D51F0B6F2BE4AC7AC18E2CAFE83C109.description: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of an informational text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.

59304F823BAA4503A2306704B39AFABD.description: Describe characters in a literary story (e.g., their traits, motivations, or feelings) and explain how their actions contribute to the sequence of events.

EC3A5680AED64C118D264462D4B3D0C4.description: Recount stories, including fables, folktales, and myths from diverse cultures; determine the central message, lesson, or moral and explain how it is conveyed through key details in the literary text.

5CB3B97662EE499A9CFC469CF4DA5D92.description: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a literary text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.

9DCE176B55B448B5B9EBAED66BF53AE0.description: Write legibly in cursive or joined italics, allowing margins and correct spacing between letters in a word and words in a sentence.

83474D7ABE4E4BA284EE63A00575287E.description: Decode words with common Latin suffixes.

B171597B85A04C8B8D5AB86EC2AB1679.description: Identify and know the meaning of the most common prefixes and derivational suffixes.

3821DD328F1548F3B7D34ECC707C4EBD.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

545C10E1CE814B3B90D36D964372DA5D.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

621EB282E3434176BB04A6737D87544B.description: Read on-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.

9CFD5F8708F54092AEF2BBCEBBFB03DF.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

B378B9F2E11146758C7D09316006798E.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

document.title: Next Generation Standards and Objectives for Science in West Virginia Schools

278F86E3483C47F98F6197CD1EBB0CBA.description: write routinely over extended time frames (time for reflection and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

767C8B165EE14D5F9CE652D103BE5286.description: draw evidence from informational texts to support analysis, reflection and research.

8B961FF1D03B4562892DA6A2935E0D99.description: gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, using search terms effectively; assess the credibility and accuracy of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

64995D3B26D146488C53A9D6A8F66E1F.description: conduct short research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question), drawing on several sources and generating additional related, focused questions that allow for multiple avenues of exploration.

66E736CAC47041098B01846253650A71.description: Writing - Research to Build and Present Knowledge

B7E06437A9CF4AD191F38A3D418B9715.description: use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and present the relationships between information and ideas clearly and efficiently.

D8B24A81A04E4D18A6929AEA7CDEF80E.description: with some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting or trying a new approach, focusing on how well purpose and audience have been addressed.

5246E45AFEFA4BBFB0F14B02742C7570.description: produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization and style are appropriate to task, purpose and audience.

82AE5D3A03374511B346D923F568C85E.description: Writing - Production and Distribution of Writing

E4DA919897774AAA931AE89CAA0BF4A8.description:
write informative/explanatory texts, including the narration of historical events, scientific procedures/experiments or technical processes:
  • introduce a topic clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts and information into broader categories as appropriate to achieving purpose; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts and tables) and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.
  • develop the topic with relevant, well-chosen facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.
  • use appropriate and varied transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.
  • use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.
  • establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone.
  • provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented.

C456818E8270441BA2808A905050882E.description:
write arguments focused on discipline-specific content:
  • introduce claim(s) about a topic or issue, acknowledge and distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims and organize the reasons and evidence logically.
  • support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant, accurate data and evidence that demonstrate an understanding of the topic or text, using credible sources.
  • use words, phrases and clauses to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among claim(s), counterclaims, reasons and evidence.
  • establish and maintain a formal style.
  • provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

F5B379834CB14A9BB3FDD7E78BC2BBBA.description: by the end of grade 8, read and comprehend science/technical texts in the grades 6–8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

77C57EA3AE5C489E9F548008DF9633D0.description: Reading - Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

77E2812E0F31403B8B337EF1AAD29B25.description: compare and contrast the information gained from experiments, simulations, video, or multimedia sources with that gained from reading a text on the same topic.

EF75ADAC9459417FA34FCF10937EAD74.description: distinguish among facts, reasoned judgment based on research findings, and speculation in a text.

B6B9F1EF4AFA4A3E9007BD4C187FFCAC.description: integrate quantitative or technical information expressed in words in a text with a version of that information expressed visually (e.g., in a flowchart, diagram, model, graph, or table).

2D514EF3B3A8430AA047B956D3502D7D.description: Reading - Integration of Knowledge and Ideas

02657F34D9E14212A53660BA33DE2EF9.description: analyze the author's purpose in providing an explanation, describing a procedure, or discussing an experiment in a text.

3124E6CB6D474581AA42C229A378B85E.description: analyze the structure an author uses to organize a text, including how the major sections contribute to the whole and to an understanding of the topic.

9A5235A602A640368AAD2556DE14E647.description: determine the meaning of symbols, key terms, and other domain-specific words and phrases as they are used in a specific scientific or technical context relevant to grades 6–8 texts and topics.

A3AD6374038F4E67B6502971A85F753B.description: follow precisely a multistep procedure when carrying out experiments, taking measurements, or performing technical tasks.

3A63B33D25FE4446A5B77E11E5F84175.description: determine the central ideas or conclusions of a text; provide an accurate summary of the text distinct from prior knowledge or opinions.

26EDFA34B53A456BA71291F41D408158.description: cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of science and technical texts.

16DA8C2AE74744219F0E6E43F6C6532C.description: develop a model to generate data for iterative testing and modification of a proposed object, tool, or process such that an optimal design can be achieved.

9FBAEDD415004C0CA2390BA4F193AE0D.description: analyze data from tests to determine similarities and differences among several design solutions to identify the best characteristics of each that can be combined into a new solution to better meet the criteria for success.

D4F22F34C6154A57B932129B6B1EB5CB.description: evaluate competing design solutions using a systematic process to determine how well they meet the criteria and constraints of the problem.

010F26AEC7B54D9B9023899C7F2AE261.description: define the criteria and constraints of a design problem with sufficient precision to ensure a successful solution, taking into account relevant scientific principles and potential impacts on people and the natural environment that may limit possible solutions.

5CEF9E10D3154AC68A214DCEF421F591.description: Engineering, Technology, and Applications of Science

296C4477C7E14258A89757A1279CBD7C.description: construct an argument supported by evidence for how increases in human population and per-capita consumption of natural resources impact Earth's systems.

D7345A603E0F4807B101D1F2BB275EF7.description: undertake a design project to construct, test, and modify a device that either releases or absorbs thermal energy by chemical processes.

60D08D2EEA574C6E87BB065326E4DF07.description: develop and use a model to describe how the total number of atoms does not change in a chemical reaction and thus mass is conserved.

FBB6FE5007D94EBF80A5268B2DAB50AA.description: analyze and interpret data on the properties of substances before and after the substances interact to determine if a chemical reaction has occurred.

57B00A3776174A8586116EB9DE2A424E.description: develop a model that predicts and describes changes in particle motion, temperature, and state of a pure substance when thermal energy is added or removed.

0A05575862104EC3AFC4A76AD1D45E0C.description: gather and make sense of information to describe that synthetic materials come from natural resources and impact society.

AC2661A31FD24B0A8197E51D5FDF39BE.description: develop models to describe the atomic composition of simple molecules and extended structures.

64121D41F5CA4620825AE6EE70071823.description: Expand, combine, and reduce sentences for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.

58231287D2D743E990F76BF2BFBA93B6.description: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.

9B67030B9BAB45F5B26742FC3EC75DB7.description: Use a comma to set off the words yes and no (e.g., Yes, thank you.), to set off a tag question from the rest of the sentence (e.g., It's true, isn't it?), and to indicate direct address (e.g., Is that you, Steve?).

6286395336CB4BD68B3F4ED656589C33.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation and spelling when writing.

72B91771727B4D199F98501AF8BDD8B3.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in verb tense.

223AAF3D6ACF4A348E5BDAD4164F2DE3.description: Use verb tense to convey various times, sequences, states, and conditions.

6236858678DE4E0AB8310843697CC282.description: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach. ACABB82CD261482FBA6BFA88529ADB65.description: Write a narrative to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.

B3CDBCD50173429E87B671CFE9F41066.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the information or explanation presented.

A48C8F49EBE44857B22E22A3F1E41411.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

CEFF4436A94941F6933938E7629FA27C.description: Link ideas within and across categories of information using words, phrases, and clauses (e.g., in contrast and especially).

C5DC21A4F1AA4DBB80D7B3EBD8AB15D2.description: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples related to the topic.

CE15F26675C24F00A9C65D428B9840A7.description: Introduce a topic clearly, provide a general observation, and focus and group related information logically; include formatting (e.g., headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aid comprehension.

AE6538763642405C82698862FEF2B974.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.

C571AF3EE8454A82AA0E7F2829701380.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the opinion presented.

01264939D25C40D4A48ED955BEE39F10.description: Link opinion and reasons using words, phrases, and clauses (e.g., consequently and specifically).

5BFF7368004349878B1373E8F108A880.description: Provide logically ordered reasons that are supported by facts and details.

FA4E4CF4356E493B94565F035AE6D960.description: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which ideas are logically grouped to support the writer's purpose.

443194C9233E411FA5B40137972261E5.description: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons and information.

442036F87FCC4AF18D05F7F1551EDF12.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend informational texts, including social studies, science, and technical texts, at the high end of the grades 4–5 text complexity range independently and proficiently.

173307F1B13840129880B6CB07112C65.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, at the high end of the grades 4–5 text complexity range independently and proficiently.

E1465DE8090740C092693CFBAA359E1A.description: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in an informational text, identifying which reasons and evidence support which point(s).

C1314981D2444854B25EC08EF9A03954.description: Draw on information from multiple print or digital informational sources, demonstrating the ability to locate an answer to a question quickly or to solve a problem efficiently.

18A5808BACD440DFBC9C3C48195A5348.description: Analyze how visual and multimedia elements contribute to the meaning, tone, or beauty of a literary text (e.g., graphic novel, multimedia presentation of fiction, folktale, myth, and/or poem).

B3FC962FE77E4E56857945A2FDCA3D6B.description: Analyze multiple accounts of the same event or topic, noting important similarities and differences in the point of view they represent in informational texts.

A13D9A7A81BE4DAF8C6FF32D80235C87.description: Compare and contrast the overall structure (e.g., chronology, comparison, cause/effect, and problem/solution) of events, ideas, concepts, or information in two or more informational texts.

C901D5177EE946E8B3B2C89E0F9EE8F8.description: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in an informational text relevant to a grade 5 topic or subject area.

48C30A241C0E4DB189280210D25A78D0.description: Describe how a narrator's or speaker's point of view influences how events are described in a literary text.

15D05694471E4C28903AB8688CAAC833.description: Explain how a series of chapters, scenes, or stanzas fits together in a literary text to provide the overall structure of a particular story, drama, or poem.

1658054987304EF68DEBE110D8F3A32C.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a literary text, including figurative language such as metaphors and similes.

420D4122900D4E43AFBE91D3E3F7ED96.description: Using an informational text, explain the relationships or interactions between two or more individuals, events, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, or technical text based on specific information in the text.

091ABD344AB049BF9A04F94FD5676845.description: Determine two or more main ideas of an informational text and explain how they are supported by key details; summarize the text.

0ABDB1B2160F4EBF8EF5D5575DC52000.description: Quote accurately from an informational text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

F5A4F76D08634843895AAC9945373253.description: Compare and contrast two or more characters, settings, or events in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the literary text (e.g., how characters interact).
