4D89C5FA661349DEAF11304F5F668352.description: Quote accurately from a literary text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

ABF6E5B1411545E193753DB4D1FB67F4.description: Use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (e.g., roots and affixes) to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context and out of context.

4471AA3068DF4A999809772B874EEA8A.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

6A3A979896D8459F847416A1B4E62C01.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

2068844FEA2E4005855BEDCF7D557761.description: Read on-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.

149D964ED8984A20BACA9848A1266A16.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

0C05695903EE480D8D6C9784903BE51E.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Mathematics

8777C2EF280F4F56BFED61C3FA6B918A.description: Observe using graphs and tables that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing linearly, quadratically, or (more generally) as a polynomial function.
comments: Instructional Note: Compare linear and exponential growth to growth of quadratic growth.

E9DB670BE509419F94E126FFDCEE337E.description: Construct and compare linear, quadratic and exponential models and solve problems.

08A78FE90B5D4FBCAF6C95FE040A5342.description: Solve an equation of the form f(x) = c for a simple function f that has an inverse and write an expression for the inverse.
comments: For example, f(x) = 2 x³ or f(x) = (x+1)/(x-1) for x ≠ 1.
Instructional Note: Focus on linear functions but consider simple situations where the domain of the function must be restricted in order for the inverse to exist, such as f(x) = x², x > 0.

1E11D94145224FE0B99BB9F8081F8641.description: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology. Include recognizing even and odd functions from their graphs and algebraic expressions for them.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on quadratic functions, and consider including absolute value functions.

E043AEF89D7A478CA09AF279CDC0C84E.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

9925AC66987D4F6E8A60FBEC441D57AA.description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations.
comments: For example, build a function that models the temperature of a cooling body by adding a constant function to a decaying exponential, and relate these functions to the model.

D5EA26BD27A6449F83632A6CC3E5E1B9.description: Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context.

91BC9FAA475E404382ABB94FAFE2284A.description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on situations that exhibit a quadratic relationship.

FD8821EB39DD48D1BDC98D8C816AF3FC.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

C84068304EC8428283D9B5B4055EB058.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). (e.g., Given a graph of one quadratic function and an algebraic expression for another, say which has the larger maximum.)
comments: Instructional Note: Extend work with quadratics to include the relationship between coefficients and roots, and that once roots are known, a quadratic function can be factored.

F3F0D9177C744E87BBABBBAC7004B966.description: Use the properties of exponents to interpret expressions for exponential functions.
comments: For example, identify percent rate of change in functions such as y = (1.02)<sup>t</sup>, y = (0.97)<sup>t</sup>, y = (1.01)<sup>12t</sup>, y = (1.2)<sup>t/10</sup>, and classify them as representing exponential growth or decay.

FE97133ACB3D469AB11770ECC08E1A76.description: Use the process of factoring and completing the square in a quadratic function to show zeros, extreme values, and symmetry of the graph, and interpret these in terms of a context.

3767513F8A1E4755B36C8075FC02D7D4.description: Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.
comments: Instructional Note: Extend work with quadratics to include the relationship between coefficients and roots, and that once roots are known, a quadratic function can be factored. This unit, and in particular in M.A18.68b, extends the work begun in Unit 2 on exponential functions with integral exponents.

D34DBE9CED6840E4A0995B8951F0A5E9.description: Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value functions.

1F7B134A8FC346DA805135D6A6FEA4A0.description: Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima.

B84030F3A3954DDCA1B10E71F92C523D.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.
comments: Instructional Note: Compare and contrast absolute value, step and piecewise-defined functions with linear, quadratic, and exponential functions. Highlight issues of domain, range, and usefulness when examining piecewise-defined functions. Extend work with quadratics to include the relationship between coefficients and roots, and that once roots are known, a quadratic function can be factored.

80C7BB4514434AB387C2A436450F335A.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on quadratic functions; compare with linear and exponential functions studies in the unit on Linear and Exponential Functions.

61AD2895CF8F43A4B39341D4BE2AC43F.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes.
comments: For example, if the function h(n) gives the number of person-hours it takes to assemble n engines in a factory, then the positive integers would be an appropriate domain for the function.
Instructional Note: Focus on quadratic functions; compare with linear and exponential functions studies in the unit on Linear and Exponential Functions.

DA363F3A5F824948BEFC962731C5BF34.description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship. Key features include: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on quadratic functions; compare with linear and exponential functions studies in the unit on Linear and Exponential Functions.

D1CC6FD61E64483BA48D8E5E3640448B.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of a context.

064B9CDF32694767944CEBE62B368DE0.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between two points in a coordinate system.
comments: Instructional Note: Discuss applications of the Pythagorean theorem and its connections to radicals, rational exponents, and irrational numbers.

7697A92B78474C37965243B77BE44E8F.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to determine unknown side lengths in right triangles in real-world and mathematical problems in two and three dimensions.
comments: Instructional Note: Discuss applications of the Pythagorean theorem and its connections to radicals, rational exponents, and irrational numbers.

D60D9E3F074D4434B705E04B65C007D6.description: Explain a proof of the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse

2356F3182422498D99D0F1E7FAB3EDC4.description: Understand and apply the Pythagorean theorem.

E36B3E2C60D24F209E5E9F1BB3AAAD7F.description: Explain why the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational; that the sum of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational; and that the product of a nonzero rational number and an irrational number is irrational.
comments: Instructional Note: Connect to physical situations (e.g., finding the perimeter of a square of area 2).

56AE5D2A93CE4260AA57A906DAA7B0CD.description: Use properties of rational and irrational numbers.

0BE3C8027644404AA27695203EDAE631.description: Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically. (e.g., Find the points of intersection between the line y = –3x and the circle x² + y² = 3.)
comments: Instructional Note: Include systems consisting of one linear and one quadratic equation. Include systems that lead to work with fractions. For example, finding the intersections between x² + y² = 1 and y = (x+1)/2 leads to the point (3/5, 4/5) on the unit circle, corresponding to the Pythagorean triple 3² + 4² = 5².

3DBFE8391B56476DAC2676BD612A521D.description: Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x² = 49), taking square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula and factoring, as appropriate to the initial form of the equation. Recognize when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

6C812FC631D24365B1837E160BA53BC9.description: Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x – p)² = q that has the same solutions. Derive the quadratic formula from this form.

D835E96B214643F5BE271D0EE70543B3.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.
comments: Instructional Note: Students should learn of the existence of the complex number system, but will not solve quadratics with complex solutions until Algebra II.

4057D2DFFEBD4E02A39C00154728BBA1.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

08E286953F604AC499A9BD029F115199.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations. (e.g., Rearrange Ohm's law V = IR to highlight resistance R.)
comments: Instructional Note: Extend work on linear and exponential equations in the unit on Relationships between Quantities to include quadratic equations. Extend M.A18.57 to formulas involving squared variables.

B1BAADC320EB4A88BFBC4DF0C0E1BEF2.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.
comments: Instructional Note: Extend work on linear and exponential equations in the unit on Relationships between Quantities to include quadratic equations.

D9D6B09EDF6A43078C4A87EB0FBBBA53.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.
comments: Instructional Note: Extend work on linear and exponential equations in the unit on Relationships between Quantities to include quadratic equations.

AAD6A112DB144285B657D90358B2D5D1.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

E7BFBF3E3C694D8FB109A348FB2319E3.description: Understand that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on polynomial expressions that simplify to forms that are linear or quadratic in a positive integer power of x.

E864D43B7C6841FFB51C86F07584DFA6.description: Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions.
comments: For example the expression 1.15<sup>t</sup> can be rewritten as (1.15<sup>1/12</sup>)<sup>12t</sup> ≈ 1.012<sup>12t</sup> to reveal the approximate equivalent monthly interest rate if the annual rate is 15%.

F6FD2999C3204AA996E6485F4AECE364.description: Complete the square in a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function it defines.

260EB3E51CF442148F4D6F13C3475DF9.description: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.

C2647FB0E1EB4406B6268ABAAF5BC6C8.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression.
comments: Instructional Note: It is important to balance conceptual understanding and procedural fluency in work with equivalent expressions. For example, development of skill in factoring and completing the square goes hand-in-hand with understanding what different forms of a quadratic expression reveal.

2EA6A9E16B0248EB923DBAF37DD5F11C.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems.

A141EE60EA9C42098AB21A07C0DB9DAE.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.
comments: For example, see x<sup>4</sup> – y<sup>4</sup> as (x²)² – (y²)², thus recognizing it as a difference of squares that can be factored as (x² – y²)(x² + y²).

336D076325334D7ABE011F62122F1CEE.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.
comments: For example, interpret P(1 + r)<sup>n</sup> as the product of P and a factor not depending on P.

75100B9716C34057AA62DA617731F43C.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

013F21359F8D44979A5FB07E4361DC64.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on quadratic and exponential expressions. For M.A18.51b, exponents are extended from integer found in the unit on Relationships between Quantities to rational exponents focusing on those that represent square roots and cube roots.
Instructional Note: The important distinction between a statistical relationship and a cause-and-effect relationship arises here.

840B58A32D2E4395B97ABB2927A28B25.description: Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.
comments: Instructional Note: Build on students' work with linear relationships and introduce the correlation coefficient. The focus here is on the computation and interpretation of the correlation coefficient as a measure of how well the data fit the relationship.

6635754D4C5240EF9AD7CB5560754433.description: Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in the context of the data.
comments: Instructional Note: Build on students' work with linear relationships and introduce the correlation coefficient. The focus here is on the computation and interpretation of the correlation coefficient as a measure of how well the data fit the relationship.

33BA30253E4741419D6CBEB7D4DBE21D.description: Fit a linear function for scatter plots that suggest a linear association.

F0C1096BC41544F492D4FA0803973917.description: Informally assess the fit of a function by plotting and analyzing residuals.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus should be on situations for which linear models are appropriate, but may be used to preview quadratic functions in the Quadratic Functions and Modeling Unit.

B359927CD23346F8BBDED43091AD8994.description: Fit a function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data. Use given functions or choose a function suggested by the context.
comments: Instructional Note: Emphasize linear and exponential models.

96FF8CC02EDF441DB3CCCEADB49B2854.description: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related.
comments: Instructional Note: Students take a more sophisticated look at using a linear function to model the relationship between two numerical variables. In addition to fitting a line to data, students assess how well the model fits by analyzing residuals.

DF724E1FECEC495B9C4CE2CF4E14338E.description: Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal and conditional relative frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data.

55779433642045E2AAE3E74C002FAACD.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables.

CF94E46A9D794BC98E9CE10D68F98AFB.description: Understand that patterns of association can also be seen in bivariate categorical data by displaying frequencies and relative frequencies in a two-way table. Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects. Use relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe possible association between the two variables. (e.g., Collect data from students in your class on whether or not they have a curfew on school nights and whether or not they have assigned chores at home. Is there evidence that those who have a curfew also tend to have chores?)

1E0A804D2855435BAC112AB792A69362.description: Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the context of bivariate measurement data, interpreting the slope and intercept. (e.g., In a linear model for a biology experiment, interpret a slope of 1.5 cm/hr as meaning that an additional hour of sunlight each day is associated with an additional 1.5 cm in mature plant height.)

81D4203568BD466285C8AED2AA8729B6.description: Know that straight lines are widely used to model relationships between two quantitative variables. For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line, and informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

539134AD7B514C3DB2C2A0C0B8C04633.description: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities. Describe patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or negative association, linear association, and nonlinear association.

53C1336B2DAC4E72919A0148ED0F67CE.description: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.

A5A1107E58D6473B92F3C67B0A6CB886.description: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).
comments: Instructional Note: In grades 6 – 7, students describe center and spread in a data distribution. Here they choose a summary statistic appropriate to the characteristics of the data distribution, such as the shape of the distribution or the existence of extreme data points.

6A8FCE54CFEB4F7098489324C0B2F20F.description: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.
comments: Instructional Note: In grades 6 – 7, students describe center and spread in a data distribution. Here they choose a summary statistic appropriate to the characteristics of the data distribution, such as the shape of the distribution or the existence of extreme data points.

2EDABF25F32341A4896464172E5D79E8.description: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, and box plots).

EE9028F4263340B9B4F8406FB9B58E84.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.

561312EEB98A435E98A392B0AD2AC2FA.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function in terms of a context.
comments: Instructional Note: Limit exponential functions to those of the form f(x) = b<sup>x</sup> + k.

9F3E3C0D8D9F42B29AB4A414D80D9E75.description: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model.

13599C45381B48A69B16AD4DFDD62783.description: Observe using graphs and tables that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing linearly, quadratically, or (more generally) as a polynomial function.
comments: Instructional Note: Limit to comparisons between linear and exponential models.

756199EE939949FC9413EECD5490C9D1.description: Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a description of a relationship or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a table).

5CB7F5E865384A10870EEA9023E7EEC7.description: Recognize situations in which a quantity grows or decays by a constant percent rate per unit interval relative to another.

222E40D7F75E433F9A79E1BB18DECED8.description: Recognize situations in which one quantity changes at a constant rate per unit interval relative to another.

E1ADFBED3F2A4764AB918604539699BD.description: Prove that linear functions grow by equal differences over equal intervals; exponential functions grow by equal factors over equal intervals.

4BE32FAEC60344DFAF7CB56B0649705B.description: Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions and with exponential functions.

F71681AF21C94A8D8D5C4897168318EF.description: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems.

638A56C369BC49BFA6AA50C4BFE3CB44.description: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology. Include recognizing even and odd functions from their graphs and algebraic expressions for them.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on vertical translations of graphs of linear and exponential functions. Relate the vertical translation of a linear function to its y-intercept. While applying other transformations to a linear graph is appropriate at this level, it may be difficult for students to identify or distinguish between the effects of the other transformations included in this standard.

C33548A791CA440D8BE71F6EFBBB93A4.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

D0C6E5F2E19B4ACB8DE7BAAD459A48AE.description: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula, use them to model situations, and translate between the two forms.
comments: Instructional Note: Connect arithmetic sequences to linear functions and geometric sequences to exponential functions.

EE1326212FC844B0BDB0BCD88EDC9EF9.description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations.
comments: For example build a function that models the temperature of a cooling body by adding a constant function to a decaying exponential, and relate these functions to the model.

E8EA9FAE2BAD465D96D4E7F58F671434.description: Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context.

CB44D48702604F0D94F0DCA790B76829.description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.
comments: Instructional Note: Limit to linear and exponential functions.

104D3E6CCDFE4E3BA53C441AE46B6041.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

C403B702EEC74B72A1B7015041648F69.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). (e.g., Given a graph of one quadratic function and an algebraic expression for another, say which has the larger maximum.)
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on linear and exponential functions. Include comparisons of two functions presented algebraically. For example, compare the growth of two linear functions, or two exponential functions such as y = 3<sup>n</sup> and y = 100·2<sup>n</sup>.

6FF64B9C3B3B468E883C5CF39A829254.description: Graph exponential and logarithmic functions, showing intercepts and end behavior and trigonometric functions, showing period, midline and amplitude.

1FA0F8B2A30D47B9B40A81DCF2A037BF.description: Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima.

39D4C3BABC31417F8760F8C286F541A4.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on linear and exponential functions. Include comparisons of two functions presented algebraically. For example, compare the growth of two linear functions, or two exponential functions such as y = 3<sup>n</sup> and y = 100·2<sup>n</sup>.

12EE44240F3845B6B685EB6741764064.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on linear functions and intervals for exponential functions whose domain is a subset of the integers. The Quadratic Functions and Modeling unit of this course and Algebra II course will address other function types.

EF3C1DE34AEE42F9A453EC0580B430A7.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on linear and exponential functions.

FC715E59C5274F35AFB6A4EE5A52A32B.description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship. Key features include: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on linear and exponential functions.

F649C225404F45409409D5C6ED89DA3C.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of a context.

053DC53B80514C4AAB84ECC4D6A3EB89.description: Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph (e.g., where the function is increasing or decreasing, linear or nonlinear). Sketch a graph that exhibits the qualitative features of a function that has been described verbally.

66A85C67DD504AAD9800ACD3B83D87DD.description: Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities. Determine the rate of change and initial value of the function from a description of a relationship or from two (x, y) values, including reading these from a table or from a graph. Interpret the rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models, and in terms of its graph or a table of values.

F5A27B8AD073455F9CBBDC1B7EB15153.description: Use functions to model relationships between quantities.

959EF671ABBD446AAD67C2AECE3625B4.description: Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset of the integers.
comments: For example, the Fibonacci sequence is defined recursively by f(0) = f(1) = 1, f(n+1) = f(n)+ f(n-1) for n ≥ 1.

Instructional Note: Students should experience a variety of types of situations modeled by functions. Detailed analysis of any particular class of function at this stage is not advised. Students should apply these concepts throughout their future mathematics courses. Constrain examples to linear functions and exponential functions having integral domains. Draw connection to M.A18.33, which requires students to write arithmetic and geometric sequences.)

4F439D05BEAF4D3B888E7111550B06E2.description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.
comments: Instructional Note: Students should experience a variety of types of situations modeled by functions. Detailed analysis of any particular class of function at this stage is not advised. Students should apply these concepts throughout their future mathematics courses. Constrain examples to linear functions and exponential functions having integral domains.

439D4C9ADFCB4A22BD2FCB1F0B89FED6.description: Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If f is a function and x is an element of its domain, then f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input x. The graph of f is the graph of the equation y = f(x).
comments: Instructional Note: Students should experience a variety of types of situations modeled by functions. Detailed analysis of any particular class of function at this stage is not advised. Students should apply these concepts throughout their future mathematics courses. Constrain examples to linear functions and exponential functions having integral domains.

98C6150B67844DC0B4F95886D686D463.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation.

7005318ECA464222A7D04AC4007B0032.description: Interpret the equation y = mx + b as defining a linear function, whose graph is a straight line; give examples of functions that are not linear. (e.g., The function A = s² giving the area of a square as a function of its side length is not linear because its graph contains the points (1,1), (2,4) and (3,9), which are not on a straight line.)

44DC0583C5A7435292EE9BB57C2B9FAD.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). (e.g., Given a linear function represented by a table of values and a linear function represented by an algebraic expression, determine which function has the greater rate of change.)

2936E250A94B44549BC5E5BCECB5A040.description: Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output. The graph of a function is the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and the corresponding output.

333843A8DBBD485E886F382EA8712F92.description: Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.

E0FE1D35D79945DFBBBBB0ABAE988E58.description: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately (e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values or find successive approximations). Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential and logarithmic functions.
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on cases where f(x) and g(x) are linear or exponential.

1D996B15EDFD41E2817AEFF18A80DBF5.description: Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).
comments: Instructional Note: Focus on linear and exponential equations and be able to adapt and apply that learning to other types of equations in future courses.

C64FDA63268040BF9FCE39207F5ECCE9.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.

A04BD558FE8F4C168E50202CE67C6949.description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.
comments: Instructional Note: Include cases where two equations describe the same line (yielding infinitely many solutions) and cases where two equations describe parallel lines (yielding no solution).

BE594CCD989D468EB0EF1FCC809E7BEC.description: Prove that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.
comments: Instructional Note: Include cases where two equations describe the same line (yielding infinitely many solutions) and cases where two equations describe parallel lines (yielding no solution).

A6B6E2F5218D4801806904BF15D2FF08.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to two linear equations in two variables. (e.g., Given coordinates for two pairs of points, determine whether the line through the first pair of points intersects the line through the second pair.)

473378E918834A6EBAB423A197981C05.description: Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables algebraically, and estimate solutions by graphing the equations. Solve simple cases by inspection.
comments: For example, 3x + 2y = 5 and 3x + 2y = 6 have no solution because 3x + 2y cannot simultaneously be 5 and 6.

D30477F1F06B42B3829873A382FF9767.description: Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables correspond to points of intersection of their graphs, because points of intersection satisfy both equations simultaneously.

BDC2277F3E4B4B4DA6E9491598BB8509.description: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.
comments: Instructional Note: While this content is likely subsumed by M.A18.10, 14, and 15, it could be used for scaffolding instruction to the more sophisticated content found there.

1AF6E7CA02C34B94B0947F50577F9892.description: Analyze and solve linear equations and pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

C814C842C48147EE8161429165C38A85.description: Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.
comments: Instructional Note: Address this standard before discussing exponential functions with continuous domains.

80EBE9FD8E944F149263D4CC6800C7E1.description: Explain how the definition of the meaning of rational exponents follows from extending the properties of integer exponents to those values, allowing for a notation for radicals in terms of rational exponents.
comments: For example, we define 5<sup>1/3</sup> to be the cube root of 5 because we want (5<sup>1/3</sup>)³ = 5(<sup>1/3</sup>)³ to hold, so (5<sup>1/3</sup>)³ must equal 5.
Instructional Note: Address this standard before discussing exponential functions with continuous domains.

034981970D6E4FC693549C49A843EA1C.description: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents.

85692634C62E4EA7BA1A5C648D45C3F6.description: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.
comments: Instructional Note: Extend earlier work with solving linear equations to solving linear inequalities in one variable and to solving literal equations that are linear in the variable being solved for. Include simple exponential equations that rely only on application of the laws of exponents, such as 5<sup>x</sup> = 125 or 2<sup>x</sup> = 1 /16.

A280E40240884CAABFB666D616FCAA1E.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

034E4D2300AD4171BD0EC3C6657006BE.description: Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method.
comments: Instructional Note: Students should focus on linear equations and be able to extend and apply their reasoning to other types of equations in future units and courses. Students will solve exponential equations in Algebra II.

FAA02B09616D4226BD2B903561E7F25B.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.

D0B35A160426498AA490202351525D7B.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations. (e.g., Rearrange Ohm's law V = IR to highlight resistance R.)
comments: Instructional Note: Limit to formulas with a linear focus.

A5F2C078925C4D71B0864463C041C97A.description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or non-viable options in a modeling context. (e.g., Represent inequalities describing nutritional and cost constraints on combinations of different foods.)
comments: Instructional Note: Limit to linear equations and inequalities.

FA4EBDFEDD8E42D09BE3A7F23E853C9B.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.
comments: Instructional Note: Limit to linear and exponential equations, and, in the case of exponential equations, limit to situations requiring evaluation of exponential functions at integer inputs.

A9799D1E1BF54258B14AC4E9EFC490D9.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.
comments: Instructional Note: Limit to linear and exponential equations, and, in the case of exponential equations, limit to situations requiring evaluation of exponential functions at integer inputs.

F7CAEACD5D7347F79299B9AE634EA6F6.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

7EC53286205B48AD9BE3995ECCB2BF62.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.
comments: For example, interpret P(1 + r)<sup>n</sup> as the product of P and a factor not depending on P.
Instructional Note: Limit to linear expressions and to exponential expressions with integer exponents.

CBE0E1D85BBC492C9AE532B9401A21D9.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

8082AADFB1194142B4580E6B2B0CA139.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

38AFDDBBAF8B462CA39D0101A7CA6C25.description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

A348CC9FEC274184A8D65D6F5244D969.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.
comments: Instructional Note: Working with quantities and the relationships between them provides grounding for work with expressions, equations, and functions.

7E993A25838645D6BF217440654FA20B.description: Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems; choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

715C1242BBF24CBAAEA4FD7F8615B2C1.description: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems

56A98B5F852947E089C0ED71E81F1D9A.description: Understand that patterns of association can also be seen in bivariate categorical data by displaying frequencies and relative frequencies in a two-way table. Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects. Use relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe possible association between the two variables. (e.g., Collect data from students in your class on whether or not they have a curfew on school nights and whether or not they have assigned chores at home. Is there evidence that those who have a curfew also tend to have chores?)

C721DECD9E6F415C9C44E8FCD1EBD923.description: Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the context of bivariate measurement data, interpreting the slope and intercept. (e.g., In a linear model for a biology experiment, interpret a slope of 1.5 cm/hr as meaning that an additional hour of sunlight each day is associated with an additional 1.5 cm in mature plant height.)

4E0F8E80E10A42EF9747532A7F0ADAC6.description: Know that straight lines are widely used to model relationships between two quantitative variables. For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line and informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

5F47BB2A24694C6A97343352A49AE90C.description: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities. Describe patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or negative association, linear association and nonlinear association.

97110983E05C4935A0A12A70DD290C94.description: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.

4FB8791A1A82475C820511DD86521975.description: Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph (e.g., where the function is increasing or decreasing, linear or nonlinear). Sketch a graph that exhibits the qualitative features of a function that has been described verbally.

A0FEF4310A9D42F4AF5AF470C733FA3B.description: Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities. Determine the rate of change and initial value of the function from a description of a relationship or from two (x, y) values, including reading these from a table or from a graph. Interpret the rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models, and in terms of its graph or a table of values.

49EB0052B49A4C1AABFC09D817710534.description: Use functions to model relationships between quantities

D8EC25EAD7704B58B8365F676E3675A5.description: Interpret the equation y = mx + b as defining a linear function, whose graph is a straight line; give examples of functions that are not linear. (e.g., The function A = s² giving the area of a square as a function of its side length is not linear because its graph contains the points (1,1), (2,4) and (3,9), which are not on a straight line.)

319F95AE9DF54EBE9EB9ED146DBD35EA.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). (e.g., Given a linear function represented by a table of values and a linear function represented by an algebraic expression, determine which function has the greater rate of change.)

1AF815C71CE543868DE0AC938FDCDABB.description: Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output. The graph of a function is the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and the corresponding output.
comments: Instructional Note: Function notation is not required in grade 8.

18B63AC7EB9F4B43AE2089B09CFE9617.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to two linear equations in two variables. (e.g., Given coordinates for two pairs of points, determine whether the line through the first pair of points intersects the line through the second pair.)

6DCC77C43DAB4B1FB372DFA7518F9B97.description: Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables algebraically and estimate solutions by graphing the equations. Solve simple cases by inspection. (e.g., 3x + 2y = 5 and 3x + 2y = 6 have no solution because 3x + 2y cannot simultaneously be 5 and 6.)

1F196454CCE74794A0741B4F1726C5E6.description: Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables correspond to points of intersection of their graphs, because points of intersection satisfy both equations simultaneously.

7CAA26FB5E6744E1B644D93BE61E53E7.description: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

CB158967ABCB44CD96BD9BBCD077278A.description: Solve linear equations with rational number coefficients, including equations whose solutions require expanding expressions using the distributive property and collecting like terms.

E60C2AA1E9C749C08C25DBE552DCECEA.description: Give examples of linear equations in one variable with one solution, infinitely many solutions or no solutions. Show which of these possibilities is the case by successively transforming the given equation into simpler forms, until an equivalent equation of the form x = a, a = a, or a = b results (where a and b are different numbers).

55EC37A401E9461EBD2F3E825F6A97EE.description: Solve linear equations in one variable.

58AFD9EFD37C4F7A9C1B4A23D345C5A3.description: Analyze and solve linear equations and pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

A126CD41FCED4EB2B87B9174FE316BC4.description: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope m is the same between any two distinct points on a non-vertical line in the coordinate plane; derive the equation y = mx for a line through the origin and the equation y = mx + b for a line intercepting the vertical axis at b.

B5000F8827574A8BA89DEEF4DDA0C490.description: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope of the graph. Compare two different proportional relationships represented in different ways. (e.g., Compare a distance-time graph to a distance-time equation to determine which of two moving objects has greater speed.)

62B029611F7E45E783656DC0A4F5629B.description: Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear equations.

1F67CF91A1CE4182B9DD616CF04F1870.description: Perform operations with numbers expressed in scientific notation, including problems where both decimal and scientific notation are used. Use scientific notation and choose units of appropriate size for measurements of very large or very small quantities. (e.g., Use millimeters per year for seafloor spreading.) Interpret scientific notation that has been generated by technology.

9023B391B8094B33A5F02B8FBB7174A1.description: Use numbers expressed in the form of a single digit times an integer power of 10 to estimate very large or very small quantities, and to express how many times as much one is than the other. (e.g., Estimate the population of the United States as 3 × 10<sup>8</sup> and the population of the world as 7 × 10<sup>9</sup>, and determine that the world population is more than 20 times larger.)

81DC962BDF5542F995EEB8EB6D0D1975.description: Use square root and cube root symbols to represent solutions to equations of the form x² = p and x³ = p, where p is a positive rational number. Evaluate square roots of small perfect squares and cube roots of small perfect cubes. Know that √2 is irrational.

4321615C9F9C4B8287304DD626D6C103.description: Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions. (e.g., 3² × 3<sup>–5</sup> = 3<sup>–3</sup> = 1/3³ = 1/27.)

9B5845C0D3F640D89C13F1F25C6BE919.description: Work with radicals and integer exponents.

5EF96C4AA56044AF816BAC77CAF3B1C1.description: Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare the size of irrational numbers, locate them approximately on a number line diagram and estimate the value of expressions such as π². (e.g., By truncating the decimal expansion of √2, show that √2 is between 1 and 2, then between 1.4 and 1.5, and explain how to continue on to get better approximations.)

8219FCEDAD314F4093DEAA76B4CD2D52.description: Know that numbers that are not rational are called irrational. Understand informally that every number has a decimal expansion; for rational numbers show that the decimal expansion repeats eventually and convert a decimal expansion which repeats eventually into a rational number.
comments: Instructional Note: A decimal expansion that repeats the digit 0 is often referred to as a "terminating decimal."

79D3F207DE3440EAACAE387B54EFBDC1.description: Know that there are numbers that are not rational, and approximate them by rational numbers.

5026CF64B915449D99B87BDDF746C661.description: Know the formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders and spheres and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

01EBFB457A9A44FAB8B41FFF1FBFB8BE.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume of cylinders, cones, and spheres.

FB40690107EF4933952A762207B57268.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between two points in a coordinate system.

149DBBC3488F4065A11036015392F5E6.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to determine unknown side lengths in right triangles in real-world and mathematical problems in two and three dimensions.

FFCD02320C5145AF9101576FEFF0761C.description: Explain a proof of the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse.

8384EA8F182B41268859FF92FEE86CBC.description: Understand and apply the Pythagorean Theorem.

DE4B6BBFE21C4600BF1D4121E0C42774.description: Use informal arguments to establish facts about the angle sum and exterior angle of triangles, about the angles created when parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and the angle-angle criterion for similarity of triangles. (e.g., Arrange three copies of the same triangle so that the sum of the three angles appears to form a line, and give an argument in terms of transversals why this is so.)

FACFCC250DC546F28B8C7389FF428411.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is similar to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, translations and dilations; given two similar two dimensional figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the similarity between them.

C4AC907CA0EE45B88535DAB921676E88.description: Describe the effect of dilations, translations, rotations and reflections on two-dimensional figures using coordinates.

31B10BB6BF784BA8A2CFB920677A673C.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is congruent to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections and translations; given two congruent figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the congruence between them.

6DDDF91D26E14065837647A330974998.description: Parallel lines are taken to parallel lines.

BE3247B87DF847D588BEC3C340FD4415.description: Angles are taken to angles of the same measure.

A882C544E9494E20BC517D167FEADA81.description: Lines are taken to lines, and line segments to line segments of the same length.

3D4046580E39466DB7F3C1DD3D58A767.description: Verify experimentally the properties of rotations, reflections and translations:

E6F131BADF8842148DC41B6D07268A02.description: Understand congruence and similarity using physical models, transparencies, or geometry software.

A097978388E24F4A9D8DE042BA11DD89.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

20B1D8CC0EEE45D5AE3AA714376789AB.description: Look for and make use of structure.

D9DCDBBD5AF649798200B5327FD06DF1.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

CF7836CFF9C04C2FBA72DFEE003E6C35.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Mathematics

965999749D4A4ECDAC5465E4647F7A03.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, fourths and quarters and use the phrases half of, fourth of and quarter of. Describe the whole as two of, or four of the shares and understand for these examples that decomposing into more equal shares creates smaller shares.

91C3DF4493BB43F9970F96A226EECF65.description: Compose two-dimensional shapes (rectangles, squares, trapezoids, triangles, half-circles, and quarter-circles) or three-dimensional shapes (cubes, right rectangular prisms, right circular cones, and right circular cylinders) to create a composite shape and compose new shapes from the composite shape.
comments: Instructional Note: Students do not need to learn formal names such as, "right rectangular prism."

18146294563842C2B29A3269F321DBDE.description: Distinguish between defining attributes (e.g., triangles are closed and three-sided) versus non-defining attributes (e.g., color, orientation, and/or overall size); build and draw shapes to possess defining attributes.

283330ECB6614BC6BA5857DE3DED3F5B.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

D885BA8975B949CD80009FA80A9AC639.description: Organize, represent, interpret data with up to three categories; ask and answer questions about the total number of data points, how many in each category and how many more or less are in one category than in another.

9CD15086F15E432C98F4E27FE1CBD5D1.description: Tell and write time in hours and half-hours using analog and digital clocks.

E1A4AF048D0E4674A3F29646A14AADA5.description: Express the length of an object as a whole number of length units, by laying multiple copies of a shorter object (the length unit) end to end; understand that the length measurement of an object is the number of same-size length units that span it with no gaps or overlaps.
comments: Instructional Note: Limit to contexts where the object being measured is spanned by a whole number of length units with no gaps or overlaps.

2D8F6483A0EB411EB8A95148A7510F4A.description: Order three objects by length and compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object.

3C9CE96E5B9243488C5A92FA422AC36C.description: Measure lengths indirectly and by iterating length units.

6DA7CED0CF664248B131465532B6022B.description: Subtract multiples of 10 in the range 10-90 from multiples of 10 in the range 10-90 (positive or zero differences) using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction. Relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.

3E040151FE6147E3BB07D7360F1DD0B2.description: Given a two-digit number, mentally find 10 more or 10 less than the number, without having to count and explain the reasoning used.

C06E53532E7D431AB792EBD5D8B6D294.description:
Add within 100, including
  • adding a two-digit number and a one-digit number and adding a two-digit number and a multiple of 10,
  • using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.
Relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used. Understand that in adding two-digit numbers, one adds tens and tens, ones and ones, and sometimes it is necessary to compose a ten.

EA3BB99BBEAC4E89B72A8911AEECD87D.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.

DC6BB756AFA145E4BE353089BFE47C51.description: Compare two two-digit numbers based on meanings of the tens and ones digits, recording the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, and <.

D8CBB54ECD134A92A1B1A5EC8365EA45.description: The numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight or nine tens (and 0 ones).

AD8917471715461782EFFFB77A8186ED.description: The numbers from 11 to 19 are composed of a ten and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight or nine ones.

A3EDF02C813042FFBAF539A423A7B38C.description: 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones — called a "ten." (e.g., A group of ten pennies is equivalent to a dime.)

0FD5C873F76F4FEF917998F62691D3D1.description: Understand the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones. Understand the following as special cases:

355DB1176A03400D918E356C9FE5669A.description: Count to 120, starting at any number less than 120. In this range, read and write numerals and represent a number of objects with a written numeral.

6D3954E83E3540738D0E08C4CC89FCC3.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

9584BD64F2C546748DFBA63A098BDF3E.description: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating three whole numbers (e.g., Determine the unknown number that makes the equation true in each of the equations. 8 + ? = 11, 5 = ? – 3, 6 + 6 = ?).

EE9CFE9DDE6B463892BCBA1DB71F05B7.description: Understand the meaning of the equal sign, and determine if equations involving addition and subtraction are true or false (e.g., Which of the following equations are true and which are false? 6 = 6, 7 = 8 – 1, 5 + 2 = 2 + 5, 4 + 1 = 5 + 2).

1A76B457747D4CE987F6CBCF0E3201D0.description: Work with addition and subtraction equations.

8549D80691BF47A1812D682B168AC831.description:
Add and subtract within 20, demonstrating fluency for addition and subtraction within 10 and use strategies such as
  • counting on;
  • making ten (e.g., 8 + 6 = 8 + 2 + 4 = 10 + 4 = 14);
  • decomposing a number leading to a ten (e.g., 13 – 4 = 13 – 3 – 1 = 10 – 1 = 9);
  • using the relationship between addition and subtraction (e.g., knowing that 8 + 4 = 12, one knows 12 – 8= 4); and
  • creating equivalent but easier or known sums (e.g., adding 6 +7 by creating the known equivalent 6 + 6 + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13).

2FF1F47632C34124900A72D8352CD7AE.description: Relate counting to addition and subtraction (e.g., by counting on 2 to add 2).

F14D0B1E64FF43E6B3F0443690856B53.description: Understand subtraction as an unknown-addend problem (e.g., subtract 10 – 8 by finding the number that makes 10 when added to 8).

44DD79BEA98F48439615659EDD994462.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract (e.g., If 8 + 3 = 11 is known, then 3 + 8 = 11 is also known: Commutative Property of Addition. To add 2 + 6 + 4, the second two numbers can be added to make a ten, so 2 + 6 + 4 = 2 + 10 = 12: Associative Property of Addition).
comments: Instructional Note: Students need not use formal terms for these properties.

A9DCC89A453B40AA937F3DBFEA12E78A.description: Understand and apply properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

C2D51F444B8847389DEC20084BE243E8.description: Solve word problems that call for addition of three whole numbers whose sum is less than or equal to 20 (e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem).

27580BDA18AE411BA3413AD8F5C2D988.description: Use addition and subtraction within 20 to solve word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions (e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem).

67398E01A69F493E9D5069572204B1C7.description: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.

BD95B444A95D4851BC26138558CE9141.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

C819CD2717A14868963DFBC13160585A.description: Look for and make use of structure.

862D4C2F063E4F33992ACA62E2A7C9D3.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

72BE0586878442A8811B98176E1DA28A.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Library Media Content Standards and Objectives for West Virginia Schools

C791B50F8822466EB9102EE0684C34CD.description: review work group projects and suggest improvements.

DA9F3A9A68124B2CB1AC081B802F7979.description: develop of workgroup roles and responsibilities.

51F90E9DE976474EAE570AC24639BDF8.description: explain the need for privacy of personal information.

79ABC5EABC144CE494B8A1BC9CFF43CC.description: discuss legal principles and ethical conduct to use of information (e.g., copyright, plagiarism, acceptable use policy).

2894B526BFE84FB4BA2846E2D7F11E72.description: recognize the role if intellectual freedom.

3A4853938F944A6C81EDCAF67C6E7A75.description:
Students will develop social responsibility and contribute positively to the learning community and society by
  • being information literate and recognizing the importance of information to a democratic society;
  • practicing ethical behavior in regard to information and information technology;
  • participating effectively in groups to pursue and generate information.

EB2518279EAB4D7482ECB6FD2D184383.description: identify topics suitable for independent learning or in-depth exploration.

E306FE21611A4126B6B2E900CA766F04.description: read, compare and contrast award-winning selections (e.g. Caldecott, Newbery, and WV Children's Book Award).

0450A06A3223473D801797CB491F8E04.description: identify WV authors and illustrators and examine and read their works.

080A5D1894CB40FCBF2061689F259088.description: compare, contrast and read a variety of classic and contemporary literature from appropriate genres (e.g., fiction, nonfiction, poetry, tall tales, biography, folk tales, fairy tales, legends).

2E828AFDBF58430C9FA3069A9FD13B23.description: recommend an author or topic of personal interest.

F8135A2E089E4E0BBF77268655EC7CE9.description: use features of the Dewey Decimal System to locate materials.

7D52BF70FDFE4CD5B460C9BCFE77768E.description: analyze appropriate behaviors of good library citizenship, including rules of behavior and proper use and treatment of print materials and electronic resources.

CF418B9BFD19433D85B68A0BF56A955B.description: utilize the automated or print catalog to locate books by author, title, and subject, and keyword.

33AC09E9F5D44E7A9D3CDD1133A7A27D.description: apply knowledge of the school library media center arrangement and procedures.

C41ADD6FCC0C4220A1EBDFE739DEA122.description:
Students will become independent learners by
  • being information literate and pursuing information related to personal interests;
  • appreciating literature and other creative expressions of information;
  • striving for excellence in information seeking and knowledge generation.

1E109DC315A6422F81EDE1E5EAA6BCB5.description: take notes on a topic, recording key words and phrases and summarizing.

84CB2145D6074444AB1DBC00D710C611.description: select information for accuracy, validity, relevance, appropriateness, comprehensiveness, and bias.

32A2AFD0C925477A8DFB187E5AA66488.description: explain the components of a bibliographic record (e.g., call number, author, title, publisher, copyright date, number of pages).

0AF53461F3144AA3A2C1B18905884526.description: interpret information to answer questions, draw conclusions, offer solutions, clarify issues, make predictions, and generate further questions.

2E082DDBD49E454F8DA1FEBB0E6B7EF3.description: select and access print, non-print, and electronic resources to locate different types of information (e.g., newspaper, dictionary, encyclopedia, atlas, magazines, almanac, thesaurus, CD-ROM and the Internet).

FB74E99030154D49A4D4675ABFD7944D.description: demonstrate organizational features of printed text (e.g., title page, table of contents, glossary, and index).

BDCC9DC1E5344D39B1CD292AFD400482.description:
Students will become information literate by
  • accessing information efficiently and effectively;
  • evaluating information critically and competently;
  • using information accurately and creatively.

document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for English Language Arts

A980BF070A5F4392896747855A7C3FC8.description: Acquire and accurately use grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases; gather vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

E4289BE13ED7472BB2ADAB0EEB6BF3E0.description: Distinguish among the connotations (associations) of words with similar denotations (definitions) (e.g., bullheaded, willful, firm, persistent, or resolute).

B1E9F9DCE67E4F61A26A236A8E7D328A.description: Use the relationship between particular words to better understand each of the words.

17DD646BB2294036A20F63894A08E626.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g. verbal irony, and/or puns) in context.

10B2E37AB0E54C439F063A76802A27D4.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

7D33B518421B47E38E8939C1C5C07DB5.description: Verify the initial determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

8291117FF3204BDDB27F46A93547357F.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, and/or thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning or its part of speech.

43B8FD549D40418C862B032A27B05509.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., precede, recede, or secede).

14C02362CDC944D0A19B696F9F8F9087.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph or a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

B968B4535CA94C8BBB2620D304386766.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words or phrases based on grade 8 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

BFBE6B362E704E2AA53831310691B84B.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in verb voice and mood.

40E540CA174B4102832053EB20FAF2E1.description: Use verbs in the indicative, imperative, interrogative, conditional and subjunctive mood to achieve particular effects (e.g., expressing uncertainty or describing a state contrary to fact).

E8BA4E89ACF24F21ACA8F9FDBC64A622.description: Use verbs in the active and passive voice (e.g., emphasizing the actor or the action).

3AC88D61B27D4869BDBE7012DDF044F1.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

AF7A4C1DA4BA495BAD7F6D64568D48D2.description: Use an ellipsis to indicate an omission.

802301C6496743C5BE8884722D4FEB05.description: Use punctuation (comma, ellipsis, or dash) to indicate a pause or break.

1D83762CF39E496F9C1A13FB0BC9B62C.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

6B2BE3199FE645D1AD4B25AC8C239DD7.description: Explain the function of verbals (gerunds, participles, and infinitives) in general and their function in particular sentences.

270E97AF45404CA0BA9E002DC7020FD8.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

81C9317FDBA34153A65F747A6F52D285.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate. (See grade 8 Language standards for specific expectations.)

42979BAE5775439DA05158F1A85E1F95.description: Integrate multimedia and visual displays into presentations to clarify information, strengthen claims and evidence, and add interest.

5512502BD48048C89BF61D522396B17E.description: Present claims and findings, emphasizing significant points in a focused, coherent manner with relevant evidence, sound, valid reasoning, and well-chosen details; use appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, and clear pronunciation.

4B916E55669A43CFB54BFDC7411655B1.description: Delineate a speaker's argument and specific claims, evaluating the soundness of the reasoning and relevance and sufficiency of the evidence; identify when irrelevant evidence is introduced.

4D55CA7EB45A4AE28EB70E80FAA94A23.description: Analyze the purpose of information presented in diverse media and formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, and/or orally) and evaluate the motives (e.g., social, commercial, or political) behind its presentation.

8900C69DBC9F4BC4BC13AEB419C09043.description: Acknowledge new information expressed by others and, when warranted, qualify or justify views in light of the evidence presented.

549A64EDD2D74DEBB48AA8742C3224E1.description: Pose questions that connect the ideas of several speakers and respond to others' questions and comments with relevant evidence, observations, and ideas.

0B4A9D4F0A8D48E18A5BAB72DE691F59.description: Follow rules for collegial discussions and decision-making, track progress toward specific goals and deadlines, and define individual roles as needed.

25CBB964D83047388B60B8BEF7535442.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence on the topic, text, or issue to probe and reflect on ideas under discussion.

96F94BE428FC43269A38F490862BFFFD.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 8 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing ideas clearly.

46CD608A3A1E45DF9786319A2A71B798.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

CCEAA055F1ED426C8C9C26B9F9E68CE2.description: Apply grade 8 Reading standards to nonfiction and other informational texts (e.g., "Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient; recognize when irrelevant evidence is introduced").

F1D6EEAA6B314AF79CCE9BD92DBB5CE6.description: Apply grade 8 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Analyze how a modern work of fiction draws on themes, patterns of events, or character types from myths, traditional stories, or religious works, such as the Bible, including describing how the material is transformed in the modern work (e.g., how a modern interpretation of a Shakespearean text draws from the original text)").

E2D8C208E99C4E3FA57F068797F6ADB5.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

991AD33103394459AB5548E83EE5FFDE.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, using search terms effectively; assess the credibility and accuracy of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation (e.g., MLA or APA).

8C10FB172D1B4E988AFBE473193DDE93.description: Conduct short research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question), drawing on several sources and generating additional related, focused questions that allow for multiple avenues of exploration.

9E1D1EE23E424587B1CAC8A5CD65E3FB.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

EC250F1F8B4B4813A683DA4BC51CC0FE.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing, present the relationships between information and ideas efficiently, and interact and collaborate with others.

5E49893A75704DBDA16496F727190CED.description: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on how well purpose and audience have been addressed. (Editing for conventions should demonstrate command of the Language standards up to and including grade 8.)

55DD4ACFBBB040D5809F5B99DE3E9F18.description: Use a variety of transition words, phrases, and clauses to convey sequence, signal shifts from one time frame or setting to another, and show the relationships among experiences and events.

88745B8DE5474BAA91E9F40838DD9A60.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, and reflection, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

B5D5F62B13E245E985706729A9B985F0.description: Engage and orient the reader by establishing a context and point of view and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally and logically.

8CED9D2C5164441288A17C41E127F000.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, relevant descriptive details, and well-structured event sequences.

C0098B11B6B9424ABBE0FA895F50F39A.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented.

83CA35909D1D45FFA23FBFFE7AEA7A1D.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

6489DF7A36F2440CAA978B99F577C4D1.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

33FC6CD40C71405EB6EA19EE015C908B.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.

A47EF92A6A724D81AF47AD613159EE25.description: Develop the topic with relevant, well-chosen facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.

E8F4FA051699496FA23039B4B1A29DE6.description: Introduce a topic clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts, and information into broader categories; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts or tables), and multimedia when useful to aid comprehension.

10C0F58517B540BD952BDCD169991A40.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts, and information through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content.

8292CAC3F8604F97BF7EC72FFAF738AF.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

EAB0363A3C624D268BD42A726A839F28.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

C00BDA13BC214902872DF38CA15B8CD7.description: Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant evidence, using accurate, credible sources and demonstrating an understanding of the topic or text.

2296E3BE9CFB4928B92923ADEF6FAAD4.description: Introduce claim(s), acknowledge and distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and organize the reasons and evidence logically.

6F53D1898A6E48FC9417C126C66953CB.description: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.

58B0F55FB32B499883ADC2E6877F2112.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend nonfiction and other informational texts at the high end of the grades 6–8 text complexity range independently and proficiently.

00CD5B7F256C4FC4863B3A90B140C2F2.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, at the high end of grades 6–8 text complexity range independently and proficiently.
