DF17B53B8A694F50BE6257A96CB3D33E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in an informational text, assessing whether the reasoning is sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient; recognize when irrelevant evidence is introduced.

C3BBA29052814E5780E4A708D7A6C249.description: Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of using different mediums (e.g., print or digital text, video, and/or multimedia) to present a particular topic or idea.

FF4F401E5A97462492F511724998F7A9.description: Analyze how a modern work of fiction draws on themes, patterns of events, or character types from myths, traditional stories, or religious works, such as the Bible, including describing how the material is transformed in the modern work (e.g., how a modern interpretation of a Shakespearean text draws from the original text).

DF18B9BC9388490D83EE201F05651BBF.description: Analyze the extent to which a filmed or live production of a story or drama stays faithful to or departs from the text or script, evaluating the choices made by the director or actors.

57D96A0B67F142F0B4A834989458CF3A.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in an informational text and analyze how the author acknowledges and responds to conflicting evidence or viewpoints.

22A28D51FF9B4A2D916EA49BE5F787CE.description: Analyze in detail the structure of a specific paragraph in an informational text, including the role of particular sentences in developing and refining a key concept.

451455E4A56A4312AC7749981681D924.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in an informational text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including analogies or allusions to other texts.

F7E5A99D6EFB45F5BDC4D0FF49320765.description: Analyze how differences in the points of view of the characters and the audience or reader (e.g., created through the use of dramatic irony) create such effects as suspense or humor in a literary text.

6C68F4E4B67B4ACC9369994649A58AFE.description: Compare and contrast the structure of two or more literary texts and analyze how the differing structure of each text contributes to its meaning and style.

BE281B3C6AC740C79B0560B1ACAB0ED4.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a literary text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including analogies or allusions to other texts.

48EE24E9ACC14791ABC9849C82C8F2AA.description: Analyze how an informational text makes connections among and distinctions between individuals, ideas, or events (e.g., through comparisons, analogies, or categories).

28DD5C2EB5FB49F684B1B9DB016825D9.description: Determine a central idea of an informational text and analyze its development over the course of the text, including its relationship to supporting ideas; provide an objective summary of the text.

EBA39A7335804B2891A865ADAC6D58B3.description: Cite the textual evidence that most strongly supports an analysis of what the informational text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

403D675A714D43D09E8497E03AF685B3.description: Analyze how particular lines of dialogue or incidents in a story or drama propel the action, reveal aspects of a character, or provoke a decision.

10A1D3CA00CC4F3F90D7A6A653036F50.description: Determine a theme or central idea of a literary text and analyze its development over the course of the text, including its relationship to the characters, setting, and plot; provide an objective summary of the text.

F9DFA399C7C043F9955D9FCD59DDE234.description: Cite the textual evidence that most strongly supports an analysis of what the literary text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for English Language Arts

BA9BF136C0DD427FA28A6836251E14EF.description: Acquire and accurately use general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college- and career-readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

70B5F9510CA44B7FB109C3A7106C1C52.description: Analyze nuances in the meaning of words with similar denotations.

A63B80CE687A47AB979A7E9A8BFDD078.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., euphemism or oxymoron) in context and analyze their role in the text.

884808C288D645C8998D4DB73344310A.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

312FB3F331224E4B9730F86720C4B744.description: Verify the initial determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

8B155BC344FC4EB29C5E5A9919C5B7B1.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, and/or thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning, part of speech, or etymology.

10FD390FC88B400FA0773CB8CDF41120.description: Identify and correctly use patterns of word changes that indicate different meanings or parts of speech (e.g., analyze, analysis, analytical, advocate, or advocacy).

9CA1E2EBAE074C26BDE205D8907A7FD0.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence, paragraph or text or a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

F056D157522C40F9AE5797F6E6087DD0.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 10 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

EB81A7DA814747ACB4B9509024A54039.description: Write and edit work so that it conforms to the guidelines in a style manual (e.g., MLA Handbook or APA Handbook) appropriate for the discipline and writing type.

7920999A936D4130B377B04FECFB8E4A.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

21F7F4347614410FB60742AC4472FB03.description: Use a colon to introduce a list or quotation.

85B9443DB37C4ED38BEBAD66B762A047.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

B95267EB8AF146DD8575FBA86A524B40.description: Use various types of phrases (noun, verb, adjectival, adverbial, participial, prepositional, or absolute) and clauses (independent and dependent; noun, relative, and adverbial) to convey specific meanings and add variety and interest to writing or presentations.

09CB1BD7417F4600A594B0AB04EE33D6.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

057D2397E1F24E55A7BCEAC520B08067.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate. (See grade 10 Language standards for specific expectations.)

FC404B649A144675BEB9E0E0ABA20E2D.description: Make strategic use of digital media (e.g., textual, graphical, audio, visual, and interactive elements) in presentations to enhance understanding of findings, reasoning, and evidence and to add interest.

5AA24326025D4722A356A786D4B4C3DA.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence, conveying a clear and distinct perspective, such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, substance, and style are appropriate to purpose, audience, and task.

792C12A4365D4C858F517764F5644146.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric, assessing any fallacious reasoning or exaggerated or distorted evidence.

D50F644658FD4EEAAA53EB907A9CB3FD.description: Integrate multiple sources of information presented in diverse media or formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, and/or orally), evaluating the credibility and accuracy of each source in order to make decisions and solve problems.

AE7E1DACA19D40729F2ED2EF680221B0.description: Respond thoughtfully to diverse perspectives; analyze points of agreement and disagreement and, when warranted, qualify or justify views and understanding and make new connections in light of the evidence and reasoning presented.

A38BAABEE8264B0D940514AF5626450C.description: Propel conversations by posing and responding to questions that relate the current discussion to broader themes or larger ideas; actively incorporate others' perspectives into the discussion; and clarify, verify, or challenge ideas and conclusions.

796CCA0E92FF435FBB492627847C74F1.description: Work with peers to set rules for democratic, collegial discussions and decision-making (e.g., informal consensus, taking votes on key issues, presentation of alternate views); establish clear goals, deadlines, and individual roles as needed.

14269E0856574965B657CE2F23F99A43.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read and researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence from texts and other research on the topic or issue to stimulate a thoughtful, well-reasoned exchange of ideas.

ACB6ECD1661C42EAAAA0E6D5C08B748E.description: Initiate and effectively participate in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 10 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing ideas clearly and persuasively.

843C92A939494CF09DCB607AFC565729.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

5BFFAE4F77C84BA1BB8411F842A08AB9.description: Apply grade 10 Reading standards to nonfiction and other informational texts (e.g., "Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is valid and the evidence is relevant and sufficient; identify false statements and fallacious reasoning").

663BA9D343224F9F90A52064ACE28A1C.description: Apply grade 10 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Analyze how an author draws on and transforms source material in a specific work [e.g., how Shakespeare treats a theme or topic from Ovid or the Bible or how a later author draws on a play by Shakespeare]").

32C72743CC884F1EA82EB4889909AD4C.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

018ED44E54214752BA48C56FD2445660.description: Gather relevant information from multiple authoritative print and digital sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the usefulness of each source in terms of task, purpose, and audience and in answering the research question; integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation (e.g., MLA or APA).

E94F8B8F116A4A8C83A096239C7C5946.description: Conduct short, as well as more sustained, research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

A055109AEEF84713AC2BD7594D21B558.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

A50BE6BC6E0C428A93D9FFE40A211136.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products, taking advantage of technology's capacity to link to other information and to display information flexibly and dynamically in response to ongoing feedback.

8B2F8FCCBE6A41B5969237A523FD3C3F.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience. (Editing for conventions should demonstrate command of all Language standards up to and including grade 10.)

E66E949777874BE189702AA4895D1EDC.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in Text Types and Purposes.)

F29476C914E140AEB888BAD31F49DC21.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on what is experienced, observed, or resolved over the course of the narrative.

7C9F2D640A3A4AB7A859EDB2BAA6CCED.description: Use precise words and phrases, effective details, and sensory language to convey a vivid picture of the experiences, events, setting, and/or characters.

6BA4088A56EB4B80B6D118DC4DD6D9CF.description: Use a variety of techniques to sequence events so that they build on one another to create a coherent whole and build upon a particular outcome.

FF8A1DFCBB8F480AADFA3904AA9E1011.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple plot lines, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

D7618FC2ED5C40D5A4211EE95524E03A.description: Engage and orient the reader by setting out a problem, situation, or observation, establishing one or multiple point(s) of view and introducing a narrator and/or characters; create a smooth progression of experiences or events.

A400AA04FAA449B2B1AAC7EC53EAA798.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

5656AB60394F4D7B868BDE6388C8A609.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

32AEA118D7334FE0B539177CDD3398A3.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline.

27E48794D27A494AA664F2F6572475D5.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to manage the complexity of the topic.

A80B9AC9FCA94B55BE8AD91A1ED085F0.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.

3795C3AA60FC4DCF88EDED98C395B720.description: Develop the topic with well-chosen, relevant, significant, and sufficient facts; extended definitions; concrete details, quotations, or other information; and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.

7BC77025BE2D4534819578F746CE6B29.description: Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, and information to analyze important connections and distinctions; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures and/or tables), and multimedia when useful to aid comprehension.

4AF09C9C99F6422CA80B48EFE9B1FF87.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

FCDF81DDEF844245B60725875B3038C5.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

967D91A6360347349B67084DBE2CAFBA.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline.

13E1A0D7050E4B20BC6250111BFF782A.description: Use a variety of words, phrases, and clauses to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence and between claim(s) and counterclaims.

878D096BAA474ACAABC31D8C05856031.description: Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly, supplying relevant evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level and concerns.

49A2230B06D142DFAF3AC98D34DAD341.description: Introduce precise, knowledgeable claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that establishes clear relationships among claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

DB0965D9C3D24C89A7A611464E5B3BBB.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

8EB75F3404FF4B409D501B64106755D3.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend nonfiction and other informational texts, independently and proficiently, at the high end of the grade 9-10 text complexity range.

9A5E13DFE7034F60B0866B479B07854A.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, independently and proficiently, at the high end of the grade 9-10 text complexity range.

9F819C20EE3D44DCB7B9AE57F0B9A9C4.description: Range of Reading and Text Complexity

D260623E7D144249A9B596F970D36EF9.description: Analyze and defend influential U.S. documents of historical and literary significance (e.g. Roosevelt's Four Freedoms speech or King's "Letter from Birmingham Jail"), including how they address related themes and concepts.

6D6E6D3C44B44E439A53EA6B97B6EE2C.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims and counterclaims in an informational text, assessing whether the reasoning is valid and the evidence is relevant and sufficient; identify false statements and fallacious reasoning.

75A4E2576C4446DAAEB70F47BD6747E9.description: Analyze and defend various accounts of a subject told in different mediums of informational texts (e.g., a person's life story in both print and multimedia), determining which details are emphasized in each account.

5020A661FAB54AAA9B05EC98E4E37874.description: Analyze and defend how an author draws on and transforms source material in a specific literary work (e.g., how Shakespeare treats a theme or topic from Ovid or the Bible, or how a later author draws on a play by Shakespeare).

E6F19005AA924CA0B82D50582CCB5187.description: Analyze the representation, in a literary text, of a subject or a key scene in two or more different artistic mediums, including what is emphasized or absent in each treatment and why (e.g., Auden's "Musée des Beaux Arts" and Breughel's Landscape with the Fall of Icarus).

AA8242E6B450436FA2655A94A3483A7F.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in an informational text and evaluate how the author uses rhetoric to advance that point of view or purpose.

00AFF2F1C0BC491CBB39E5C4E1FD9088.description: Analyze and defend in detail how an author's ideas or claims are developed and refined by particular sentences, paragraphs, or larger portions of an informational text (e.g., a section or chapter).

17FDF365FDB14693940C8C0EE3ABC5AB.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in an informational text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze and defend the cumulative impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone (e.g. how the language of a court opinion differs from that of a newspaper).

ABE760DF34084FC98E6BF676DFFE1B2E.description: Analyze and defend a particular point of view or cultural experience reflected in a work of literature from outside the United States, drawing on a wide reading of world literature.

38D8FEC1594B438E8C3FF01A344B45F2.description: Analyze how an author's choices concerning how to structure a literary text, order events within it (e.g., parallel plots), and manipulate time (e.g., pacing or flashbacks) contribute to its overall structure and create such effects as mystery, tension, or surprise.

7034A59147F5443788678B43AAE92354.description: Determine the meaning of multiple-meaning words and phrases as they are used in a literary text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the cumulative impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone (e.g., how the language evokes a sense of time and place or how it sets a formal or informal tone).

1572A83F9C8248CA81392BB8F47F9D1B.description: Analyze how the author unfolds an analysis or series of complex ideas or events in informational texts, including the order in which the points are made, how they are developed, and how they interact.

FC0606956A924E8B90D22AD85248CBD1.description: Determine two central ideas of an informational text and analyze their development over the course of the informational text, including how they emerge and are shaped and refined by specific details; provide an objective summary of the informational text.

D3464F43C6174E46B328D11B3A4E1BC9.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the informational text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the informational text, recognizing when the text leaves matters uncertain.

273341BFF30E468993215BE1524863C4.description: Analyze how complex characters (e.g., those with multiple or conflicting motivations) develop over the course of a literary text, interact with other characters, and affect the plot or develop the theme.

361248F9301942F3A729A3B4B364BC9C.description: Determine two themes or central ideas of a literary text and analyze in detail their development over the course of the literary text, including how they emerge and are shaped and refined by specific details; provide an objective summary of the literary text.

9E6BE70694D84A11B863072A76B510A0.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the literary text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, recognizing when the text leaves matters uncertain.

document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Mathematics

C06818AE01E94B13ABA2425D8E2AD594.description: Understand statistics as a process for making inferences about population parameters based on a random sample from that population.

FD9D711238034CB48D7DCBC8C9166DBC.description: Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments

814A60C98CD04F638FC73D0CDB11D361.description: Computer (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.

E1236F0258464089951B6AC81204D0ED.description: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).

75E3678E8DA44F318E57B7500CC69060.description: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.

D2A97E2DDCA54BFEBDD7B02AF98FC410.description: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, and box plots).

5B272A2108484D58A72A0C6E8E0162BC.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.

5A800B25BAC345338619862C31253364.description: Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data.

FD6365C22E96406FA7833E84A8F60746.description: Know that straight lines are widely used to model relationships between two quantitative variables. For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line, and informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

B4B13F1291D245F3B08BE214F2D5A932.description: Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in the context of the data.

03EDC2F1F9894F9DB79A9A7281D0E03F.description: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related. Interpret linear models.

0FEEC68F6D29493496558365BFA109E5.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables.

026FEA7C14734D719009727EEC9C1293.description: Statistics and Probability - Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data

CB7CB5230721411898E08537A465CEFA.description: Apply geometric methods to solve design problems (e.g., designing an object or structure to satisfy physical constraints or minimize cost; working with topographic grid systems based on ratios).

7DEFDC3085104EF1BCB59338B346F644.description: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations.

638B66DF051C45CB95408CA4979C1D3D.description: Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and rectangles, (e.g., using the distance formula).

B39BCAB1D8874C42A820ECCF367E12A9.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.
comments: For example, prove or disprove that a figure defined by four given points in the coordinate plane is a rectangle; prove or disprove that the point (1, √3) lies on the circle centered at the origin and containing the point (0, 2).

69E51DD56A684550B229559B44C264ED.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically

0C08AFF393774023A0365AEADC7CBFDB.description: Geometry – Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations

5CF0BC0651054502A72BC551CE1B4E37.description: Give an informal argument using Cavalieri's principle for the formulas for the volume of a sphere and other solid figures.

A5A25FEFEF6B466B940ADB040E072998.description: Give an informal argument for the formulas for the circumference of a circle, area of a circle, volume of a cylinder, pyramid, and cone. Use dissection arguments, Cavalieri's principle, and informal limit arguments.

comments: For example, if T(y) is the temperature in the atmosphere as a function of height, and h(t) is the height of a weather balloon as a function of time, then T(h(t)) is the temperature at the location of the weather balloon as a function of time.

document.title: Library Media Content Standards and Objectives for West Virginia Schools

62EC1C870CF74480B8DA7FEAB1304274.description: develop information and ideas orally and in simple written sentences, and prepare a group media product (e.g., class alphabet book, class fact book).

6521E46687F14F7B9CB388FE4CE2E9C0.description: recognize the importance of free and open access to information for everyone.

0507223C1EE2498EBCA4967AB3FE83E1.description:
Students will develop social responsibility and contribute positively to the learning community and society by
  • being information literate and recognizing the importance of information to a democratic society;
  • practicing ethical behavior in regard to information and information technology;
  • participating effectively in groups to pursue and generate information.

0BB47EF700F242728B7D77170DBD38DB.description: recognize and read a variety of literature including award-winning selections (e.g. Caldecott Award).

6F8F9867984D41AB88136AB3F74D1E2D.description: state favorite authors and topics of personal interest.

A010D37464364925A95F36346B111602.description: identify various genre of literature (e.g., folklore, fairy tales, poetry, fiction and nonfiction).

3EB4188087874F5A97EBD2BA6F931339.description: describe story elements (e.g. setting, plot, characters and theme), make simple predictions, and recall specific details from print, visual, and auditory materials.

A607BB60C60648D1A2D716F417CAF516.description: describe good library citizenship including rules of behavior and proper use and treatment of print materials and electronic resources.

0071CA4397DC4C5B9CFC23C22C606C9B.description: apply knowledge of alphabetical order to locate books in appropriate sections and use checkout procedures.

ED34756068764A228D9775EB7B9787EB.description: explain the location and organization of materials in the library media center (LMC).

0E7E623A180D4A9C889BC430ED043A2F.description:
Students will become independent learners by
  • being information literate and pursuing information related to personal interests;
  • appreciating literature and other creative expressions of information;
  • striving for excellence in information seeking and knowledge generation.

500084601284404E890BE59FA61CA12E.description: identify print, non-print and electronic resources (e.g. books, newspapers, magazines, dictionaries, CD-ROMs and the Internet).

7578888D560F4B6F85FE2C3BC93B1C92.description: identify parts of a book (e.g. title page and table of contents).

CCC2E746F6E047C2A9F738614B8DA654.description:
Students will become information literate by
  • accessing information efficiently and effectively;
  • evaluating information critically and competently;
  • using information accurately and creatively.

F99E3442A61A4CEBB972ECF5C8D224F8.description: Create Equations that describe number or relationships.

document.title: Next Generation Standards and Objectives for Science in West Virginia Schools

3727EDB0DA81428C8EF48348FA5F71C0.description: write routinely over extended time frames (time for reflection and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

1BBADB803DDF4F03919D8BF79EF5D42B.description: conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem and narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

4C2E0973DD4E4B1892E18C54964DB229.description: develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.

108C29BA95B748FB821D16466A99F9B0.description: produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization and style are appropriate to task, purpose and audience.

19101E52F28B44A794C11D8F5D8F12B4.description: Writing - Production and Distribution of Writing

C2FCDC5426C54F0F8D6FB38B935B72BD.description:
write informative/explanatory texts, including the narration of historical events, scientific procedures/experiments, or technical processes:
  • introduce a topic and organize ideas, concepts, and information to make important connections and distinctions; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g. figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.
  • develop the topic with well-chosen, relevant and sufficient facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.
  • use varied transitions and sentence structures to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.
  • use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to manage the complexity of the topic and convey a style appropriate to the discipline and context as well as to the expertise of likely readers.
  • establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.
  • provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

448424E7BE2C4E519B5193F842348E5E.description:
write arguments focused on discipline-specific content:
  • introduce precise claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims and create an organization that establishes clear relationships among the claim(s), counterclaims, reasons and evidence.
  • develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly, supplying data and evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both claim(s) and counterclaims in a discipline-appropriate form and in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level and concerns.
  • use words, phrases and clauses to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence and between claim(s) and counterclaims.
  • establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.
  • provide a concluding statement or section that follows from or supports the argument presented.

document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for English Language Arts

211CDC8D3D0C41D08BD4B205145BDCB4.description: Acquire and accurately use general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, sufficient for reading, writing, speaking and listening at the college- and career-readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

DAF1CC519A25443E9AF6EAC1CBEEFE19.description: Verify the initial determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

3011F6E7FE67432EADB235EA805B820D.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning, its part of speech, its etymology or its standard usage.

7709CA088CEB4F22BC32B1EDB433C67F.description: Identify and correctly use patterns of word changes that indicate different meanings or parts of speech (e.g., conceive, conception, conceivable).

41C50DDBE19D43C689FF450C609FE80F.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence, paragraph or text; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

44D2722629FA442984DA3576AE4C171C.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 12 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

EC5BE79188CF41DB8A8A182E476CC996.description: Vary syntax for effect, consulting references (e.g., Tufte's Artful Sentences) for guidance as needed; apply an understanding of syntax to the study of complex texts when reading.

BF5141C2C3354879BE36BB3FBC8D95E7.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

8CDC7D48441B488598D204EAFEEFE91A.description: Resolve issues of complex or contested usage, consulting references (e.g., Merriam-Webster's Dictionary of English Usage or Garner's Modern American Usage) as needed.

8DF25C84325346459511B6DA44011DBE.description: Apply the understanding that usage is a matter of convention, can change over time and is sometimes contested.

4AC32D72873C4011865077BED1AED085.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

6DDB466FD4704CE6A0BB935454D1C39D.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating a command of formal English when indicated or appropriate. (See Transition English Language Arts Language standards for specific expectations.)

7FEE594114214B4390A724FB298D2EBC.description: Make strategic use of digital media (e.g., textual, graphical, audio, visual, and interactive elements) in presentations to enhance understanding of findings, reasoning, and evidence and to add interest.

C6FA6B09C86C4F1796B8AC4BED6CDBEA.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence, conveying a clear and distinct perspective, such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning; address alternative or opposing perspectives, and determine if the organization, development, substance, and style are appropriate to purpose, audience, and a range of formal and informal tasks.

0D08EFED4E3A4087AB7FA5DF48EB1CB8.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric, assessing the stance, premises, links among ideas, word choice, points of emphasis, and tone used.

6CC041580CAC4AD69D3EBE58AC75B166.description: Integrate multiple sources of information presented in diverse formats and media (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) in order to make informed decisions and solve problems, evaluating the credibility and accuracy of each source and noting any discrepancies among the data.

410D10E57B5C4573B9DDE39F0B1F0C35.description: Respond thoughtfully to diverse perspectives; synthesize comments, claims, and evidence made on all sides of an issue; resolve contradictions when possible; and determine what additional information or research is required to deepen the investigation or complete the task.

6044F94FCE4347F69304728186AB7118.description: Propel conversations by posing and responding to questions that probe reasoning and evidence; ensure a hearing for a full range of positions on a topic or issue; clarify, verify, or challenge ideas and conclusions; and promote divergent and creative perspectives.

CCECAD33986C4DDB8727CE520AA4CD5D.description: Work with peers to promote civil, democratic discussions and decision-making; set clear goals and deadlines, and establish individual roles as needed.

69FEFF9D799C4C23874B2B5288DC6D03.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read and researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence from texts and other research on the topic or issue to stimulate a thoughtful, well-reasoned exchange of ideas.

AF7742D80BD543BF97DED6D7AFD30300.description: Initiate and effectively participate in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 12 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing ideas clearly and persuasively.

F51FD0157D5647169DEF47F63D5ECA7C.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

F8431281CCCE49F8BE912D3A5CDDA05B.description: Apply Transition English Language Arts for Seniors Reading standards to nonfiction and other informational texts.

ED4144EB962F44E0B78A792D391EB517.description: Apply Transition English Language Arts for Seniors Reading standards to literature.

75551597A8A94C87B4190327203CC937.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

4FEE6774565E4566BD11E2A26FF9621C.description: Gather relevant information from multiple authoritative print and digital sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the strengths and limitations of each source in terms of the task, purpose, and audience; integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and overreliance on any one source and following a standard format for citation.

E672BA4E69CC41AD8FC5904247AD4F9B.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

EFEB6227A558456DB6CF6589D4A0C572.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

DD127074F7634F97BADC571B3860828F.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.

6749D43D2DBB42A7BA06241BB67CC21A.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in Text Types and Purposes.)

5E3A2FD4D8734155A7DAB90016F26FCE.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on what is experienced, observed, or resolved over the course of the narrative.

AF52AADBFF294BC99AA8D11F12153533.description: Use precise words and phrases, effective details, and sensory language to convey a vivid picture of the experiences, events, setting, and/or characters.

3A7BD468572842B981ECE647176764DE.description: Use a variety of techniques to sequence events so that they build on one another to create a coherent whole and build toward a particular tone and outcome (e.g., a sense of mystery, suspense, growth, or resolution.

DEE87B71C51A47718E091716884693BC.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple plot lines, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

A276F9397365435EA0BF49579DF103ED.description: Engage and orient the reader by setting out a problem, situation, or observation and its significance, establishing one or multiple point(s) of view, and introducing a narrator and/or characters; create a smooth progression of experiences or events.

66273453A1B74EB09D1E651B54DB4D5E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

92A718F56E95427F85EE10070C923B23.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

DBDF4729BEB840D99A789EE83A0C02CF.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline.

E28D1BAFBCD04C4089ACB560B48C69D1.description: Use precise language, domain-specific vocabulary, and techniques such as metaphor, simile, and analogy to manage the complexity of the topic.

885A6C51C511450C8D168DE43DECD9B6.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions and syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.

50E7474F63C84DCFBCCCBDA4CCEEF027.description: Develop the topic thoroughly by selecting the most significant and relevant facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.

F6C8ABB8749A4AC0BFBB524D6263D7AD.description: Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, and information so that each new element builds on that which precedes it to create a unified whole; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aid comprehension.

6F3410A96CF44564998834FF16479B38.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

D484E638DC8442B198083D21E0490416.description: Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly and thoroughly, supplying the most relevant evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level, concerns, values and possible biases.

E800743DC2B54111BDE048C7D28C19A1.description: Introduce precise, knowledgeable claims(s); establish the significance of the claim(s); distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claim(s); and create an organization that logically sequences claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

5E7DCD97D74143F285E935C552BA6602.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

DFB5D0666308410BA6C77409B18AAEB8.description: By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend nonfiction and other informational texts at the high end of the grades 11-12 text complexity range independently and proficiently.

0219B32F74DB483CBCE34823A679ED05.description: By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, at the high end of the grades 11-12 text complexity range independently and proficiently.

42A755F254674628B016DE0D41A5087B.description: Range of Reading and Text Complexity

D7918DB134FC4CBF8D4EF5917B560BD9.description: Integrate and evaluate multiple sources of information presented in different media or formats (e.g., visually or quantitatively) as well as in words in order to address a question or solve a problem.

8F05BC3A29C24A98ADDDEE98F88258CF.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in an informational text in which the rhetoric is particularly effective, analyzing how style and content contribute to the power, persuasiveness or beauty of the text.

1E40D000869D41C59A32942E9A8328EB.description: In informational text, analyze and evaluate the effectiveness of the structure an author uses in his or her exposition or argument, including whether the structure makes points clear, convincing, and engaging.

3A83875FB54B4D6B855521DFE1D345C5.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in an informational text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze how an author uses and refines the meaning of a key term or terms over the course of a text (e.g., how Madison defines "faction" in Federalist No. 10).

770AFB701B8F486FB27ECF278483B51D.description: Analyze how an author's choices concerning how to structure specific parts of a literary text (e.g., the choice of where to begin or end a story, and the choice to provide a comedic or tragic resolution) contribute to its overall structure and meaning as well as its aesthetic impact.

8E5AD58D0CF84965854053512E09A088.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a variety of literary texts, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including words with multiple meanings or language that is particularly fresh, engaging, or beautiful. (Include Shakespeare as well as other authors.)

CA5A5A4F15EC48BDA7A18AF76961B6D5.description: Analyze a complex set of ideas or sequence of events and explain how specific individuals, ideas, or events interact and develop over the course of the informational text and media.

1AB0F20F7306481A9903297B708D63CD.description: Determine two or more central ideas of an informational text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to provide a complex analysis; provide an objective summary of the informational text.

4807BBE32D9F41DA8ACC4B89166A4253.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the informational text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where the informational text leaves matters uncertain.

497A7F319A894D6893230A0AE1D68651.description: Analyze the impact of the author's choices regarding how to develop and relate elements of a story or drama (e.g., where a story is set, how the action is ordered, and how the characters are introduced and developed).

3A557298439B49159A2443815D2F2161.description: Determine two or more themes or central ideas of a literary text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to produce a complex account; provide an objective summary of the literary text.

368D23500295440096B0F015C6BC67C5.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the literary text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where the literary text leaves matters uncertain.

14C3F9BF2A8D41B29BF851BC5811675A.description: Transition English Language Arts for Seniors

114B8DD87886428CABD4A0180BABB772.description: Acquire and accurately use general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college- and career-readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

4E1EB346671E4AB3B158F191CA611D01.description: Analyze nuances in the meaning of words with similar denotations.

2DD6817E9AE740E6A1614C1819143E20.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., hyperbole or paradox) in context and analyze their role in the text.

A0AD8F70C0C549169C219BEB26E995C7.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

DC17D74969EA403CAE8ED06F162E5769.description: Verify the initial determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

04E7F5F2CBD7489BA1502BD717558CA9.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, and/or thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning, its part of speech, its etymology, or its standard usage.

7ED32BC885CA4F32814F946A614B24E8.description: Identify and correctly use patterns of word changes that indicate different meanings or parts of speech (e.g., conceive, conception, or conceivable).

263EDF807ECC47FEA5CF09C7109BB49D.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence, paragraph, or text; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

080978835E3C4DBEA079842D8EA0A871.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 11 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

5F8071B95FFF402185E0AD2CF9F82780.description: Vary syntax for effect by consulting references (e.g., Tufte's Artful Sentences) for guidance as needed; apply an understanding of syntax to the study of complex texts when reading.

635EED77FFB84DE69C7F7EFA8CAADA73.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

EC001342C45A4CC6B0116B1BDEBE3732.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

8C3894A8BB464FF3A00104CF606932FA.description: Resolve issues of complex or contested usage, consulting references (e.g., Merriam-Webster's Dictionary of English Usage or Garner's Modern American Usage) as needed.

29015A65136746A7840D8FEBFF6C98E5.description: Apply the understanding that usage is a matter of convention, can change over time, and is sometimes contested.

EEDF0338FF0A4305BBCAE1E5954780C5.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

E65EF1D96C644A0591BFCE30A12E5B51.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating a command of formal English when indicated or appropriate. (See grade 11 Language standards for specific expectations.)

ABA1DB04F1674A8C8FD13C4180E31358.description: Make strategic use of digital media (e.g., textual, graphical, audio, visual, and interactive elements) in presentations to enhance understanding of findings, reasoning, and evidence and to add interest.

DB11A47E8325486E8F355BDE880B3B7A.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence, conveying a clear and distinct perspective, such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning; alternative or opposing perspectives are addressed and the organization, development, substance, and style are appropriate to purpose, audience, and a range of formal and informal tasks.

3E2E2246F5D0467E89429C27EE9E0D49.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric, assessing the stance, premises, links among ideas, word choice, points of emphasis, and tone used.

7C7B0954E27C4440A3631C53D11CBEE6.description: Integrate multiple sources of information presented in diverse formats and media (e.g., visually, quantitatively, and/or orally) in order to make informed decisions and solve problems, evaluating the credibility and accuracy of each source and noting any discrepancies among the data.

1A395842055D4DD6860372E182367857.description: Respond thoughtfully to diverse perspectives; synthesize comments, claims, and evidence made on all sides of an issue; resolve contradictions when possible; and determine what additional information or research is required to deepen the investigation or complete the task.

5C1FF4952DA641E29D6807001501A7EB.description: Propel conversations by posing and responding to questions that probe reasoning and evidence; ensure a hearing for a full range of positions on a topic or issue; clarify, verify, or challenge ideas and conclusions; and promote divergent and creative perspectives.

D866923D6FCB4913AD104309094AB056.description: Work with peers to promote civil, democratic discussions and decision-making; establish clear goals, deadlines, and individual roles as needed.

58982AD09764406BA3B2F7BA6949759A.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read and researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence from texts and other research on the topic or issue to stimulate a thoughtful, well-reasoned exchange of ideas.

6A7C26FD822E47B0BB7602CE60E7433B.description: Initiate and effectively participate in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 11 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing ideas clearly and persuasively.

74532A5C613243358CCF712B78AE327D.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

ED5001818B6646689246A345E4E171AA.description: Apply grade 11 Reading standards to nonfiction and other informational texts (e.g., "Delineate and evaluate the reasoning in influential U.S. texts, including the application of constitutional principles [e.g., in U.S. Supreme Court Case majority opinions and dissents] and the premises, purposes and arguments in works of public advocacy [e.g., The Federalist Papers or presidential addresses]").

8BD8FA23EA244067963C50BE4980C79D.description: Apply grade 11 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Demonstrate knowledge of eighteenth-, nineteenth-, and early-twentieth-century foundational works of American literature, including how two or more texts from the same period treat similar themes or topics").

64D00FE7FA81483FBC64B10D95EF01DC.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

E09CE0FD7E994AFDB4884A65B8543549.description: Gather relevant information from multiple authoritative print and digital sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the strengths and limitations of each source in terms of the task, purpose, and audience; integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and overreliance on any one source and following a standard format for citation (e.g., MLA or APA).

A5F488B9B3EF471EAAF1B43517A3CDB2.description: Conduct short, as well as more sustained, research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

F9018E4367674CDA9056583EF5E78C97.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

09C54A1136674B329B0FEBC13A785FFD.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products in response to ongoing feedback, including new arguments or information.

FEB30EA29B2748B7971C030DF4A336B6.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience. (Editing for conventions should demonstrate command of all Language standards up to and including grade 11).

36139A551F804F4C995E4227AED6E8A1.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in Text Types and Purposes.)

987C16864864460499407609FEC7DBE4.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on what is experienced, observed, or resolved over the course of the narrative.

8C4EE554177247FABDA22E591A598474.description: Use precise words and phrases, effective details, and sensory language to convey a vivid picture of the experiences, events, setting, and/or characters.

2D2D565EE017497690236969921CEB17.description: Use a variety of techniques to sequence events so that they build on one another to create a coherent whole and build toward a particular tone and outcome (e.g., a sense of mystery, suspense, growth, or resolution).

F11B7E6A65E44441A2856BDBCC36DE20.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple plot lines, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

8FECC9E0C8924F6AA64B539A7BEE8BFC.description: Engage and orient the reader by setting out a problem, situation, or observation and its significance, establishing one or multiple point(s) of view and introducing a narrator and/or characters; create a smooth progression of experiences or events.

E59F1CB317C44F4895DBA661725DCD9D.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

72199287EAA94BD0A5588EA4BD8A9F4A.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

9E0B5B3A3D3C4F9FB5DDD58240D29C32.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline.

881261C8A9B043388225EA89D7A0DD30.description: Use precise language, domain-specific vocabulary, and techniques such as metaphor, simile, and analogy to manage the complexity of the topic.

1797BC7A2A2E4675A2E2296FA7382068.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions and syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.

35602181274F402EBC055FEAD47EA6B5.description: Develop the topic thoroughly by selecting the most significant and relevant facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.

DDCD09CC29E042AF81C487579499C5B9.description: Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, and information so that each new element builds on that which precedes it to create a unified whole; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures and/or tables), and multimedia when useful to aid comprehension.

8FC4DA99B32C41E8BFA6FE58EB89228B.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

6A1B8EAE11374D2AB50B350F4A2F17D2.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

0E15E67925E54B62AD0AD4FD2F613BF3.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline.

7E97BC0E8B564FCAB348C3FCFCE53895.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses as well as varied syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence, and between claim(s) and counterclaims.

24F40E30360445F3ABCB07FB91DA7A63.description: Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly and thoroughly, supplying the most relevant evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level, concerns, values, and possible biases.

42C44F61AF3549F691DD4AF7623D88E6.description: Introduce precise, knowledgeable claim(s); establish the significance of the claim(s); distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that logically sequences claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

157D5E34380643499148C391F771C55C.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

83CD3D8AECD741699322447CB6347D52.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend nonfiction and other informational texts in the grades 11-12 text complexity range proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

37908BD8271343C28AD5AF27C21C9E23.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, in the grades 11–12 text complexity range proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

CE051A96FAC14A5C955BCA52D1592A0A.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

249B9E892C6543F981047C05A8DAF0F6.description: Use a comma to separate coordinate adjectives (e.g., It was a fascinating, enjoyable movie.).

A23124D073804836AA61CC1A8DAD2EC9.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

2F9ACC100D0A43B4A8050A1DCAD6A72D.description: Choose among simple, compound, complex, and compound-complex sentences to signal differing relationships among ideas.
