B1604D51FEB94B90945100F1E1955BD0.description: Draw, construct and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them.

0937BB2F21964327B4C65CD63AD9E199.description: Solve word problems leading to inequalities of the form px + q > r or px + q < r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Graph the solution set of the inequality and interpret it in the context of the problem (e.g., as a salesperson, you are paid $50 per week plus $3 per sale; this week you want your pay to be at least $100; write an inequality for the number of sales you need to make and describe the solutions).

A2F6163B265C41D08EEF351902BFAEA2.description: Solve word problems leading to equations of the form px + q = r and p(x + q) = r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Solve equations of these forms fluently. Compare an algebraic solution to an arithmetic solution, identifying the sequence of the operations used in each approach (e.g., the perimeter of a rectangle is 54 cm; its length is 6 cm; what is its width?; an arithmetic solution similar to "54 – 6 – 6 divided by 2" may be compared with the reasoning involved in solving the equation 2w + 12 = 54; an arithmetic solution similar to "54/2 – 6" may be compared with the reasoning involved in solving the equation 2(w + 6) = 54).

5EFA45D1575D4A1191D5B3E5B3CDFBA3.description: Use variables to represent quantities in a real-world or mathematical problem and construct simple equations and inequalities to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.

9BC5B51D20914F27ABD6AA921515A073.description: Solve multi-step real-life and mathematical problems posed with positive and negative rational numbers in any form (whole numbers, fractions, and decimals), using tools strategically. Apply properties of operations to calculate with numbers in any form; convert between forms as appropriate; and assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies (e.g., if a woman making $25 an hour gets a 10% raise, she will make an additional 1/10 of her salary an hour, or $2.50, for a new salary of $27.50; if you want to place a towel bar 9¾ inches long in the center of a door that is 27½ inches wide, you will need to place the bar about 9 inches from each edge; this estimate can be used as a check on the exact computation).

811217B5C25648609243C28D5F01F1FF.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions and equations.

4A51C5843CCD4722AB06111D80A95249.description: Understand that rewriting an expression in different forms in a problem context can shed light on the problem and how the quantities in it are related (e.g., a + 0.05a = 1.05a means that "increase by 5%" is the same as "multiply by 1.05.").

845894EC94CE454E81B1C39A8E2C1C80.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add, subtract, factor and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.

52F7EB7A054D4F3289A0C3FB6499FB2E.description: Use properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

EC3F5913E00F4137BBAE4BFED2C3DC9B.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations with rational numbers.

F97622EB48B141BFA9E1AAFBF30AE00F.description: Convert a rational number to a decimal using long division; know that the decimal form of a rational number terminates in 0s or eventually repeats.

A585A7AB6EF048608F4E2C5EE5E1CB8E.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide rational numbers.

052FEFEF4E4D47B8BC152100454F9F14.description: Understand that integers can be divided, provided that the divisor is not zero, and every quotient of integers (with non-zero divisor) is a rational number. If p and q are integers, then –(p/q) = (–p)/q = p/(–q). Interpret quotients of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

6B1E53D7176E43CBA76140D727BB10E9.description: Understand that multiplication is extended from fractions to rational numbers by requiring that operations continue to satisfy the properties of operations, particularly the distributive property, leading to products such as (–1)(–1) = 1 and the rules for multiplying signed numbers. Interpret products of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

32F8BA2550BD4B158984912E966827BC.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division and of fractions to multiply and divide rational numbers.

E66FCCE84EEE4493B9AE797BF9C4EEF1.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract rational numbers.

6F1150885BCB4C97937885264A43B45D.description: Understand subtraction of rational numbers as adding the additive inverse, p – q = p + (–q). Show that the distance between two rational numbers on the number line is the absolute value of their difference and apply this principle in real-world contexts.

FFEA11E6639642BE85A6425210FE7917.description: Understand p + q as the number located a distance |q| from p, in the positive or negative direction, depending on whether q is positive or negative. (e.g., to add "p + q" on the number line, start at "0" and move to "p" then move |q| in the positive or negative direction depending on whether "q" is positive or negative). Show that a number and its opposite have a sum of 0 (are additive inverses). Interpret sums of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

F719EE8DD7534463AF8ECCD63C78F863.description: Describe situations in which opposite quantities combine to make 0 (e.g., a hydrogen atom has 0 charge because its two constituents are oppositely charged).

1C270EBF562541898694EF2E03B715F3.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers; represent addition and subtraction on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram.

5282B49A0C08452BB69B749854628A8B.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with fractions to add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational numbers.

768A5D85615A47E19B04FEFA5A9FFC68.description: Use proportional relationships to solve multistep ratio and percent problems (e.g., simple interest, tax, markups and markdowns, gratuities and commissions, fees, percent increase and decrease, and/or percent error).

41E1C184D6B04F1EB93C19B3931C0783.description: Explain what a point (x,y) on the graph of a proportional relationship means in terms of the situation. Focus special attention on the points (0,0) and (1,r) where r is the unit rate.

D449A8353AB84D71A66073E74CDD47ED.description: Represent proportional relationships by equations (e.g., if total cost t is proportional to the number n of items purchased at a constant price p, the relationship between the total cost and the number of items can be expressed as t = pn).

DA02928EC2374524B1780CE798354C26.description: Identify the constant of proportionality (unit rate) in tables, graphs, equations, diagrams and verbal descriptions of proportional relationships.

0C469423DC584809B4605571525D0379.description: Decide whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship (e.g., by testing for equivalent ratios in a table or graphing on a coordinate plane and observing whether the graph is a straight line through the origin).

441542CEF11F41C59C257A3022F98FB3.description: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.

6AFDAD3D3841429595F85D9F1440AC5C.description: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas and other quantities measured in like or different units (e.g., if a person walks ½ mile in each ¼ hour, compute the unit rate as the complex fraction 1/2/1/4 miles per hour, equivalently 2 miles per hour).

F64996818D8548E4B7E2717F6C724C1F.description: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

042127BE22384FD79D702EA9E64507DC.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

49EE37448FD547C9867AC262B6114304.description: Look for and make use of structure.

6FE899F440004045BC443CCC95FFD9B3.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

4D457C2D329647D4950A5DD4C7706C33.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Mathematics

8FFEF3B8EC95449E827B8547BA1B2BB9.description: Understand that patterns of association can also be seen in bivariate categorical data by displaying frequencies and relative frequencies in a two-way table. Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects. Use relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe possible association between the two variables (e.g., collect data from students in your class on whether or not they have a curfew on school nights and whether or not they have assigned chores at home; is there evidence that those who have a curfew also tend to have chores?).

13AC766B18A1494187710548BAAD9275.description: Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the context of bivariate measurement data, interpreting the slope and intercept (e.g., in a linear model for a biology experiment, interpret a slope of 1.5 cm/hr as meaning that an additional hour of sunlight each day is associated with an additional 1.5 cm in mature plant height).

4A3D52DA67FF4D89ACB316C19D245A4E.description: Know that straight lines are widely used to model relationships between two quantitative variables. For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line and informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

82821A94A4CC41469ED57DAFF4C05073.description: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities. Describe patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or negative association, linear association and nonlinear association.

1C7AFC45BE8F482A8F80F0AEE3B729EE.description: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.

B517B3A071E04824B4301DB767CC2378.description: Know the formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders and spheres and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

EA7082A0235B43BDA121E678A3BFE0E6.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume of cylinders, cones, and spheres.

BF8724D284314630906D0E610630979C.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between two points in a coordinate system.

9C86B898C0324D6C906B281B838CA8D8.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to determine unknown side lengths in right triangles in real-world and mathematical problems in two and three dimensions.

A39F66BF9FA0409AA8C46BCE7E96E1D5.description: Explain a proof of the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse.

3EDAC92A78DC4E70995E98AC3548E79F.description: Understand and apply the Pythagorean Theorem.

01AA97374D454815A464FA657BDB759D.description: Use informal arguments to establish facts about the angle sum and exterior angle of triangles, about the angles created when parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and the angle-angle criterion for similarity of triangles (e.g., arrange three copies of the same triangle so that the sum of the three angles appears to form a line; give an argument in terms of transversals why this is so).

A086F47CD8B04E12BB42587AB195C1AD.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is similar to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, translations and dilations; given two similar two-dimensional figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the similarity between them.

25139DD323C0444F80C21822B2CD4196.description: Describe the effect of dilations, translations, rotations and reflections on two-dimensional figures using coordinates.

7173922220F241F48F059E52829BC1F9.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is congruent to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections and translations; given two congruent figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the congruence between them.

CDED556BB0AD4AF181DAA2BCC0CBADEA.description: Parallel lines are taken to parallel lines.

01151CB8FB8C42929733A1185B0031BD.description: Angles are taken to angles of the same measure.

D1B91561CF4C4F40940AE123CF2A109E.description: Lines are taken to lines, and line segments to line segments of the same length.

E7412EF22CE347388B4D36DB8FF481F5.description: Verify experimentally the properties of rotations, reflections and translations:

B3E3D3AFE2B7472D8E572E4C9B6C706E.description: Understand congruence and similarity using physical models, transparencies, or geometry software.

B9855C5CE66C468097097D0A24225DBD.description: Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph (e.g., where the function is increasing or decreasing, linear or nonlinear). Sketch a graph that exhibits the qualitative features of a function that has been described verbally.

A862619A5DB84A73AE642A1CB024B266.description: Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities. Determine the rate of change and initial value of the function from a description of a relationship or from two (x, y) values, including reading these from a table or from a graph. Interpret the rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models, and in terms of its graph or a table of values.

656993239ACF4FC3A77E99440DD59B9F.description: Use functions to model relationships between quantities.

75CABBA0121A46D187B1153ECF20A44A.description: Interpret the equation y = mx + b as defining a linear function, whose graph is a straight line; give examples of functions that are not linear (e.g., the function A = s² giving the area of a square as a function of its side length is not linear because its graph contains the points (1,1), (2,4) and (3,9), which are not on a straight line).

33AA09FEC54B4DC28FFD7EE77D6FCF49.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way, such as algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions (e.g., given a linear function represented by a table of values and a linear function represented by an algebraic expression, determine which function has the greater rate of change).

49EBBE77DCBF488C9C1789F62DA7E876.description: Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output. The graph of a function is the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and the corresponding output.

C30F1AA5A2B146CE974CAF960C733E32.description: Rearrange formulas to isolate a given variable, using the same reasoning as in solving equations (e.g., rearrange Ohm's law V = IR to isolate resistance R).

84CE5B8FA5C34FD4B45F7512AB44789F.description: Analyze and solve real-world mathematical problems utilizing linear inequalities in one variable. Solve linear inequalities with rational number coefficients, including inequalities whose solutions require expanding expressions using the distributive property and combining like terms.

1E993B60CA0641F18A62D72878BE2E28.description: Explain each step in solving a linear equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method.

B054DE04CAA94A88B819D1C7049FCA30.description: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations by graphing, limiting to integer solutions. Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables correspond to points of intersection of their graphs, because points of intersection satisfy both equations simultaneously.

0CE367B8B0BF41A18AF46713015B3A73.description: Solve linear equations with rational number coefficients, including equations whose solutions require expanding expressions using the distributive property and combining like terms.

4B49E13B120D4CCD89E3F55E46E70E48.description: Give examples of linear equations in one variable with one solution, infinitely many solutions or no solutions. Show which of these possibilities is the case by successively transforming the given equation into simpler forms, until an equivalent equation of the form x = a, a = a, or a = b results (where a and b are different numbers).

A019E57982154EAFB5CA9F521ECF48FE.description: Analyze and solve real-world and mathematical problems utilizing linear equations in one variable.

6DA68E2744164BB2858947BED3922322.description: Analyze and solve linear equations, pairs of simultaneous linear equations, and linear inequalities in one variable.

87A9B3BF11BF40C2A5160CFB875F9E95.description: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope m is the same between any two distinct points on a non-vertical line in the coordinate plane; derive the equation y = mx for a line through the origin and the equation y = mx + b for a line intercepting the vertical axis at b.

8181900BA6504DF0904CFE42B1DB8D0D.description: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope of the graph. Compare two different proportional relationships represented in different ways (e.g., compare a distance-time graph to a distance-time equation to determine which of two moving objects has greater speed).

6ED60C5B382B4A6696314BCFF4074511.description: Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear equations.

FC15970E78834619BB07B61575A46363.description: Perform operations with numbers expressed in scientific notation, including problems where both decimal and scientific notation are used. Use scientific notation and choose units of appropriate size for measurements of very large or very small quantities (e.g., use millimeters per year for seafloor spreading). Interpret scientific notation that has been generated by technology.

9F976909FF7644518608F08CEDBA13C8.description: Use numbers expressed in the form of a single digit times an integer power of 10 to estimate very large or very small quantities, and to express how many times as much one is than the other (e.g., estimate the population of the United States as 3 × 10<sup>8</sup> and the population of the world as 7 × 10<sup>9</sup>; determine that the world population is more than 20 times larger).

FEAA06ABFB39486A87B4B173093EE9FA.description: Use square root and cube root symbols to represent solutions to equations of the form x² = p and x³ = p, where p is a positive rational number. Evaluate square roots of small perfect squares and cube roots of small perfect cubes. Know that √2 is irrational.

A62ED94CB7B8449187459394B48FFCBF.description: Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions (e.g., 3² × 3<sup>–5</sup> = 3<sup>–3</sup> = 1/3³ = 1/27).

4AF3D164E6FA4274AD592EB1520C18E3.description: Work with radicals and integer exponents.

72837B5420154B33A97AF29B1EA3B7E5.description: Explain why the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational; that the sum of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational; and that the product of a nonzero rational number and an irrational number is irrational.

01EB42FD348844BDAA54A2F5E36EBC43.description: Compare the size of irrational numbers, locate them approximately on a number line diagram, and estimate the value of expressions such as π² (e.g., by truncating the decimal expansion of √2, show that √2 is between 1 and 2, then between 1.4 and 1.5, and explain how to continue on to get better approximations).

D70625146AC14DF6984C1E332F28386E.description: Apply approximations and properties of rational and irrational numbers to:

54FBA6CBBE524D338041FC424AF68E49.description: Know that numbers that are not rational are called irrational. Understand informally that every number has a decimal expansion; for rational numbers show that the decimal expansion repeats eventually and convert a decimal expansion which repeats eventually into a rational number.

C051D0413E594570B846A2A8858390F6.description: Know that there are numbers that are not rational and approximate them by rational numbers.

591B267D160A4D2E891E4A518B76E628.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

ABAF324878CF4154AE21565CBC4C01AE.description: Look for and make use of structure.

E8863EA42DE848DFB8084AFCB91E048E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

9F56E57884C14E05B07235E1448B7C80.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Mathematics

6CFE071213BD4264A914DE3B800E69D8.description: Research and analyze taxes including payroll, sales, personal property, real estate, and income tax returns.

B5EAEC99C6C44C5694934FB46B1013AB.description: Research, develop, and analyze personal budgets based on given parameters (e.g., fixed and discretionary expenses, insurance, gross vs. net pay, types of income, wage, salary, commission, career choice, geographic region, retirement, and/or investment planning).

249C376F7F724A8CAF33314EA2F9EA87.description: Determine, represent, and analyze mathematical models for investments involving simple and compound interest with and without additional deposits (e.g., savings accounts, bonds, and/or certificates of deposit).

86A8F5476891476FB9A92135B0A8DD70.description: Determine, represent, and analyze mathematical models for loan amortization and the effects of different payments and/or finance terms (e.g., business loans, auto, mortgage, and/or credit card).

BAC54E72515742EE9608AF16A1B43B39.description: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).

1C994CBC4C434F5888B63411F8BFB6C6.description: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation only as a tool to describe spread and not to explicitly find standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.

04BFB454446E4F02B0CA269C23627D57.description: Analyze and interpret tables, charts, and graphs (e.g., interpret a body mass index (BMI) chart).

E00CFF2320D049D3811E26A784196DA2.description: Select applicable representations to display data on the real number line (e.g., dot plots, histograms, and box plots).

042E78AF33474B848457785909BC888C.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.

AECD83CF9BDA4C2AA66FE3D38B9FBBB6.description: Statistics and Probability: Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data

013B838D272640FAB331A5A57A7BAB31.description: Identify positive and negative correlations (e.g., vehicle depreciation). Use technology to compute and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.

9B816DE5696A40AC812BB9E89FEB7496.description: For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line, and informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line. Interpret the rate of change and the constant term of a linear model in the context of the data.

712C1B207DF44366A99C2DB9BBD9B851.description: Collect numerical bivariate data; represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot; determine whether or not a relationship exists; if so, describe how the variables are related and select a function to model the data, justify the selection and use the model to make predictions (e.g., cost of the materials for a construction project, cost of the labor for a project, cost and value of a vehicle based on depreciation).

F676763039F24085AC9758B10A45CD33.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two quantitative variables.

66FAD62539D74E1487536702B4AF3F48.description: Gather data, conduct investigations, and apply mathematical concepts and models to solve problems (e.g., designing and building a house or a car).

C0B93C6070F944F3980B2A394638CDEF.description: Create and use two- and three-dimensional representations of authentic situations using paper techniques or dynamic geometric environments for computer-aided design and other applications.

FCCADBDB4117485197A8E9B0B8B1D14D.description: Solve application problems by calculating circumference, area, radius, diameter, area of sector, arc length of a circle with appropriate unit labels (e.g., develop a circular watering system).

EC40BB7051CA4D1E93B99A4FA574A5AC.description: Solve application problems by calculating volume for three-dimensional objects using formulas for cylinders, pyramids, prisms, cones, and spheres (e.g., compute amount of cement needed for a sidewalk, amount of water in a fire hose, amount of air in ductwork).

2CC305BADDF14CDE8351504F9603DD1D.description: Solve application problems by calculating area and surface area for two-dimensional objects (e.g., calculate the cost of installing flooring in a building and painting the interior and exterior of a building based on square footage).

CA9DA0DA2C7B439EB13602FA1CE1A3F6.description: Understand and apply the Pythagorean Theorem for solving real-world problems (e.g., checking accuracy on gate construction, conduit bending, roof pitch).

142B7A65C1AC4D24BB92AEA1A93422CD.description: Explore theorems about triangles to solve real-world application problems.

D298191BF42A491B9162DA759C031333.description: Use geometric theorems and formulas to solve problems.

39D41AADABDD40BA94CE753D9F7DD483.description: Apply geometric methods to solve design problems to satisfy given constraints (e.g., designing an object or structure to satisfy physical constraints or minimize cost; working with topographic grid systems based on ratios).

633945848A4D4FD2B40EBD8F99B49153.description: Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in modeling situations.

3BE6E3A93B504C39A07DD6476F5F4040.description: Use two- and three-dimensional shapes and circles, their measures, and their properties to describe objects.

F959AE00C3A54B9881087506D0F88D42.description: Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of three-dimensional objects, and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects (e.g., three-view drawings and blueprints).

C54AEEEC814F46A8AEFFF871FB80E588.description: Visualize relationships between two dimensional and three-dimensional objects and apply geometric concepts in modeling situations.

6E1864FC05B04D54A0FCDD19E7199AD3.description: Recognize that the graph of a linear or exponential equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane.

4EE29FF0156D4DCE88FE3EB37F9DD4EB.description: Represent application problems as linear equations. Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities (e.g., level of education versus pay; rate of speed versus fuel consumption; caloric intake versus expenditure).

952B25333771497B950F59A438299038.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

3253981E37E341C4B764BDB1315573EC.description: Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph.

D064E857A7BF4CB49309C16F440146CC.description: Interpret the equation y = mx + b as defining a linear function, whose graph is a straight line; give examples of functions that are not linear.

A9F479FF6DA64665B39F30E406DB1F3E.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear function in terms of a context.

41C824083304468AADA32211A404482E.description: Use multiple representations of functions to recognize that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. Develop function notation utilizing the definition of a function to represent situations both algebraically and graphically.

5423F2354FA346C0BD25C6D1FCAE06FD.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation.

F8E35B9F119645EF940D2BD43CC7748A.description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables (e.g., childcare facility – sq. footage to number of children; solving electrical current in a circuit with multiple paths, break-even point).

F0696CCF3C064F4B805DCD36E1A094F1.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations (e.g., rearrange Ohm's law V = IR to highlight resistance R).

43C4B858D9E345FC84DE7B4808C082F1.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales (e.g., profit vs. number of units, cost vs. number of units, resistance vs. current).

4F28EE4FF0274CBBA0B1EAE224C15E1A.description: Analyze real-world problem situations and use variables to construct and solve equations and inequalities in one variable, representing linear, exponential, and simple rational functions (e.g., using spreadsheet functions, determine sale price of items).

6A40C7C869814C5A9A34EDD65BC89EEF.description: Analyze real-world problem situations and use variables to construct and solve equations involving one or more unknown or variable quantities to answer questions about the situations, such as creating spreadsheet formulas to calculate prices based on percentage mark-up or solving formulas for specified values. Demonstrate understanding of the meaning of a solution. Identify when there is insufficient information given to solve a problem.

DF98FA8DC0BE4598A0BF9FCE6B5AA0AA.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

27C2E47C848F4C359A4875CB125ACF02.description: Solve application problems using direct and inverse variation equations (e.g., determine the mechanical advantage of gears, Ohm's Law).

494C018E10AC4C44A8C8A604E45ACC90.description: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rates as the slope of the graph. Compare two different proportional relationships represented in different ways. For example, compare a distance-time graph to a distance-time equation to determine which of two moving objects has greater speed (e.g., labor cost per time, material cost per job).

C486C1B7A92246498B14BD2ABD15B784.description: Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear equations.

7C92CE9A55DB4F64B533FF6F69558E7C.description: Recognize the concept of complex solutions when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions.

388AC9376F564D73A704E67C0DB1501D.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable by inspection (e.g., for x² = 49), taking square roots, factoring, completing the square when a=1 only, and the quadratic formula, as appropriate for the initial form of the equation.

1EC228A7CCED4676A1CC8E5687C88245.description: Solve linear equations including equations with coefficients represented by letters, simple exponential equations that rely on application of the laws of exponents, and compound linear inequalities in one variable.

56F683F8E6FE4613B9EFB742757A33EE.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

C791044106B74741999D5D5851A2BF59.description: Represent constraints by linear equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or non-viable options in a modeling context.

E61982DCBF134C84864349D1FE6053A3.description: Create equations in two or more variables, representing linear and exponential relationships between quantities. In the case of exponential equations, limit to situations with integer inputs.

5930B773667846F2803B0BED77008919.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable, representing linear and exponential relationships, and use them to solve problems. In the case of exponential equations, limit to situations with integer inputs.

2228199576EA4D869F75C46A138C1935.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

D920051207FC41F98D3C66D61E0547D0.description: Recognize that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials. Focus on linear or quadratic terms.

BA4F8FBDD8834EE9AD754298FD7EA92A.description: Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions in exponential functions. For example, the expression 1.15<sup>t</sup> can be rewritten as (1.15<sup>1/12</sup>)<sup>12t</sup> ≈ 1.012<sup>12t</sup> to reveal the approximate equivalent monthly interest rate if the annual rate is 15%.

EF20FF8384974CB0AE5ACF4CC8E28881.description: Complete the square in a quadratic expression, when a=1 only, to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function it defines.

FC1D726491764535882D771DAE63C0CB.description: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.

77CB095F986E4497909676EA4A0D125D.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of linear, exponential, and quadratic expressions to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression through connections to a graphical representation of the function.

3EA5C16D08204490A536DDEF13CCBACF.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems.

3366B7B17B0C4FAA9D48369BD11116AA.description: Rewrite expressions involving radicals, including simplifying, and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.

E4F724CE3F314DD4A29195D374044A46.description: Explain the connections between expressions with rational exponents and expressions with radicals using properties of exponents. Extend from application of properties of exponents for expressions with integer exponents.

47CDAA4F499349F7A1BA613B989E7D8B.description: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents.

F350253538B6479A98CCB3E7EC98CE9B.description: Use the structure of quadratic and exponential expressions to identify ways to rewrite them.

77240A036630413E8C6BA404F3DB6AF7.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear function or exponential function of the form f(x) = a*b<sup>x</sup> in terms of a context.

77582287101E453A98A96BCDAF144A42.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.

9C70BE8163AF4BF2BF99D5E9844305EF.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

A48EA51D978344B49C28743BFAF7771E.description: Interpret linear, exponential, and quadratic expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

A9C913F3BF7641F5BD675934AAADDC9A.description: Interpret the structure of expressions and equations in terms of the context they model.

17621CD5642E4E6786ECCEE489E8F5E8.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

EBE2FFD67A9D49BBB06934ADCD71E62F.description: Look for and make use of structure.

8C64493637DE4503BEC38FD86B5DE4F4.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

EA9A2E8EB7D840E3971A738AD7FF2383.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Mathematics

B2F9939473BF432CA4B8A69019053748.description: Research and analyze taxes including payroll, sales, personal property, real estate, and income tax returns.

E51E40C94329423DA1E040F2D0EBBFCB.description: Research, develop, and analyze personal budgets based on given parameters (e.g., fixed and discretionary expenses, insurance, gross vs. net pay, types of income, wage, salary, commission, career choice, geographic region, retirement, and/or investment planning).

B0D2428AF2684AB5BEF9365B40B15E3B.description: Determine, represent, and analyze mathematical models for investments involving simple and compound interest with and without additional deposits (e.g., savings accounts, bonds, and/or certificates of deposit).

6AA35BD96C1B4D57A4B6DEBDBA3071D0.description: Determine, represent, and analyze mathematical models for loan amortization and the effects of different payments and/or finance terms (e.g., business loans, auto, mortgage, and/or credit card).

D15DB2D0FE574B158ADBF4E600CF4ECE.description: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).

9DB6C749AFDB4B5B833AC0DE14459F22.description: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation only as a tool to describe spread and not to explicitly find standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.

42970565C2594F74B3F9D6B22A043EE2.description: Analyze and interpret tables, charts, and graphs (e.g., interpret a body mass index (BMI) chart).

23E990D552854470BC0CEF7620DFA684.description: Select applicable representations to display data on the real number line (e.g., dot plots, histograms, and box plots).

2657A43571B64EDF84FF2D426A5E639D.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.

21324CB88DF346D49C7A2D2FA39A960E.description: Statistics and Probability: Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data

1D2F031C09604F61B6ACA8027AD8494C.description: Identify positive and negative correlations (e.g., vehicle depreciation). Use technology to compute and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.

F11605BBEDF54E7AAC0150DE2E9091CD.description: For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line, and informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line. Interpret the rate of change and the constant term of a linear model in the context of the data.

22F17409100B4990B881A45F33FC5719.description: Collect numerical bivariate data; represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot; determine whether or not a relationship exists; if so, describe how the variables are related and select a function to model the data, justify the selection and use the model to make predictions (e.g., cost of the materials for a construction project, cost of the labor for a project, cost and value of a vehicle based on depreciation).

99768C7F48344BF89FE0C59A249DCB2A.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two quantitative variables.

C74E6A71F8174BBC87492316814D4896.description: Gather data, conduct investigations, and apply mathematical concepts and models to solve problems (e.g., designing and building a house or a car).

83636EF0BBB74686ACE6CA39F442019D.description: Create and use two- and three-dimensional representations of authentic situations using paper techniques or dynamic geometric environments for computer-aided design and other applications.

463D26A6F622432AB90547D097E6CC9D.description: Solve application problems by calculating circumference, area, radius, diameter, area of sector, arc length of a circle with appropriate unit labels (e.g., develop a circular watering system).

6143C66FC0F54317B4343C45FC398079.description: Solve application problems by calculating volume for three-dimensional objects using formulas for cylinders, pyramids, prisms, cones, and spheres (e.g., compute amount of cement needed for a sidewalk, amount of water in a fire hose, amount of air in ductwork).

C6EF8C65DC6D4D9D9353EBE22BBAAD11.description: Solve application problems by calculating area and surface area for two-dimensional objects (e.g., calculate the cost of installing flooring in a building and painting the interior and exterior of a building based on square footage).

CA344695133F4F8DAB3C187A98A16D72.description: Understand and apply the Pythagorean Theorem for solving real-world problems (e.g., checking accuracy on gate construction, conduit bending, roof pitch).

3DE2FCC8F1F445FA9DC40E25D1EEF9B5.description: Explore theorems about triangles to solve real-world application problems.

73CBDC684880474E8A27332B2C9A3F33.description: Use geometric theorems and formulas to solve problems.

5D0413FB2F81481BB04FDA83440AF66F.description: Apply geometric methods to solve design problems to satisfy given constraints (e.g., designing an object or structure to satisfy physical constraints or minimize cost; working with topographic grid systems based on ratios).

6094DA37CEA54C799C5CC6AE5E6609EB.description: Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in modeling situations.

68B9001807A14658BB63E8C0DBEB93EC.description: Use two- and three-dimensional shapes and circles, their measures, and their properties to describe objects.

9949C1A4932B4A4D90C66E3177FBCEF2.description: Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of three-dimensional objects, and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects (e.g., three-view drawings and blueprints).

01B31D3EAA454D50AF48ECE1BF04A314.description: Visualize relationships between two dimensional and three-dimensional objects and apply geometric concepts in modeling situations.

242B1CCFC28E48E2AE80AC134F3BAC99.description: Recognize that the graph of a linear or exponential equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane.

A6A8F78FAAD64703BA25A56A900682AB.description: Represent application problems as linear equations. Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities (e.g., level of education versus pay; rate of speed versus fuel consumption; caloric intake versus expenditure).

4412C4800E5A45BFA9483DE41DCFF0D3.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

778752A4733948E09B31FD45698BA776.description: Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph.

C8B44B56466849B18E8860D0229FDF8F.description: Interpret the equation y = mx + b as defining a linear function, whose graph is a straight line; give examples of functions that are not linear.

193BC7A2125B451FB3C35C1906A9BD6D.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear function in terms of a context.

3029CAA905224C5486E54DCAF4FECD09.description: Use multiple representations of functions to recognize that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. Develop function notation utilizing the definition of a function to represent situations both algebraically and graphically.

35AC87A2890C47849140D1C0232D848A.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation.

8D590544B5914E1B89031115E4708D4A.description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables (e.g., childcare facility – sq. footage to number of children; solving electrical current in a circuit with multiple paths, break-even point).

2448EBA0706A4EF0BBAE14FB92D6CDC8.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations (e.g., rearrange Ohm's law V = IR to highlight resistance R).

9D1E5E703BA44BD0A89435B30D59EA6A.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales (e.g., profit vs. number of units, cost vs. number of units, resistance vs. current).

20A57B6C72C74B8794BCA8DEDAE26C3F.description: Analyze real-world problem situations and use variables to construct and solve equations and inequalities in one variable, representing linear, exponential, and simple rational functions (e.g., using spreadsheet functions, determine sale price of items).

A4F35A20D92B4CAC85C85C6EFE7380F2.description: Analyze real-world problem situations and use variables to construct and solve equations involving one or more unknown or variable quantities to answer questions about the situations, such as creating spreadsheet formulas to calculate prices based on percentage mark-up or solving formulas for specified values. Demonstrate understanding of the meaning of a solution. Identify when there is insufficient information given to solve a problem.

F9F221AC55E24EB1931C739CAC466485.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

433A1723D49D451EADD3F3487DA8692A.description: Solve application problems using direct and inverse variation equations (e.g., determine the mechanical advantage of gears, Ohm's Law).

5ECCC49B2D1D42209C698AA5E5580557.description: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rates as the slope of the graph. Compare two different proportional relationships represented in different ways. For example, compare a distance-time graph to a distance-time equation to determine which of two moving objects has greater speed (e.g., labor cost per time, material cost per job).

EA26A854DD2D47039A1A0AB151379F49.description: Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear equations.

C63EF933CBB94505AC6B9B6DD63A256C.description: Solve real-world problems in a variety of contexts by representing quantities in equivalent forms (fractions, decimals, and percentages) to investigate and describe quantitative relationships. Compare the size of numbers in different forms arising in authentic real-world contexts, such as growth expressed as a fraction versus as a percentage. Interpret the meaning of numbers in different forms, such as scientific notation and the meaning of a fraction or percentage greater than 100 and its validity in a given context. Recognize incorrect or deceptive uses of fractions, decimals, or percentages.

B8B53779BC4148FB97DE3AE511B883BC.description: Perform operations and convert quantities between fractions, decimals, and percents using positive and negative numbers, fractions, absolute value, decimals, percentages, and scientific notation (e.g., given the cost of a project, determine what percentage of the budget were salaries; percent of increase/decrease).

827FA988C9D14C478403A5FDC55709B1.description: Distinguish between proportional and non-proportional situations, apply proportional reasoning when appropriate, solve for an unknown quantity in proportional situations; apply scale factors to perform indirect measurements using maps, blueprints, concentrations, dosages, and densities.

AAE9B8683CC049868B024AB4122AE2AE.description: Solve real-world problems requiring conversion of units using dimensional analysis for measurements in English and metric systems. Solve problems involving multiple units of measurement (e.g., converting between currencies, calculating dosages of medicine, trip planning from miles to kilometers).

18A922F870974BCC824133D0A93879D1.description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

CBF6579B8BDA49F39665FC9AC664FE99.description: Select and correctly use an appropriate tool (e.g., tape measure, ruler, compass, level, micrometer, scale, protractor, thermometer, speedometer, odometer, pressure gauge, measuring squares, multimeter) to measure and/or calculate lengths, distances, directions, masses, temperatures, rates of change (e.g., slope, speed), areas, volumes, voltages, currents, and resistances.

ED3A0B3E9FFA42DE980C43177A64AF42.description: Use units to understand problems and to guide the solutions of multi-step problems; choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

F48F0F0C88C5425BAF65920BA11D439A.description: Communicate with and about mathematics orally and in writing as part of independent and collaborative work, including making accurate and clear presentations of solutions to problems.

1F2CE392BCDE45A1A45836416695CF83.description: Demonstrate reasoning skills in developing, explaining, and justifying sound mathematical arguments and analyzing the soundness of mathematical arguments of others.

04144D509E804AE295B2DD5A2A7D2572.description: Use one-way analysis of variance to test claims involving three or more means. Introduce two-way analysis of variance.

6A8C2B5096C74BBE9A9F356B21AE5864.description: Perform a two-sample F-test to compare two variances. Interpret the F-distribution and use an F-table to find critical values.

8CBA18DD5DB24A0088ADC0B84C83E519.description: Perform a two-sample F-test to compare two variances.

77F65035A6174BB6BA68A750A64DFA2B.description: Interpret the F-distribution and use an F-table to find critical values.

B70BE5F0630D49E5A777976C94462142.description: Use the chi-squared distribution to test whether a frequency distribution fits a claimed distribution and to test whether two variables are independent.

B63525119DA245B8BD67521A3C7D1927.description: Use a contingency table to find expected frequencies.

8A6501690AEA44EA98EDF374BC4B4081.description: Use statistical tests to determine a relationship.

8553F708F9F741B1BC0D06F000CCDCC4.description: Use technology to find a multiple regression equation, the standard error of estimate, and the coefficient of determination.

0AE1E41FE2194601BB7E783FD46A0606.description: Find and interpret the standard error of estimate for a regression line; construct and interpret a prediction interval for y.

D2C22E4D82B047EBB1B59A2A8025B3BC.description: Find and interpret the coefficient of determination.

87F1DD2C2C834711B09418F2CFFEDD21.description: Interpret the types of variation about a regression line.

C6DBB8058980488689597F48B09039D5.description: Find the equation of a regression line; predict y-values using a regression line.

98A68597BA294389966F79C97C8869ED.description: Use linear regression to predict and interpret.

08EB006F12EE4240B4AD145CB4E72F8A.description: Perform a hypothesis test for a population correlation coefficient.

5EAFFB9C29634973B50F0BF0689E5578.description: Test a population correlation coefficient using a table.

F9F08FAB72A0455E8ED533C941AEB213.description: Find critical values for chi squared test. Use the chi squared test to test a variance or a standard deviation.

8EBA4C48228B4D40A0FD445EC28AFC19.description: Use the z-test to test a population proportion, p.

8A986DC92FD04E4183FE698DB7941C36.description: Find critical values in a t-distribution and use the t-test to test a mean.

F20B8FB19F63407BACD9217E8ED2344A.description: Find critical values and rejection regions in a normal distribution. Use rejection regions for a z-test.

079C23E2F86C4834811392E9D9C471E7.description: Find probability values and test for mean. Use in a z-test.

BDF6391D50334EC993F78FE0EC351BC5.description: Make and interpret decisions on comparing two hypotheses based on results of a statistical test. Write a claim for a hypothesis test.

1B4C8527ABB24886B9C075617600C807.description: Use one-tailed and two-tailed statistical tests to find p-value.

794C319346F8441AAEC7C996E1B04CBD.description: Identify Type I and Type II errors and interpret the level of significance.

44650BC20E27447AAE11A7D224CC43C1.description: Interpret a hypothesis test; state a null hypothesis and an alternative hypothesis.

08BAC824856540F08435F140810EEE2E.description: Use hypothesis testing in making and interpreting decisions.

FE3E9CC8188F4DF0B494BB1FB471A791.description: Interpret the chi-square distribution and use chi-square distribution table. Use the chi-square distribution to construct a confidence interval for the variance and standard deviation.

484859ED0A4C4BB1AB6D00EE061373AD.description: Construct confidence intervals when the sample size, n, is less than 30, population is normally distributed, and standard deviation, σ, is unknown.

131957D0D6E949BA84B7DBC458222AA3.description: Interpret the t-distribution and use t-distribution table in real-world scenarios.

191D13147D524CBD806BA18B8205A1A5.description: Determine minimum sample size requirements when estimating mean, µ (population proportion).

B26B119445214A4BB5303C17D2D6CBBB.description: Construct and interpret confidence intervals for the population mean.

BB4C2839811F47F28656EF62B22264A1.description: Find the point estimate and margin of error in a given scenario.

8D10697E135C4CA0BE7A8C707FCF04BB.description: Interpret the rate of change and the constant term of a linear model in the context of the data. Use technology to compute and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.

89EEAEB96E274294A839092E2E18C261.description: Fit a linear function for scatter plots that suggest a linear association.

B316D222719D45559817FF9D039FFE17.description: Informally assess the fit of a function by plotting and analyzing residuals. Focus should be on situations for which linear models are appropriate.

A5E6B57436EF4EBDBE3824E16279A9CF.description: Fit a function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data. Use given functions or choose a function suggested by the context. Emphasize linear and exponential models.

97CE1744B9A849BAA81C5EADBDECF419.description: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot and describe how the variables are related.

C3B6C799046A4C97A34476CA22B7E2FA.description: Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts.

D4DB1E5147484D13BA1F79AAA10AAFBD.description: Evaluate and compare strategies on the basis of expected values.

1629E1C7A5544F02BCE01E82C1D154E2.description: Weight the possible outcomes of a decision by assigning probabilities to payoff values and finding expected values (e.g., find the expected payoff for a game of chance).

32E03C63A3FC4BB19E3B9B14B05813ED.description: Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which probabilities are assigned empirically to find the expected value.

9C4BD0BFF37B456F8D68A1297355BEBB.description: Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which theoretical probabilities can be calculated to find the expected value.

4B5CEF8D744A421C9FE119D34C12E0EE.description: Calculate the expected value of a random variable; interpret it as the mean of the probability distribution.

976E7B62D4244A9EAF9AE702C81B190D.description: Define a random variable for a quantity of interest by assigning a numerical value to each event in a sample space; graph the corresponding probability distribution using the same graphical displays as for data distributions.

429C09E26AB746A3AC8B1D4B8F67D6D0.description: Calculate expected values and use them to solve problems.

FF809C1E2BC64FCB98146E6814AA6725.description: Use permutations and combinations to compute probabilities of compound events and solve problems.

289608733A81426AA3D2266535FFC66E.description: Apply the general Multiplication Rule in a uniform probability model, P(A and B) = P(A)P(B|A) = P(B)P(A|B) and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

75763844AAFF42CC9B20D06A0282DA2E.description: Apply the Addition Rule, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) – P(A and B) and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

858AD2921B6D459DBFBA36361F6D1879.description: Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B's outcomes that also belong to A and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

CC00C32087A34674BFCE4D20782F1BD5.description: Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in everyday language and everyday situations. For example, compare the chance of having lung cancer if you are a smoker with the chance of being a smoker if you have lung cancer.

111FDB278C834DE09F567B62257087A4.description: Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data when two categories are associated with each object being classified. Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities. For example, collect data from a random sample of students in your school on their favorite subject among math, science, and English. Estimate the probability that a randomly selected student from your school will favor science given that the student is in tenth grade. Do the same for other subjects and compare the results.

9EC7898F3FFC42658DE24FD715FAC038.description: Recognize the conditional probability of A given B as P(A and B)/P(B), and interpret independence of A and B as saying that the conditional probability of A given B is the same as the probability of A, and the conditional probability of B given A is the same as the probability of B.

482C814967734A46A2CAE5069A975C24.description: Understand that two events A and B are independent if the probability of A and B occurring together is the product of their probabilities and use this characterization to determine if they are independent.

D213AE1C9813479D88D352375B55F53E.description: Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events ("or," "and," "not").

B55A70CBB7AE4CBE98E486310DDDA3DC.description: Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data.

1270102D19954EEF8111FAB0EBFA476F.description: Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data.

4F9970D89C2D41918E44B0345CEAF69E.description: Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data when two categories are associated with each object being classified. Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities.

8EF61F5FDFC44CFCBA0D6DFBCF6AE9F4.description: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distributions to compare center and spread of two or more different data sets. Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).

A9492B2D83AF4E81BDFAB117F5B82BFC.description: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dots plots, histograms, and box plots).

AD7D46E53D464507AA5A584849341F28.description: Evaluate reports based on data. Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.

7FB9271A3EA54DD9ACCF7F34E87294B1.description: Use data from a randomized experiment to compare two treatments; use simulations to decide if differences between parameters are significant.

8CF80EF5DABE4681B3FDCC24577ACE5B.description: Use data from a sample survey to estimate a population mean or proportion; develop a margin of error through the use of simulation models for random sampling.

A4BDA8573A0F452BB852E510CAD4BF8C.description: Recognize the purposes of and differences among sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies; explain how randomization relates to each.

FDB45ECA594D4744ADE9928D7535E00C.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on single count or measurement variable.

952CDB1A1FF7442AB7C89CE96AFCF72A.description: Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts.

423D2695A1B545EF97C739027A16BDEA.description: Use probabilities to make fair decisions.

38BDE3D2A5234A9AAEE590CE8A17AD1B.description: Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions.

4BFCA3B31D21446FB9046B3B035F72C5.description: Use permutations and combinations to compute probabilities of compound events and solve problems.

CEEA473E57794803BDBF0C752AC089FE.description: Apply the general Multiplication Rule in a uniform probability model, P(A and B) = P(A)P(B|A) = P(B)P(A|B) and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

9F6F280D777544AA85219E7800CBCCBF.description: Apply the Addition Rule, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) – P(A and B) and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

27A4E5F0FCC64DD194F289EF52BDB76C.description: Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B's outcomes that also belong to A and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

EE6504E8E68E4E0AB3D7040507979344.description: Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model.

900D5F9BC0054D96AAAB8089A7B80177.description: Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in everyday language and everyday situations.
