Theorems include: measures of interior angles of a triangle sum to 180°; base angles of isosceles triangles are congruent; the segment joining midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half the length; the medians of a triangle meet at a point; points on a perpendicular bisector of a line segment are exactly those equidistant from the segment's endpoints.

14C71F65613B4CD88E38408B93045C85.description: Use congruence criteria for triangles to solve problems and to prove relationships in geometric figures.

069959A2B179421C970B023B8879AB8D.description: Explain how the criteria for triangle congruence (ASA, SAS, and SSS) follow from the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions.

88BC5B86FA104C029F9C8F7E0461E06B.description: Use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to show that two triangles are congruent if and only if corresponding pairs of sides and corresponding pairs of angles are congruent.

AB25BBD6FC11447888985D5866BCE660.description: Use geometric descriptions of rigid motions to transform figures and to predict the effect of a given rigid motion on a given figure; given two figures, use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to decide if they are congruent.

BB95364A7CDB47D18DC3762A2B60A524.description: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions.

C6DDA637E7BE4170A9A868218CAE9F56.description: Given a geometric figure and a rotation, reflection, or translation, draw the transformed figure using, for example, graph paper, tracing paper, or geometry software. Describe a sequence of transformations that will carry a given figure onto another.

30B301FA079B48BC889516ABC27F3728.description: Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, and translations in terms of angles, circles, perpendicular lines, parallel lines, and line segments.

8A7AABEE08374426A85F76D872BC1814.description: Given a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular polygon, describe the rotations and reflections that carry it onto itself.

DB51F2ABF9F04994935BA016F0ED0E49.description: compare transformations that preserve distance and angle to those that do not.

1A5B69FC3EEE477694365271DF1BA651.description: describe transformations as functions that take points in the plane as inputs and give other points as outputs.

EB44345A35A240029756975CD52712FB.description: represent transformations using geometric concepts in the plane.

0AB3C7988BD5403298D50D4BAB1DB589.description: Build on prior knowledge from rigid motions to:

599EB987A4CA43248C633FE451D19535.description: Experiment with transformations in the plane.

65CC53F1794F4E1E84D78B48DED46267.description: constructing a line parallel to a given line through a point not on the line.

60C011EA13EC49B5AF6A25B01AC4A350.description: constructing perpendicular lines, including the perpendicular bisector of a line segment; and

0026920761654309BBF4443C4FB4D34D.description: Make formal geometric constructions with a variety of tools and methods, such as a compass and straightedge, string, reflective devices, paper folding, dynamic geometric software, etc.:

1C96F2D32DE34A9886951D11A007E9DA.description: Find the point on a directed line segment between two given points that partitions the segment in a given ratio.

7F18D17872C44A46801A8902A2FB3AC1.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

CAB9CC918AE248438D820B8BB30192EE.description: Use appropriate methods of proof to prove theorems about lines and angles. Theorems include: vertical angles are congruent; when a transversal crosses parallel lines, alternate interior angles are congruent and corresponding angles are congruent.

3FF5FDDE066E43FC90D80B23B85ED233.description: Use Venn diagrams to represent set relationships.

EC98EAC289524C95952FC1BC504C5935.description: Translate a short, verbal argument into symbolic form.

BB05155D572743CCB0F17BDA98C3561E.description: Identify the converse, inverse, and contrapositive of a conditional statement.

5A3A778C6F294C19B01D56B7AC1F0EBF.description: Construct and justify the validity of a logical argument.

C599367266CB46F88353C58F5A44E8DF.description: Identify and utilize inductive and deductive reasoning.

6578E899E655403792AC1D3EEB0D1497.description: Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line segment, based on the undefined notions of point, line, distance along a line, and distance around a circular arc.

22A0827883C44FC1B747E9EA5F6178D3.description: Experiment with transformations in the plane.

31C5F2E60BA74A099655AAA6AD2FF8E0.description: Interpret the rate of change and the constant term of a linear model in the context of the data. Use technology to compute and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.

0B337C7E72D74A91B3AAC87327D71004.description: Fit a linear function for scatter plots that suggest a linear association.

296A00A0ED9E474B8D150678D6794E1A.description: Informally assess the fit of a function by plotting and analyzing residuals. Focus should be on situations for which linear models are appropriate.

96AE92F03CA341E1AD7A643851EB0F61.description: Fit a function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data. Use given functions or choose a function suggested by the context. Emphasize linear and exponential models.

480136E41ED7432485E5A0875DD7C256.description: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot and describe how the variables are related.

C626C1612C4C4E1A8542C73A72622E63.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables.

A91A4487B3AC424F8D541F6287D6656C.description: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).

58E56C1E359D4491835A5807D23C588B.description: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation only as a tool to describe spread and not to explicitly find standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.

2D99D5978A124382A4CE65512683878C.description: Select applicable representations to display data on the real number line (e.g., dot plots, histograms, and box plots).

94B44F85C7D8409D9BE348791AE3868C.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.

FEA088C87FE740FFBB94F40462E84888.description: Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and rectangles.

B41A24E0BC6041F3A9220D951AFE7EEC.description: Prove the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines and use the slope criteria to solve geometric problems (e.g., find the equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line that passes through a given point).

65CDF9C8DE164971812AA8EC553B071B.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

8874BAA58DE64C639244015AA791E869.description: Observe using graphs and tables that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing linearly or quadratically. Extend the comparison of linear and exponential growth to quadratic growth.

B1F1A5232C974A4A9F805D4D6FC97AFF.description: Recognize situations in which a quantity grows or decays by a constant percent rate per unit interval relative to another.

FFB4C36AE7C5490C9B6097D0E509FA9A.description: Recognize situations in which one quantity changes at a constant rate per unit interval relative to another.

F7E6FE69C94D42D5972A4E06D79F5F0E.description: Prove that linear functions grow by equal differences over equal intervals; exponential functions grow by equal factors over equal intervals.

9F47B650C8784287B1CA03A6E5FC9464.description: Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions, with exponential functions, and with quadratic functions.

067B453A1814496AA323F7475690D340.description: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems.

75F93A09862945D8A92D8D665FF9753A.description: Identify the effect on the graphs of linear and exponential functions, f(x), with f(x) + k, and the graphs of quadratic functions, g(x), with g(x) + k, k g(x), g(kx), and g(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology.

51E7CB8CDD324925B5DF899E9CA16A1C.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

389625AA5BF846349941F1388ACA63BB.description: Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences to model situations, given a graph, a description of a relationship or given input-output pairs (include reading these from a table).

EE5CC21E0E754D0CA632CE8E70B05835.description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations.

AE7F0A5F1A1640708268364C9C9CC9F6.description: Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context.

D3C32E58F3254889BF8998C74F2991EF.description: Write linear, exponential, and quadratic functions that describe a relationship between two quantities.

C026471D15984427B5E8332B77394514.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

0878B54B2A434E5595903CAD66C06C81.description: Use the properties of exponents to interpret expressions in exponential functions.

9C87C8CAFD294C9AA307D9CF37662BA1.description: Use the process of factoring and completing the square for a=1 only in a quadratic function to show zeros, extreme values, symmetry of the graph, the relationship between coefficients and roots represented in factored form and interpret these in terms of a context.

DEC57EBABBE0471CB78E2E1C0CAC7D0C.description: Write a function defined by a linear, exponential, or quadratic expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.

4D062AB7E7754247BCF005E18E26F6C1.description: Compare properties of two linear, exponential, or quadratic functions each represented in a different way, such as algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or from verbal descriptions.

467AF8EA1D2448178DEBB10E902BA204.description: For quadratic functions, focus on intercepts, maxima, minima, end behavior, and the relationship between coefficients and roots to represent in factored form.

0EB381089EC24DBF8BF38E23CE796144.description: For exponential functions, focus on intercepts and end behavior.

038FE5A749754AECB51FADED0000CFF7.description: For linear functions, focus on intercepts.

51F8ABE9BA9C4D4790FD3188287AF9C1.description: Graph linear, exponential, and quadratic functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph.

1133C26FEA2F4A28984E31E118253F8E.description: Key features of quadratic graphs include: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximum or minimum; symmetry; and end behavior.

75768DEB0F71403AAB60128BD97AF888.description: Key features of linear and exponential graphs include: intercepts; and intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative.

ECB7C493EA884FA6A9843C1B58FD36B3.description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship. Relate the domain of a function to its linear, exponential, and quadratic graphs and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes.

8A84AD9BE3B847F7AD474B08CEC62116.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of a context.

2259100592CF46CDA3FECB96F74FD71D.description: Recognize arithmetic and geometric sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset of the integers (e.g., the Fibonacci sequence is defined recursively by f(0) = f(1) = 1, f(n+1) = f(n)+ f(n-1) for n ≥ 1).

6F4AD329B82545638BB232214B64DB99.description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

70195B84A1B94A5DB559D6515E038FB4.description: Use multiple representations of linear and exponential functions to recognize that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. Develop function notation utilizing the definition of a function to represent situations both algebraically and graphically.

4CD6F07E3514480390C1D106895FF2C5.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation.

9C3A6303B245488AB8B6F7C16E0ABA45.description: Graph the solutions of a linear inequality in two variables as a half‐plane and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half‐planes.

57C1A111E2FC460DA8BF04D12D643F4C.description: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the linear and/or exponential equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately (e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values or find successive approximations).

0A1F7ECFF81C41C294E7844BDD1AFCD5.description: Recognize that the graph of a linear or exponential equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane.

DA7A5DE85AD348EBBBBAC8ECFE341085.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.

CF80ADE61EE24180BA998DD3F7A69C57.description: Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two variables graphically.

C8C9A67182794EBA99ED66A61E078A29.description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables. Include examples of solution sets with no solutions, an infinite number of solutions, and one solution.

04F7DA6FCA2E40339BB123577201488C.description: Understand and demonstrate ways to manipulate a system of two equations in two variables while preserving its solution set.

6258A8649F4A4DC28DCEE4D83662956A.description: Solve real-word and mathematical problems leading to two linear equations in two variables (e.g., given coordinates for two pairs of points, determine whether the line through the first pair of points intersects the line through the second pair).

895007576F33412297CAED54E5D94E43.description: Solve simple cases by inspection (e.g., 3x + 2y = 5 and 3x + 2y = 6 have no solution because 3x + 2y cannot simultaneously be 5 and 6).

D111AE1155E540A689CF49D83C17A24D.description: Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables correspond to points of intersection of their graphs, because points of intersection satisfy both equations simultaneously.

3A411C00CA934BE498C2417B8613B47A.description: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

55A0276B91624F9CAD4A708DD39FD5D9.description: Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x – p)² = q. Derive the quadratic formula from this method of completing the square.

68060C0C768344E8B999FFA8483D9AE1.description: Recognize the concept of complex solutions when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions.

2936F435FE624E0B9A434FA89316313C.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable by inspection (e.g., for x² = 49), taking square roots, factoring, completing the square when a=1 only, and the quadratic formula, as appropriate for the initial form of the equation.

873DA386A42646988064BA302EFB6322.description: Solve linear equations including equations with coefficients represented by letters, simple exponential equations that rely on application of the laws of exponents, and compound linear inequalities in one variable.

22749A41D67140AD91FCFB017EBB89B5.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

45246A197626444D89420EA59CBA9455.description: Represent constraints by linear equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or non-viable options in a modeling context.

A4866FC136B548BBB2F763E64B73E6D7.description: Create equations in two or more variables, representing linear and exponential relationships between quantities. In the case of exponential equations, limit to situations with integer inputs.

F2D30A9962834F7B9616D226A43A5EBB.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable, representing linear and exponential relationships, and use them to solve problems. In the case of exponential equations, limit to situations with integer inputs.

00804C34E4BD44558AF6DD576A4B2654.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

AECDE6D3FF814ED5A2AED0C60FA14D18.description: Recognize that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials. Focus on linear or quadratic terms.

B5BA49AA40C8405CAA22D69472DDB834.description: Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions in exponential functions. For example, the expression 1.15<sup>t</sup> can be rewritten as (1.15<sup>1/12</sup>)<sup>12t</sup> ≈ 1.012<sup>12t</sup> to reveal the approximate equivalent monthly interest rate if the annual rate is 15%.

BF3DF267D69C447293297EBEEF5FC4DD.description: Complete the square in a quadratic expression, when a=1 only, to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function it defines.

863EB1CDD67746B0908DE782F5C4752E.description: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.

D55B7E505F56471B88E22C2F681F929E.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of linear, exponential, and quadratic expressions to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression through connections to a graphical representation of the function.

04CCB534792943799D7BFA3EB7FCB9FC.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems.

D9AE93D13E7A47FB8754EFA517E6158F.description: Rewrite expressions involving radicals, including simplifying, and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.

BD55069661E54227843EBCD99685E328.description: Explain the connections between expressions with rational exponents and expressions with radicals using properties of exponents. Extend from application of properties of exponents for expressions with integer exponents.

C138CD2285C74FC4A074E2B571305458.description: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents.

DEAE32CA8CC640488D196DBD675A77C9.description: Use the structure of quadratic and exponential expressions to identify ways to rewrite them.

6B78D2580CA941CEB07A375EBFBEBE9C.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear function or exponential function of the form f(x) = a*b<sup>x</sup> in terms of a context.

FFED3558ECCF445D8E4C1E78F0335C19.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.

A5FAF226CE0645098F9A07FD03F6DEC4.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

6F84B4EBCCB94885B03F30D8632377C2.description: Interpret linear, exponential, and quadratic expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

8671454E66644B13835C2A5A32E079DB.description: Interpret the structure of expressions and equations in terms of the context they model.

D0B7B51E369948588B3B356EBFC6008D.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

D9D6B45A13084D74A0DD8F985F092F04.description: Look for and make use of structure.

D97095ED81D34D0B9C2FCFADD9CF2DD1.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

9562358BA36B4F8BB4DE103087B7D6EF.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Social Studies

13E673F07002414EB3DC790677B84DFD.description: Explain the causes and effects of political, social and economic transformation in Europe in the nineteenth century, including the significance of nationalism, the impact of industrialization on different countries and the effects of democratization.

B21694E556B742A68A3A7F7D9F8AA7D5.description: Assess the impact of colonization on both the mother countries and their colonies.

7A164FF6E6094063BFB1023B63A29DA1.description: Compare the political actions of European, Asian and African nations in the era of imperial expansion.

8EB7744DD89746C0BB4E87C79D076344.description: Illustrate the significant political, commercial and cultural changes that took place in China.

964CEDE8983646308F9969957AC7C02D.description: Analyze the causes and effects of political revolutions and determine their impact on the formation of governments and on the citizens of a society (e.g., French, Italian, German, Latin America, etc.).

ED3C83087712408CA013C896CC103DD4.description: Describe the Agricultural and Industrial Revolutions and determine their impact on the evolution of society.

6F4A8E4A83CB4F48A253779BAD140C4D.description: Explain the long-term effects of political changes because of the emergence of strong monarchial governments.

3400D2E428C14B7789A9BF9360914720.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the global political environment of the sixteenth through the nineteenth centuries.

537ADF2DF204457FA084DA6DBCB34F21.description: Explain the ways that Enlightenment ideas spread through Europe and their effect on society (e.g., John Locke, Voltaire, Jean-Jacques Rousseau and Baron de Montesquieu.)

4C6DBD959F004812A2EE2B9B814E3E1A.description: Explain how European needs/wants for foreign products contributed to the Age of Exploration.

7017DAF90D894A2EB854331A89D23531.description: Summarize the origins and contributions of the scientific revolution.

2AF088719A22483D8B3B6B26853A3189.description: Analyze the religious reformations and their effects on theology, politics and economics.

55F470C084DB4D90B71ACBE5A3D6805A.description: Compare the impacts of the Renaissance on life in Europe (e.g., Humanism, art, literature, music and architecture).

E5D928B44F354CEFBFB6D7470C05E63A.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the changes in society because of the Renaissance, Reformation, Age of Exploration and the Enlightenment.

8363103C225E49F08264D95F3195ED82.description: Examine and assess the effects of warfare on society during the Middle Ages.

5470468FAADC40928479546317667F42.description: Summarize the economic, geographic and social influences of African and trans-Saharan trade, including education and the growth of cities.

8C730B4B4CF7411CA8A598A1A3F5A699.description: Analyze the social, political and economic upheaval and recovery that occurred in Europe during the Middle Ages, including the plague and the subsequent population decline, the predominance of religion and the impact of the crusades.

FDF5384EF16D4CB1B3E33042796833DA.description: Identify and evaluate the individual, political, religious and economic roles in medieval society.

9F88A19A27084B1FBD54153721682E22.description: Outline the origins of religion in the Middle East and the changing role of women in that region through to the modern (or contemporary) period.

C394797699B845CABDBDC8EA906BAC3E.description: Summarize the functions of feudalism and manorialism in Europe, China and Japan (including the creation of nation-states) as feudal institutions helped monarchies centralize power.

3D247F39BE2E4DEF8483D64FC5FAD943.description: Investigate and explain the influence of the Byzantine Empire, including the role the Empire played in preserving Hellenistic (Greek) learning.

D977D336D8EA49AD889B70F8FFA3B2F2.description: Demonstrate an understanding of Middle Age societies and the influence of those societies on the history of the world in areas of social, political and economic change.

2896A89684D94A8E85EDC9059195A9FD.description: Analyze the impact of religion on classical civilizations, including the rise and growth of Christianity and Hinduism, and the effects of their beliefs and practices on daily life, changes that occurred as a result of Buddhist teachings, and the influence of a variety of religions on culture and politics.

7367E4F9BFA04EEB963BA65C2032013F.description: Compare and contrast the causes and effects of the rise and decline of classical civilizations.

6CAACDAE7273426F964A5E93A8187FEB.description: Demonstrate an understanding of classical civilizations and the influence of those civilizations across time and space.

543ED8C0AA514CDBB2974D365D2C0059.description: Investigate and detail the various components of culture and civilization including customs, norms, values, traditions, political systems, economic systems, religious beliefs and philosophies in ancient river civilizations.

190F9F52E25C48EF9C1D1D37317B9BDB.description: Compare and contrast the causes and effects of the rise and decline of ancient river valley civilizations.

421BC7B6C42047818606940D70455E9C.description: Demonstrate an understanding of ancient river civilizations and the ways in which early civilizations evolve.

23BDD69BBBDC43178F3E8ACB5A06EE49.description: Detail and predict the causes and effects of the Agricultural Revolution.

DB5F5F5B47A0442D818CF6B66965AD09.description: Analyze the interaction of early humans with their environment and evaluate their decisions (e.g., hunting, migration, shelter, food and clothing.)

0DC804E15E1E4F88894BBBF90A644C6C.description: Demonstrate an understanding of prehistory, the concept of change over time and the emergence of civilization.

567E0311F888426F9556CDD07E482001.description: Use maps, charts and graphs to depict the geographic implications of world events.

58DF1A7E7ED5428A991CCFE188CD2644.description: Explain how the uneven distribution of resources in the world can lead to conflict, competition or cooperation among nations, regions, and cultural groups.

3D8BDD214EA3481799256E08B49AF850.description: Explain how migration of people and movement of goods and ideas can enrich cultures, but also create tensions.

5E6FBA8EB7A340CEAA866CD144C1BF1C.description: Apply geography skills to help investigate issues and justify possible resolutions involving people, places and environments.

5FA9DF8DC6284362B34B36F69BA3BB73.description: Explain how altering the environment has brought prosperity to some places and created environmental dilemmas for others.

EA07EC1C1CB144758347D944944ABFA1.description: Use different types of maps, terminology, and geographic tools to analyze features on Earth to investigate and solve geographic questions.

2FB2885F79294CC88B46823A0512DF7A.description: Define scarcity, demonstrate the role of opportunity costs in decision making, and examine economic reasons for the rise and fall of civilizations (e.g., Roman Empire, the Crusades and Imperialism).

F63FAE4EB67445D3A6FF1A63112F93F5.description: Analyze the importance of family, labor specialization and regional commerce in the development of global trade systems.

F0EEAE949BAA4315A2A8F65A1A3B2372.description: Identify types of exchange systems (e.g., barter, money) and the role forms of currency play in acquiring goods and services.

35893DF0F7414CEF8F5E2B722657A583.description: Examine and illustrate the trade patterns (e.g., resource allocation, mercantilism and other economic systems) of regions of the world across time and explain their significance to the evolution of global economics.

E92D2A58E54C4EAB86FBB625F2620003.description: Research and categorize multiple current and historical world aid organizations and assess the importance of global volunteerism as a 21st century citizen (e.g., Amnesty International, Doctors Without Borders, Human Rights Campaign, International Red Cross, Invisible Children, Peace Corps, etc.).

2C35F3DB051448D28C9CC41B7FD2A1A3.description: Compare and contrast political ideologies in order to analyze the evolving role of government in world affairs prior to the year 1900 (e.g., democracies, republics, dictatorships, various types of monarchies, oligarchies, theocracies and parliamentary systems).

20E7A6B71F434B49967C1B6DDB21289B.description: Analyze and evaluate various ways of organizing systems of government in order to illustrate the continuity and change in the role of government over time (e.g., Hammurabi's Code, the Twelve Tables of Rome, Justinian Code, Magna Carta, English Bill of Rights, Articles of Confederation and the U.S. Constitution).

B02EC451B1994A4D9E5EECA6751134AD.description: Analyze and connect the status, roles and responsibilities of free men, women, children, slaves and foreigners across time in various civilizations.

ECEB8D0C28244903BD75372E3D50C19A.description: Describe the roles of citizens and their responsibilities (e.g., prehistoric societies, river civilizations, classical civilizations, feudal systems, developing nation states and neo-feudal systems).

document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Social Studies

4804003E1AFC4FC1AC3C168556E0ADEC.description: Analyze and explain how political, social and economic factors influenced American involvement in World War I (e.g., treaties, alliances and nationalism).

3CAC262CC9DF42719DC04993968BDEA6.description: Investigate the impact of technological advances and innovation in the early twentieth century both in the United States and the world (e.g., telephone, automobiles, flight, transportation, weapons and medical advances).

CC19B6E7045C4A7FA7EE495CC9DD140D.description: Investigate and explain the impact of the Spanish-American War on the United States as a world power, including locations of expansion and the changing image of the United States by the global community.

21EFD1082ADF45708AD22FA9B01DF97E.description: Analyze the development of American expansionism, including the shift from isolationism to intervention and the economic and political reasons for imperialism.

98E70A65D5394F49BF2A88CC548B4754.description: Evaluate the impact of United States foreign policy on global affairs (e.g., Open Door Policy and presidential programs of Taft, Roosevelt, and Wilson, such as Big Stick Diplomacy, Dollar Diplomacy and Moral Diplomacy).

7AA9591AD195457D876AAAC356AAB45D.description: Use units to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems; choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays (e.g., use units appropriately as a way to understand multi-step problems in relationship to understanding credit card fees and finance charges; compute distance, rate and time to solve problems to analyze driving and safety data, using single and multiple unit conversion; use and compare researched reaction times and vehicle velocity, as well as accepted equations to solve problems with braking distances).

7398306B60F348B2A0B0D602135F6BD5.description: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).

8DF362836CD3431A85BE3FA23A816C06.description: Summarize categorical data in various forms (e.g., two-way frequency tables, circle graphs, segmented bar charts). Interpret relative frequencies in the context of the data in making financial decisions.

6FA6783F2E3A4706B9B07C079B2F71E7.description: Create a data display modeling financial situations.

A8734EE1C4B84FBEB791937D081C1882.description: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related. Fit regression lines to scatterplots and make predictions based on lines of best fit. Find and interpret correlation coefficients of regression equations in financial situations (e.g., use scatter plots to show correlation between two funds, two stocks, a stock and the general market, or in business situations to forecast sales or to compare revenue to the number of units sold).

0E1503B78BC54A148CC284BBBB54C84D.description: Select applicable representations to display data on the real number line (e.g., dot plots, histograms, and box plots).

5CF79923B4944EE0808AA73EBD85E350.description: Apply exponential formulas to solve for future and present value of investments by hand or with graphing technology (e.g., PV=FV*(1/(1+r)<sup>n</sup>) and A(t) = Pe<sup>rt</sup>).

FF06F007290B4E7E984079E40C14FEBE.description: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula, use them to model financial situations, and translate between the two forms (e.g., create recursive and explicit models of sequences related to retirement planning, amortization schedules for a loan, comparing subsidized and unsubsidized loans, reasoning and making decisions about the length of the loan and a fixed versus adjustable rate mortgage).

7852BD85770D427FAACA542406D93D55.description: Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions that model financial situations, including step functions and absolute value functions (e.g., develop and communicate the appropriateness of representing a commission salary using a linear versus a piecewise function; analyze graphs of functions that model profit).

684742F0C5AB4C5494347617DAD6EE43.description: Identify the effect on functions that model financial situations of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology (e.g., identify the impact of a change in a constraint in a function that models retirement planning, business income and expenses, or employment benefits).

AC6775BB795842BDACFCD0086CC5ADE3.description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities in a financial context (e.g., calculate the costs associated with purchasing a vehicle, including leasing, purchasing with cash, or with a loan).

EA7A6A0CFD074627A81494E6DF5627BA.description: Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima (e.g., in the model of a profit function, determine the break-even points, the maximum possible loss, and the maximum profit).

2A29BB14DCDE41A6BC6225770C7A524B.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way, such as algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions (e.g., utilize linear and exponential functions to compare simple with compound interest; calculate and compare using both the loan payment formula and payment schedules in table format, the monthly cost of purchasing an automobile, and discuss the feasibility of that payment in relation to monthly budget; compare two functions showing interest accrued when paying the minimum monthly payment over time compared to paying a larger monthly payment; identify and compare the average rate of change between given time periods).

BACF9D725DEB4174A049DD1BAD6E90FC.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph (e.g., graph the linear, quadratic, or exponential curve that models the demand versus supply functions and find the equilibrium point with and without technology).

DE69CF6A9F2440C3BCC372A5A8BBED79.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function modeling a financial context (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph (e.g., examine depreciation trends).

33E0BB91A15B464C8DBB785EE75F598A.description: Fit a function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data. Use given functions or choose a function suggested by the context. Emphasize linear, quadratic, and exponential models. Data may address, but is not limited to automobile financing, investing in the stock market, business, employment, banking, consumer credit, taxes, and retirement planning.

96804E18F167418AA653E26BBF1A688C.description: Construct linear and exponential functions modeling financial contexts, including arithmetic and geometric sequences to model situations, given a graph, a description of a relationship, or given input-output pairs including reading these from a table (e.g., utilize linear and exponential functions to compare simple with compound interest).

A7BCDB6F2AA64EEEA31DDE7281D224D2.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function in terms of a context (e.g., investigate and compare, using technology and regression, historical data to determine if automobile depreciation follows a linear or exponential model).

07A32FBEBB2D4D07B142C1260592F59A.description: Select a function that models a relationship between two quantities in financial contexts, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship (e.g., write, graph, and interpret the revenue (quadratic) function in comparison to the expense (linear) function using key features of the functions; reason quantitatively to compare subsidized and unsubsidized loans, as well as other forms of financial aid available to college students; calculate mortgage payments, reasoning and making decisions about the length of the loan and a fixed versus adjustable rate mortgage).

0FBD8DD16AB244FFB8DBB898EC99DB36.description: Prove that linear functions grow by equal differences over equal intervals, and that exponential functions grow by equal factors over equal intervals. Use this relationship in analyzing financial situations (e.g., compare the linear function modeling simple interest with the exponential function modeling compound interest).

74A8B9E8C21942DB9885C5432FE488BE.description: Use function notation in financial applications, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a financial context (e.g., in making decisions regarding retirement income, apply the formula A(t) = Pe<sup>rt</sup> to determine future value).

D9F4D7C4A27D4CC19E420218DB037F71.description: Use functions to model financial situations. Use multiple representations of functions to recognize that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. Develop function notation utilizing the definition of a function to represent situations both algebraically and graphically (e.g., develop and communicate the appropriateness of representing a commission salary using a linear versus a piecewise function; use linear and polynomial functions to evaluate and communicate quantities as required by Internal Revenue Service and Social Security Administration regulations and to determine when and why the models may be discontinuous).

23F3EB470924415799C74455DE375F0B.description: Construct, graph, use, and interpret functions.

D18BE708814C4379A3AAD35969E7FDE2.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable in a financial context that may include, but are not limited to, business modeling or employment decisions (e.g., given a quadratic equation that models a profit function, determine the break-even points; apply braking distance/stopping distance formulas to solve problems related to driving and safety data).

B3025FC62A734CC8876CA307F712B3C9.description: Recognize that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract and multiply polynomials (e.g., combine the polynomials that model income and expense to create a profit model).

10084D1FD24E467F9A73F909BA2D9553.description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (with graphs) in making financial decisions, focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables (e.g., create and solve a system of equations based on the expenses incurred and monthly payment when choosing home ownership versus rental).

50A35FBC68E647ECA501D556995C22D6.description: Rearrange formulas for financial applications to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations. Know difference between growth and decay functions (e.g., solve the literal equation for exponential depreciation to find a depreciation rate and the literal equation for continuous interest to find the interest rate; apply the formula for average daily balance, (average daily balance*APR*days in billing cycle)/365, using literal equations with varying APRs and billing cycles).

61CEFB8F5D15487AB8207BA947BFB26F.description: Represent constraints in financial applications by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context (e.g., create a system of equations based on the expenses incurred and monthly payment when choosing home ownership versus rental; find the percentage of total salary that a benefits package represents; calculate taxes owed based on a given income and tax table and determine total percentage of income paid to taxes; calculate the gross pay and net pay using the FICA percentage (7.65%), retirement contribution, and worker's compensation insurance (employer match)).

499BAB841F7B42B0A78FA3D7702959FB.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities in a financial context; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales. Financial contexts may include, but are not limited to, stock markets, automobile ownership, business modeling employment, banking, consumer debt, and independent living decisions regarding taxes or planning for retirement (e.g., create a linear expense equation based on fixed and variable expenses and graph choosing an appropriate scale and origin for the graph).

E0B7B8322870454CA97708C714909F30.description: Create and solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems in financial applications that may include, but are not limited to, stock markets, automobile ownership, business modeling, or employment (e.g., calculate wages by hourly rates or pay periods to make decisions about pay in a real-world context).

E82C9441C9AA41979E084ACD29AE93A4.description: Interpret parts of an expression or equation, such as terms, factors, and coefficients, in a variety of financial models including those found in stock markets, automobile financing, and in banking contexts.

5920FC4AA589489B8FBC187C71173DE3.description: Communicate with and about mathematics in writing and orally, both independently and collaboratively, by preparing financial plans (e.g., plan for an emergency savings fund that will last three to six months in the case of loss of income; determine the total percentage of income paid to taxes or the percentage of total salary that a benefits package represents).

09DA496EBFAA4BD59B3D987CE39AE97D.description: Communicate with and about mathematics in a financial context.

B68EEC0AFF6142A689ABFC297D85CCCA.description: Demonstrate reasoning skills in developing, explaining, and justifying sound mathematical decision making (e.g., demonstrate reasoning skills in creating and presenting a budget of monthly expenses based on a career pathway income, and analyze the soundness of the mathematical reasoning of others; determine outlook for a chosen career pathway and use the average salary to determine if the desired cost of living can be met).

C7D7C46AAAEB4DF08C3D0C261510DD2B.description: Mathematical Language in a Financial Context

document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Mathematics

5594E03247CD4964B6BCF8B31DDE1C27.description: Identify a real-world situation that involves quantities that change over time; pose a question; make a hypothesis as to the answer; develop, justify, and implement a method to collect, organize, and analyze related data; extend the nature of collected, discrete data to that of a continuous function that describes the known data set; generalize the results to make a conclusion; compare the hypothesis and the conclusion; present the project numerically, analytically, graphically, and verbally using the predictive and analytic tools of calculus.

FA1C94EED00F491CBE92661242DBA03B.description: Apply the key concepts and applications of limits, continuity, derivatives, and integration to analyze functions that represent a collection of data.

53F38D3EB4854FA78C786C98D206AA04.description: Use integration to solve problems that involve linear displacement, total distance, position, velocity, acceleration, and area between curves by looking at both functions of x and functions of y; utilize units to interpret the physical nature of the calculus process.

294A862557B7480FB9FDCE058CF539F3.description: Calculate a definite integral using Riemann sums by evaluating an infinite limit of a sum using summation notation and rules for summation.

EE6804F6E49649F68BA07A5A17696850.description: Justify why differentiability implies continuity and classify functional cases when continuity does not imply differentiability.

60C9F707B0F8417B9B9009FB14D3CDD6.description: Apply the key concepts, connections and applications of limits, continuity, derivatives, and integration for a wide variety of regions.

4807F66C20194E9DA8D75F413ABE7AA2.description: Approximate areas under a curve using Riemann sums by applying and comparing left, right, and midpoint methods for a finite number of subintervals.

F641260688D34BAC900AF1F3756D7F7B.description: Investigate and explain the relationships among the graphs of a function, its derivative and its second derivative; construct the graph of a function using the first and second derivatives including extrema, points of inflection, and asymptotic behavior.

230B106B4B3C4666A89DF6234CB0DD11.description: Develop tangent lines as best linear approximations to functions near specific points; explain this conceptually; construct these tangent lines; and apply this concept to Newton's Method.

3B156EE1ACE044AF9C0985BE793FA7BB.description: Compare and contrast the limit definition (not delta epsilon) of continuity and the graphical interpretation of the continuity of a function at a point; recognize different types of discontinuities.

EB0C25E51C4A44B1A9CDE2934BFBABAD.description: Use limits to deduce asymptotic behavior of the graph of a function.

0E53CE7E755E472CB5C405CDA143987F.description: Apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus to evaluate definite integrals and to formulate a cumulative area function and interpret the function as it relates to the integrand.

FCB12367D49A455D98F89DFC61F15840.description: Characterize the definite integral as the total change of a function over an interval and use this to solve real-world problems.

355200A876754BDA8BE98E434DEB39CC.description: Evaluate definite integrals using basic integration properties such as addition, subtraction, constant multipliers, the power rule, substitution, and change of limits.

C9A11942A29B4BD6926810899F86E90E.description: Determine antiderivatives that follow from derivatives of basic functions and apply substitution of variables.

6A8174BC6DCB40A4B32C7DF7310995C7.description: Construct and use mathematical models to solve optimization, related-rates, velocity, and acceleration problems.

6B476B30F1CB4566860906A3D9DA8AE8.description: Apply Rolle's Theorem and the Mean Value Theorem to real-world problems.

0DA1648D54BB46B0894C70F89AA72822.description: Quickly recall and apply rules of differentiation including the constant multiple rule, the sum rule, the difference rule, the product rule, the quotient rule, the power rule, and the chain rule as applied to algebraic, trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic, and inverse trigonometric functions using techniques of both explicit and implicit differentiation.

046A48CC02B14509A12A9A1190C92510.description: Recognize when the Extreme Value Theorem indicates that function extrema exist.

FB715757DF7843B68F2894169DF99F19.description: Discriminate between the average rate of change and the instantaneous rate of change using real-world problems.

6B837241A9B440E69A68E3CF7D343BA8.description: Investigate and apply the definition of the derivative graphically, numerically, and analytically at a point; conceptually interpret the derivative as an instantaneous rate of change and the slope of the tangent line.

0C0D3D9DCC7648C888DD56C3BD104501.description: Apply the definition of continuity to determine where a function is continuous or discontinuous including continuity at a point, continuity over an interval, application of the Intermediate Value Theorem, and graphical interpretation of continuity and discontinuity.

873F7528DFE14B7F9C2A502DF6C58F6B.description: Use the properties of limits including addition, product, quotient, composition, and squeeze/sandwich theorem to calculate the various forms of limits: one-sided limits, limits at infinity, infinite limits, limits that do not exist, and special limits such as and

7B47B19B3860417CA7BBFFD15E69AEDB.description: Demonstrate a conceptual understanding of the definition of a limit via the analysis of continuous and discontinuous functions represented using multiple representations (e.g., graphs and tables).

3EEA0DF1DE7E459D8E6F8CAB21FC6D8E.description: Use abstract notation to apply properties of algebraic, trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic, and composite functions, as well as their inverses, represented graphically, numerically, analytically, and verbally; and demonstrate an understanding of the connections among these representations.

AEB2408C8B3D4BCAB24D85B2BA410106.description: Understand the key concepts, connections and applications of functions, limits, continuity, derivatives, and integrals represented in multiple ways.

document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Mathematics

51B2B58160494AD895A4FC01CFD7B644.description: Use matrices to represent geometric transformations and solve applied problems.

C8F6B51FAC734D579131AA6B868275FF.description: Use vectors to represent and solve applied problems.

41C91AF3D4224DE486A51A476A13DE8E.description: Solve geometric problems involving inaccessible distances.

3BBF67B5BAC64AD7A6EA64FB3E99CF36.description: Create and use two- and three-dimensional representations of authentic situations using paper techniques or dynamic geometric environments for computer-aided design and other applications.

56FDA7AB6B434ECDB7BDAB7ADB69F6FE.description: Analyze various voting and selection processes to determine an appropriate method for a given situation (e.g., preferential vs. non-preferential methods, and/or weighted voting).

D1D9A3733BC847658FECB04E264CA383.description: Apply and analyze various ranking algorithms to determine an appropriate method for a given situation (e.g., fair division, apportionment, and/or search engine results).

3B5DBB20A72C434ABFDFAF8B01AA27A5.description: Make decisions using ranking and voting.

B1BE9B76B74449779CC6B720DA62B98B.description: Construct, analyze, and interpret flow charts in order to develop and describe problem solving procedures.

B54B05A5A6B3446DAAB9F459565FAC11.description: Solve problems involving scheduling or routing situations that can be represented by a vertex-edge graph; find critical paths, Euler paths, Hamiltonian paths, and minimal spanning trees (e.g., Konigsberg bridge problem, mail vs. Fed Ex delivery routes, Kolam drawings of India, traveling salesman problem, and/or map coloring).

11D872402FD541779A03AD50A5901267.description: Collect numerical bivariate data; use the data to create a scatter plot; determine whether or not a relationship exists; if so, select a function to model the data, justify the selection and use the model to make predictions.

846D3A5CB72E4D629A4094AE30E6997B.description: Solve problems using recursion or iteration (e.g., fractals, compound interest, population growth or decline, and/or radioactive decay).

246017A749474C2BA54981E51FDA0003.description: Determine or analyze an appropriate piecewise model for problem situations (e.g., postal rates, phase change graphs, sales tax, and/or utility usage rates).

4B26C0BB4600422A892E4CCD7E6EC633.description: Determine or analyze an appropriate cyclical model for problem situations that can be modeled with trigonometric functions (e.g., predator-prey models, tide heights, diurnal cycle, and/or music).

CEEF92FD9C2C4E55BCC5B8B282242B1B.description: Determine or analyze an appropriate model for problem situations - including linear, quadratic, power, exponential, logarithmic and logistic functions (e.g., stopping distance, period of a pendulum, population growth, Richter Scale, and/or Fujita Tornado Scale).

A91E750921A8416AAE5DCD2B8E36A929.description: Model data and change with functions.

4E2FFB3ABE98472E9D2EC7137FE10CF4.description: Use arrays to efficiently manage large collections of data and add, subtract, and multiply matrices to solve applied problems.

591FA13BE2B44C1386F88533DC7EB5A6.description: Solve problems involving large quantities that are not easily measured.

15EDA64F3C4F47B0B109646AB7CFC6B1.description: Communicate statistical results in both oral and written formats using appropriate statistical and nontechnical language.

1B82CFB67F8D46A08E175B18DC3B2100.description: Report results of statistical studies to a particular audience, including selecting an appropriate presentation format, creating graphical data displays, and interpreting results in terms of the question studied.

1FB91666106243E6A5EF2658A062C02A.description: Determine possible sources of variability of data, both those that can be controlled and those that cannot be controlled.

104ECB6328114E05B2B1EB186FC5166E.description: Create data displays for given data sets to investigate, compare, and estimate center, shape, spread, and unusual features.

FF7316A4DF414C5CB52A26C679DD5317.description: Determine possible sources of statistical bias in a study and how such bias may affect the ability to generalize the results.

5D9A8D37F53B4B0AA4581B1DABFB1D97.description: Identify the variables to be used in a study.

785116A4D51A446AB83BE2E0078CBFCC.description: Identify the population of interest, select an appropriate sampling technique, and collect data.

D80C9A652BEB4FD1965E400D9AFE7395.description: Describe strengths and weaknesses of sampling techniques, data and graphical displays and interpretations of summary statistics, and other results appearing in a study, including reports published in the media.

44F6F9864D5443CE8C8A9BF2D2CF5479.description: Identify uses and misuses of statistical analyses in studies reporting statistics or using statistics to justify particular conclusions, including assertions of cause and effect versus correlation.

32C0FFE3C91A438ABE7A8AC1B118D5EA.description: Interpret and compare the results of polls, given a margin of error.

AC96824BF5374B728846FBEB051E0BE7.description: Identify limitations or lack of information in studies reporting statistical information, especially when studies are reported in condensed form.

A8C5E94B2EA64D60A4314C9C0A2EDE89.description: Calculate expected value to analyze mathematical fairness, payoff and risk.

21D699C6506242D89CB247D8F1E2BDC9.description: Use probabilities to make and justify decisions about risks in everyday life.

E2193D923EA140B88F7D0F36BE5F27BE.description: Determine and interpret conditional probabilities and probabilities of compound events by constructing and analyzing representations, including tree diagrams, Venn diagrams, two-way frequency tables and area models, to make decisions in problem situations.

FCE1066265234523BF6564A5E6416A9E.description: Use the Fundamental Counting Principle, permutations, and combinations to determine all possible outcomes for an event; determine probability and odds of a simple event; explain the significance of the Law of Large Numbers.

7A352B02B83447FD84D3945D85CE437C.description: Analyze information using probability and counting.

7185C96ABA4A477787190131702F97BE.description: Research and analyze taxes including payroll, sales, personal property, real estate, and income tax returns.

3D23F06E6F4B42948BE04CE0B1102D14.description: Research and analyze personal budgets based on given parameters (e.g., fixed and discretionary expenses, insurance, gross vs. net pay, types of income, wage, salary, commission, career choice, geographic region, retirement and/or investment planning).

A852F1D8DD3140A0A6080A2C6B653AB7.description: Determine, represent, and analyze mathematical models for inflation and the Consumer Price Index using concepts of rate of change and percentage growth.

73A0770065524CAA8651466ABD83CDED.description: Determine, represent, and analyze mathematical models for investments involving simple and compound interest with and without additional deposits (e.g., savings accounts, bonds, and/or certificates of deposit).

3FCD9488A38D42A9B704EC645A90B910.description: Determine, represent, and analyze mathematical models for loan amortization and the effects of different payments and/or finance terms (e.g., business loans, auto, mortgage, and/or credit card).

24F2644706B649038121FC7E11352129.description: Gather data, conduct investigations, and apply mathematical concepts and models to solve problems in mathematics and other disciplines.

09857EC6E54F4D56A48699A121A1D0C9.description: Communicate with and about mathematics orally and in writing as part of independent and collaborative work, including making accurate and clear presentations of solutions to problems.

AB2E5DCBDF794153A7445270066164C3.description: Demonstrate reasoning skills in developing, explaining, and justifying sound mathematical arguments and analyze the soundness of mathematical arguments of others.

document.title: West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Mathematics

2B8CB30C7B1343F299CAC838A39A19A0.description: Understand statistics as a process for making inferences about population parameters based on a random sample from that population.

FE733E29597F4E0CA44810259DB952A0.description: Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments.

C0FC41B4705B47F9AE7A706644FB6CF0.description: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).

C6A51F3BC9BB444FAADB63A6C42F1542.description: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation only as a tool to describe spread and not to explicitly find standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.

44D296104CEE483E99F1108E74CAA3C1.description: Select applicable representations to display data on the real number line (e.g., dot plots, histograms, and box plots).

110790AB65C14261AB398672C89FD284.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.

9C69B664130242CB8D41CF4E2E8D0DC8.description: Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data.

66973DA4ABD745F49EAD9D7E44EC243F.description: Know that straight lines are widely used to model relationships between two quantitative variables. For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line, and informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

C0EE698835834C90B06749735D0913C5.description: Interpret the rate of change and the constant term of a linear model in the context of the data. Use technology to compute and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.

AD5B9BA6782544CF8E764F047A09AAA0.description: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot and describe how the variables are related. Interpret linear models.

12B04621199F4D078FB423DF552093EF.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables.

D71038A53C6349418897A7907FDEA2BB.description: Statistics and Probability - Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data

E9A5D3198A4A4904B5DE86C645E3E7B0.description: Apply geometric methods to solve design problems (e.g., designing an object or structure to satisfy physical constraints or minimize cost; working with topographic grid systems based on ratios).

149F78A8934F4A179B9D0884D2A34582.description: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations.

83D0B2F6A1294D478F5BE156A6EB64EB.description: Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and rectangles.

FBDB31D1BA3549F7B208C5E963C7E608.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically. For example, prove or disprove that a figure defined by four given points in the coordinate plane is a rectangle; prove or disprove that the point (1, √3) lies on the circle centered at the origin and containing the point (0, 2).

03FFAF1E65074642B9ECF0CBFC445674.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

46C597B9217B4AFDB56B2D6C771B4361.description: Geometry – Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations

85C8A16CBD5B4AE787B6A3BC3E04D982.description: Give an informal argument using Cavalieri's principle for the formulas for the volume of a sphere and other solid figures.

4C3DCBB3B5F5443E81E9BAE5057936FA.description: Give an informal argument for the formulas for the circumference of a circle, area of a circle, volume of a cylinder, pyramid, and cone. Use dissection arguments, Cavalieri's principle, and informal limit arguments.

26D962D5AE9E47D5BCA0A5385AAD1F36.description: Explain volume formulas and use them to solve problems.

5D2141C0DDB6429BB0E2D269214100E3.description: Compose functions. For example, if T(y) is the temperature in the atmosphere as a function of height, and h(t) is the height of a weather balloon as a function of time, then T(h(t)) is the temperature at the location of the weather balloon as a function of time.

5A594FE4E2DA446B8691F79F588940B1.description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations. For example, build a function that models the temperature of a cooling body by adding a constant function to a decaying exponential, and relate these functions to the model.

C8E94457756F42A5A7C9B01169A345F6.description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.

A6802D486AE84B8194CAD9E58F1FA5FF.description: Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences to model situations, given a graph, a description of a relationship, or given input-output pairs (include reading these from a table).

6311A0A6EF5A4C48B8417973306C8186.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

89B63C1CE1B94CCAA4A8457A7642F111.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way, such as algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions.

3F9B6838FDD342879AB78744AAFFC2FE.description: For polynomial functions, focus on identifying zeros and showing end behavior.

5E4303EB4877479EBE2273DCAD670766.description: Select a model function based on behavior of data and context to calculate and interpret the average rate of change of linear, exponential, quadratic, and model functions based on behavior of data and context (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. 0FB95CF741824C0D922947A6391703E6.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems.

901A96B7DA764911AA9D9DC240BDFB89.description: Use the structure of expressions including polynomial and rational expressions to identify ways to rewrite them.

2E24AEC67EAE4C16940262BA1F29FAF5.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.

ED06DA33B86B48629E753245A7AC7E0D.description: Interpret expressions including rational and polynomial expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

8DF7B7BE4C474F0CA9E9B9911FC22F61.description: Know there is a complex number i such that i² = −1, and every complex number has the form a + bi with a and b representing real numbers.

29463AE432AC40D597CE136415133217.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.
